items.statement: Board approved sale of IndoStar Home Finance to EQT for INR1,750 crores on fully diluted basis
items.quote: On 19th September 2024, the Board of IndoStar Capital Finance Limited approved the sale of its subsidiary, IndoStar Home Finance Private Limited to EQT, which is a global private equity investor for INR1,750 crores on a fully diluted basis.

items.statement: EQT plans to invest INR500 crores into IHFPL upon or shortly after closing
items.quote: Further, EQT plans to invest INR500 crores into IHFPL upon or shortly after closing this the transaction and the Board of IHFPL has granted an intrinsical approval for this infusion.

items.statement: Deal expected to close by Q4 FY24 or early FY25, later clarified as FY25 or early FY26
items.quote: The deal closure time line will depend on the timing of the receipt of the required approvals, especially the approval of RBI. And currently, we expect this deal to close by Q4 FY '24 or early FY '25.

items.statement: Transaction subject to RBI approval, lender consent, and shareholder approval
items.quote: The transaction is subject to customary conditions resident, RBI approval, consent from lenders and shareholders.

items.statement: Sale improves book value per share by about INR70
items.quote: The premium receipt from the sale significantly improves the book value of the share by about INR70 per share.

items.statement: Transaction expected to be ROA and ROE accretive over next two to three years
items.quote: Yes. So I think Sweta, our analysis is that this is accretive to our ROA and ROE outlook for the next two, three years because of following levers.

items.statement: Cash inflow expected to reduce weighted average cost of capital and borrowing needs
items.quote: One is, there is -- there would be at least an expectation of reduction in the weighted average cost of capital because for the simple reason that we'll borrow less given the cash in the balance sheet and that itself obviously does improve the ROA.

items.statement: Cost of funds already coming down quarter-on-quarter; fund inflow will reduce cost further
items.quote: On the cost of funds, we believe that we are already in the phase where the cost of funds have been coming down quart er-on-quarter. And in fact, Vivek, in the last call also, we did mention about it. So that's a continuous process. When the fund actually comes in, this will definitely help us reduce the cost further

items.statement: Net cash inflow to parent expected at INR1,400 crores plus after tax
items.quote: Yes. I mean if you exclude, but really the net inflow is really the correct way to look at it, which is really INR1,400 crores plus is what is expected.

items.statement: Gain on transaction estimated at INR1,300 crores plus
items.quote: Gain would be at INR1,300 plus.

items.statement: No plan to use proceeds for acquisitions of other companies or entities
items.quote: There's no such plan.

items.statement: Funds to provide impetus for investment in vehicle finance and small business loans
items.quote: This will give us an impetus to invest more into the vehicle business and the small business loans which we have just started off. We'll continue to that journey.

items.statement: Growth dependent on market conditions; will decide based on market reaction
items.quote: Our growth will be dependent on market conditions, how the market is reacting on the overall side, based on which we will decide.

items.statement: Decision on use of proceeds for provisions or growth to be taken closer to closing
items.quote: We told was that we will take a call closer to the closing time. Right now we have not decided how to use it.

items.statement: Proposed merger of SeQuent Scientific and Viyash Life Sciences at swap ratio of 56 SeQuent shares for every 100 Viyash shares
items.quote: Upon the scheme becoming effective, all shareholders of Vi yash will be issued shares of SeQuent in the ratio of 56 shares of SeQuent for every 100 shares of Viyash

items.statement: Merger expected to be accretive to revenue growth and margin in first year and deleverage balance sheet
items.quote: The merger will be accretive to SeQuent in revenue growth and margin in the very first year itself and de-leverage the balance sheet.

items.statement: Transaction at 44% discount to SeQuent's current trading multiples
items.quote: The transaction would be at a valuation that is at a significant discount, in fact 44% discount to the current trad ing multiples of SeQuent

items.statement: Combined entity targeting INR 4,000 crore revenue and 20% EBITDA margin by FY27-28
items.quote: We should be expecting that by 27-28, we would be in the 20%-odd range for EBITDA margins and of course INR4,000 crores plus in the area of top line.

items.statement: Post-merger EBITDA expected 150-200 bps higher than standalone guidance of high teens by FY27-28
items.quote: What we expect is that after the merger and we really make everything execute it well, it could definitely be 150 to 200 basis points higher than what we have guided at any point of time.

items.statement: Viyash EBITDA margin improved from 12-13% to 17-21% with API segment outperforming industry
items.quote: That's how yo u can see ‘25 or ‘24, from 12 %, 13% to it ’s reached to 21%, 17%. And we are pretty confident it's going to grow

items.statement: Short-term cost synergies estimated at 100-250 bps EBITDA improvement from procurement and manufacturing integration
items.quote: But once we do that, definitely, it's going to be good synergies, that's where SeQuent can benefit at least 100 base points to 250 base points kind of thing.

items.statement: Viyash capacity utilization at 70%, no major capex needed for next two years
items.quote: Viyash's current capacity utilization is close to 70%. And we don't see any additional capex requirement for the near future.

items.statement: Combined entity expected to become debt-free soon, reducing finance costs substantially
items.quote: We are going to be a debt-free company soon unless we go and invest today. Looking at our EBITDA, it can be debt-free very soon. So, our financial cost is going to reduce substantially.

items.statement: Viyash amortization of INR 90-95 crore per annum continuing for FY25 and FY26, partial in FY27
items.quote: FY25 and FY26 will continue at around that 90-95 crores is the amortization per annum. FY27 will have part of the period.

items.statement: Viyash operates 9 USFDA-approved facilities, SeQuent to leverage for backward integration
items.quote: Finally, we ended up having nine high quality USFDA approved facilities. All if you see, every facility is USFDA approved.

items.statement: Viyash shifting from intermediate to API and formulation, API revenue doubled in two years
items.quote: Last two years, API business has grown almost double, whereas intermediate business we optimized.

items.statement: Viyash R&D team of 200 resources filing 10-12 products annually with high-end analytical capabilities
items.quote: R&D, you know, you must have seen that 200 resources in R&D with high-end analytical capabilities is able to do 10-12 products in a year.

items.statement: Merger subject to approvals from shareholders, Stock Exchanges, NCLT, CCI and other regulatory bodies
items.quote: The proposed merger is subject to receipt of customary, statutory, and regulatory approvals, including from shareholders, Stock Exchanges, NCLT competition commission, etcetera.

items.statement: Key execution risk is regulatory approval timelines for product integration and synergy realization
items.quote: That requires external approvals since we're handling an entire regulatory business. Whatever we anticipate, the timeframe that could be the risk.

items.statement: Management continuity confirmed with structural adjustments only as needed over 15-month integration
items.quote: I think clearly the theme of going ahead is continuity. I think all the management is going to continue fully committed into this role.

items.statement: Biosecurity Act could create major opportunity for combined entity as US seeks alternatives to China supply
items.quote: if it goes through, I see t hat's one of the good opportunities for SeQuent . There's large companies that are looking, the alternative majority is coming from

items.statement: Combined entity already at annualized INR 400+ crore EBITDA run rate in first quarter
items.quote: Given that in the very first quarter, both the companies together are already at an annualized INR400 crores plus run rate on EBITDA.

items.statement: Iskraemeco has back-to-back orders for 3.5 million meters from PGCIL Gujarat and significant orders from West Bengal (20 million total plan, 2 crore awarded across 4 AMISPs).
items.quote: So those ord ers have been already placed on Iskraemeco, which back to back has been placed on us. S o that’s for three and a half million meters for in the case of Gujarat, which is PGCIL is the AMISP there, and in case of West Bengal

items.statement: Total smart meter opportunity: 11 crore (110 million) awarded, another 11 crore yet to be awarded.
items.quote: As you know, already 11 crores meters have been awarded and ano ther 11 crores meters yet to be awarded

items.statement: FY25 guidance retained at INR 3,000 crore revenue and 15% EBITDA margin; acquisition will not change guidance.
items.quote: Sir, we will retain our whatever guidance we have given, INR3,000 crores on top line and 15% on EBITDA.

items.statement: Iskraemeco acquisition is margin accretive and will achieve 15% EBITDA post integration; not margin dilutive.
items.quote: Yes, so this year post integration, we will have no effect on our guidance. It certainly will achieve the 15%. And so obviously, this product is not in any way margin dilutive. It is actually margin accretive.

items.statement: Hyderabad factory ramping up with 4 million meters per annum capacity; sufficient space to expand further.
items.quote: In Hyderabad, specifically, the capacity that is being built up is about 4 million per annum. And we will work on increasing this once the entire system picks up speed. We have enough, let's say, bandwidth and space.

items.statement: Government smart meter rollout pace accelerating; management expects faster awarding of balance 11 crore meters.
items.quote: So I think they will do it fast only because I think government is committed towards this particular project. So earlier they have taken 4 years, 5 years time to come to this level, but it will be much faster than that.

items.statement: Smart meters currently ~10% of sales; expected to rise to 12-15% next year as production ramps.
items.quote: Currently, it’s about 10%. And going forward, currently, yeah, can be about -- sorry. As of this year, we’ll probably have around 10% of this. And going forward in next year, it would depend on what orders we get from other sectors. Yeah, about 10%, 12% prob ably, maybe at the peak, when we have a lot of execution load, it’ll be about 15% of our total

items.statement: Net working capital cycle for smart meter business will not exceed 90 days; acquisition will not increase working capital.
items.quote: Yeah, it will be within the consolidated guidance that we have giv en. So, this is not going to increase the working capital cycle in any way

items.statement: Payment terms across AMISPs ensure working capital exposure not more than 90 days, likely less.
items.quote: Yes, so the current payment terms, all the three stages of installation, the working capital exposure will not be more than 90 days. It will significantly be less than 90 days and it's not going to change because the same terms all the AMISPs do.

items.statement: EMS revenue per single-phase smart meter ~INR 3,000; three-phase meters cost 70-80% more.
items.quote: Sir, we get only EMS revenues which is the meter total cost of the device only. So that is anywhere around INR3,000 plus rupees. That is the kind of revenues that companies like us will make who make only devices.

items.statement: Three-phase smart meters cost 70-80% more than single-phase meters.
items.quote: See, three phased meters are much bigger meters because they deal with three phased supply of electricity. So typically, their cost will be 70%-80% more than the single phased meters.

items.quote: Approximately about 50% is with AMISPs who don’t have a device especially of their own, like IntelliSmart, EDF, Apraava, Monte Carlo, GMR. I think this is in the publi c domain. You can also find that out. So our objective is to get some share of these

items.statement: Acquired Iskraemeco India to secure orders, gain technology (gas, water, grid meters), and achieve manufacturing scale; no royalty to global parent.
items.quote: So by acquiring this company, we get access to whatever orders that Iskraemeco would have got, that is first. So it increases our scale. Second thing is they have a lot of other techn ologies, especially in the other metering area. So we get access to those areas too

items.quote: No royalty is to be paid to anybody, any entity outside of India. Since we acquired this part of the acquisition deal, that Iskraemeco brand name can be used for a specified period to service all these orders in India for as long as we wish.

items.statement: Exploring export opportunities for power distribution products; initial RFQs accepted, contracts being finalized; pilot orders exist.
items.quote: We do have clients outside of India too, wh ich the business is developing, and we are in the stages of the initial RFQ being accepted and contracts being drawn up, etc. So we’ll advise about the business from those companies as soon a s we get some firm orders on hand. There are some small pilot orders available

items.quote: Yes, we are fully integrated here. We have our own molding shop. I think those of you who were able to come to the Hyderabad facility would have seen it also. We have got full backup, end-to-end manufacturing of smart meters, full value chain.

items.quote: So fully as smart meters only. So this year it will go up because there ’s 3.5 million orders are getting executed. So this year, it will become an intercompany sal e. So it will come as part of our consolidated revenue

items.quote: There are 125 people there. It's a large organization.

And now once they are in the fold, so our target will be all the AMISPs. And we’ll work with the AMISPs in specific deals, okay? So there will be no conflict of interest

items.statement: Export market conflicts with Iskraemeco global to be resolved amicably; white-label supply acceptable with partner communication.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of around 25% for FY25
items.quote: And in terms of revenue growth, guidance would be around 25%.

items.quote: It will be between 3.5% to 4% before exceptional loss.

items.quote: So ROE in FY '24 we had 11%. And going forward we will intend to be in between 11% to 13%

items.quote: I think there is a huge shift coming from unorganized to the organized market. We are seeing a lot of traction coming from that particular space.

items.quote: So in terms of number of APs, we are in the region of around 9,000 to 10,000. And this business is also growing as equal to our digital business. So share of AP business is around 22% to 23% of our revenue.

items.statement: AMC license in final stages; approval expected any day from regulator.
items.quote: So again, in terms of the license, I can say we are in the final stages of getting the AMC license. And it could be any day, any time now that we hear it from the regulator. And that's what we maintain now also.

items.statement: True-to-label impact neutralized via cash delivery brokerage and collateral interest charges; F&O regulatory impact estimated at 13-14% of broking income per client.
items.quote: So we have increased our kind of like -- or maybe we have started charging for cash delivery transactions. We have put -- like we are charging interest on collateral that we receive for -- so that way, by putting all these additional kind of charges on cash segment and charging for collateral that we receive as a margin, we would be able to negate this impact of true-to-label.

items.statement: UPI block mechanism (ASBA in secondary market) mandatory for QSBs from January 2025; impact uncertain but expected to be minimal given client ticket sizes.
items.quote: This ASBA in secondary market or UPI block, as you mentioned, this is mandatory offering for QSBs from January onwards. Let's wait and see how the client behaviour pans out. We don't see that there is going to be any significant impact on this because of the ticket size of our clients.

items.statement: Digital players have pricing elasticity; customers not sensitive to ₹5-10 per order increases; superior platform experience drives retention over price.
items.quote: See this platform -- time and again, we have seen, it is not sensitive to price to the tune of ₹ 5, ₹ 10 per order. There are lots of competition who came out with ₹ 10 per order and all that. They were unable to gain market share. What is important is that experience of a customer on this platform, if they see value on being on this platform and if we feel that, okay, we need to increase price, t

items.statement: Revenue guidance of INR 2,150-2,200 crores by FY27 with EBITDA margin of 14-14.5%
items.quote: By end of FY27, we are expecting revenue to be in the range of INR 2,150 crores to INR 2,200 crores. And our EBITDA margin will be in the range of 14% to 14.5%.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth target of 18-20%
items.quote: Next financial year, we intend to have a growth of 18%-20%.

items.statement: Capacity utilization target of 70% by FY27
items.quote: By FY27 we expect the capacity utilization will be close to 70%.

items.statement: Ordered 1,500 kg/hour wafer line for Q1 FY26 installation
items.quote: For wafers we have already ordered 1,500 kg per hour machines line which is expected to get installed sometime in Q1 of next year.

items.statement: Total production capacity at 410,154 metric tons with 35-40% utilization
items.quote: From a manufacturing standpoint, our total production capacity now stands at 4,10,154 metric tons, which provides us ample room for growth. Our current capacity utilization is at 35% to 40%.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin at 11.6% down from 12.7% YoY due to A&P and employee costs
items.quote: EBITDA margin remained at 11.6%, down from 12.7% last year. While there has been an inflationary pressure because of increase in raw material prices for Chana and palm oil and a couple of other raw materials, but we have negated that by a couple of our initiatives.

items.statement: Gross margin steady at 29% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Our GP margins remain steady at 29%, showing a slight improvement compared to the same quarter last year is consistent with the previous quarter.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin expected around 12% if raw material prices stable
items.quote: So, my estimate is that it will be bit higher than Q2 maybe in the range of 12% provided the raw material prices etc remains in the current range. We will get to a 12% margin in Q3.

items.statement: FY25 A&P spend target at 1.5% of revenue (INR 18-20 crores)
items.quote: Overall, our estimate for FY25 is close to 1.5% of our revenue, which will be INR 18 crores to INR 20 crores this year.

items.statement: FY26 A&P spend target at 2% of revenue (INR 25 crores)
items.quote: And going forward, in FY26 also, we will have a higher, close to INR 25 crores of revenue, 2% of revenue being spent on advertising and marketing.

items.statement: Implemented grammage reduction in INR 5/10 packs and MRP revision in larger packs to offset palm oil duty hike
items.quote: To address this inflationary pressure and safeguarding our margin, we have implemented corrective measures in the month of September, which include reducing grammage in our INR 5 price point and INR 10 price point. And even in a couple of larger packs, we have revised the MRP as well.

items.statement: Palm oil import duty increased from 5% to 25% in September 2024
items.quote: 5% has gone to 25% in September.

items.statement: Raw material price easing expected in Q4 FY25 for chana and potato; palm oil dependent on duty revision
items.quote: Q4 is the quarter where again the crop of chana will come and looking at a favourable monsoon which we see last month. I think Q4 is a time where we will see the ease in the raw material prices specifically in chana and potato.

items.statement: Wafers grew 47% YoY in Q2 FY25 and 49% in H1 FY25; Gathiya grew 13% YoY in Q2 and 12% in H1
items.quote: The Gathiya segment grew by 13% Y-o-Y, while Wafers witnessed a substantial increase of 47% in Q2 FY25. Speaking of H1, Gathiya has shown growth of 12% and Wafers 49%.

items.statement: Snack pellets declined 5% in H1; corrective actions include 12-piece strips and new upmarket product launch
items.quote: We were selling in a strip size of 8 pieces in a strip unlike competition who was selling 12 pieces in a strip. So, we have already done a course correction whereas in 50% of our snack pellet items in first week of October we started selling in 12 pieces strips.

items.statement: Namkeen growth lower than Gathiya; larger packs (400g INR 100) and new contemporary products in development
items.quote: We are in process of developing larger scanty pouches like 400 grams INR 100 price point. As far as smaller packs are concerned, we are in process of improving our designs and pack sizes and introducing few new contemporary products as well.

items.statement: Targeting 1,000+ distributors by end FY25; adding ~1 distributor per working day in FY26
items.quote: By the end of this financial year, we'll have more than 1,000 distributors. And we will continue to add, you know, one distributor per working day in the next financial year as well.

items.statement: Alternate channel run rate INR 26 lakh/month; targeting INR 3+ crores/month by end FY25
items.quote: We expect all this business to be INR 3 crores plus per month by end of this financial year.

items.statement: Alternate channel profitability at par or higher than general trade for DC model (>80% of channel)
items.quote: Wherever we are giving stocks at DC level, our profitability is either at par with general trade or rather little higher than general trade. And contribution of DC model channels is more than 80% in these alternate trade channels.

items.statement: High raw material prices help gain share from unorganized players
items.quote: Typically in our industry, a brand like us or a company like us is okay with RM prices high, because it gives us opportunity to take market share from unorganized players.

items.statement: Actively evaluating M&A in Eastern, Southern, Northern India and UP for production/distribution synergy
items.quote: We are open for any kind of M&A deals wherever the company gets value out of the acquisition, be it synergy benefit from production, distribution etc. Even the Eastern part of the country if we get some opportunity, we have visited a couple of plants and we are in the process of doing due diligence.

items.statement: First interim dividend of INR 1 per share (100% face value) approved for FY24-25
items.quote: I am pleased to announce that the Board has approved the first interim dividend of INR 1 per share that is 100% on the face value of INR 1 for FY24-FY25.

items.statement: Inventory days increased to 64 in H1 FY25 from 30-42 in FY23 due to seasonal crop procurement
items.quote: Inventory in terms of number of working days has increased, which used to be 30, 42 days in FY23 has increased to 64 days in H1 of FY25.

items.statement: Trade payables at 2-3 days; creditors paid within 7 days
items.quote: It is close to 2 days to 3 days of our creditors. So we are healthy in terms of quick payment to our vendors.

items.statement: Operating cash flow INR 77 crores in H1 FY25; repaid INR 60 crores working capital
items.quote: Our operating cash flow stood at INR 77 crores for H1, which was utilized to repay working capital of INR 60 crores in the first half.

items.statement: Global agrochemical demand shows mixed recovery signals; volumes back but lower pricing impacts realizations; China production high, margins stressed; domestic monsoon 8% above normal but erratic spatial distribution caused floods and dry s
items.quote: We continue to witness mixed signals across agrochemical demand recovery in global markets. Volumes are largely back across key markets , though lower pricing continue to impact realizations.

items.statement: Kharif 2024 sowings reached 110 million hectare vs 108.8 million hectare last year; paddy up 2%, pulses 8%, maize 4%, cotton down 9%; extensive rains during key demand period lowered pesticide spray application and volume growth especially
items.quote: Kharif '24 sowings as of 20th September reached about 110 million hectare versus 108.8 million hectare last year. Area under paddy has gone up by 2%, pulses by 8%, maize by 4%, whereas area under cotton has declined by 9%.

items.statement: Export market demand recovery not promising; lower prices and volatility causing inventory buildup; China keeps market well supplied; US demand relatively better; Europe uncertain due to operating challenges and Middle East unrest
items.quote: Export market demand recovery is still not very promising. Lower prices and volatility are making chemical players also see an inventory buildup. China continues to keep the market well supplied.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 revenue Rs. 928 crore vs Rs. 832 crore in Q2 FY24; profit after tax Rs. 98 crore, 210% higher YoY; Crop Care volume-led revenue growth 7%; Seed revenue up 48% due to better Kharif liquidation; EBITDA Rs. 166 crore, up 24% YoY
items.quote: On the back of a strong double-digit volume growth in the domestic market, our revenue stood at Rs. 928 crore versus Rs. 832 crore of Q2'24 and profit after tax at Rs. 98 crore, which is 210% higher than the previous year, similar quarter.

items.statement: Metribuzin achieved highest ever volume in H1 FY25, surpassing full FY24 volume; Hexaconazole showing good momentum, working on debottlenecking; Pendimethalin steady long-term demand, capacity expansion with new efficient technologies to be
items.quote: In Metribuzin, we have done the highest ever volume in first half '25 and with half year volume surpas sing Fiscal Year '24 volume already. Hexac onazole is also showing good momentum, and we are working on debottlenecking to serve the increasing demand.

items.statement: Domestic Crop Care growth 11% with 17% volume growth; herbicide and crop nutrition grew 25% and 29% respectively; herbicide under-indexed in portfolio, consciously improving share; GeoGreen highest ever volume in H1; new launches Clasto (Co
items.quote: The quality of growth was also good, with future growth categories like herbicide and crop nutrition, witnessing 25% and 29% growth, respectively. Herbicide categories is under indexed within our business and we are consciously working on improving the share progressively.

items.statement: Seed business revenue Rs. 141 crore, 48% growth YoY due to lower Kharif sales returns from calibrated placement using Seedsay digital tool; Diggaz cotton hybrid crossed Rs. 50 crore brand with negligible returns; Aatish mature product on de
items.quote: Seed Business – It recorded Rs.141 crore revenue with 48% growth over the previous year, mainly due to lower Kharif '24 salesreturns resulting from calibrated placement leveraging Seedsay digital tool.

items.statement: Domestic crop care formulation business had minus 6% price degrowth in H1 FY25 with 18% volume growth; seed business growth driven by high single digit price/mix and flattish volume; cotton now largest crop in seed portfolio contributing to
items.quote: The domestic crop care first half you wanted, right? So, domestic crop care has had a minus 6% price degrowth, I am talking about formulation business and the volume growth is positive at 18%.

items.statement: Envisage CAPEX spends around Rs. 100 crore; plan to commence construction for integrated R&D Center in phased manner soon; measured approach in export segment - no new capacities until contracts in hand and improved utilization of existing
items.quote: We envisage spends on CAPEX would be around Rs.100 crore. We also expect to commence the construction for integrated R&D Center in a phased manner soon.

items.statement: Multi-purpose plant CAPEX ~Rs. 200 crore (part of Rs. 650 crore spent out of Rs. 800 crore planned over 5 years); formulation plant ~Rs. 100 crore working in line with expectations with significant headroom; debottlenecking existing capacit
items.quote: We have done about Rs.650 crore of CAPEX out of the Rs.800 crore of CAPEX that we spoke about in the last five years. And if I slice it, the big one had gone behind multi-purpose plant, which is around Rs.200 crore.

items.statement: Inventory levels moderated; collections improved despite stress in some markets; healthy cash and liquid balance of Rs. 229 crore as of 30th September; trade receivables increased from Rs. 773 crore to Rs. 852 crore (Rs. 80 crore increase)
items.quote: Our inventory levels have moderated. Collections have also improved. despite stress in some markets, collections improvement will continue to be a focus. We have a healthy cash and liquid balance of Rs.229 crore as of 30th September.

items.statement: Expanding customer base and securing registrations with more global players to improve share in technicals; CSM business: completed pilot scale production of pre-commercial quantities of Flavocide® for Bio-Gene Technology Limited (Australia
items.quote: On the back of three new contracts in Fiscal Year '2 4, we have further successfully completed pilot scale production of pre-commercial quantities of Flavocide®, a novel insecticide for Bio- Gene Technology Limited, an Australian company.

items.statement: Acephate market under pressure in US and Brazil with key input raw material at lowest ever price; competitors Adama and UPL significantly backward integrated with B2C presence in key markets putting Rallis at disadvantage; evaluating cost r
items.quote: our competitors here are actually Adama and UPL. Now, both of them are significantly backward integrated from a manufacturing perspective as well as they have a significant B2C market as well in these markets and that I think puts us at some disadvantage

items.statement: China continues to supply at very competitive prices, making pricing improvement difficult to predict; focus on domestic branded business to charge brand premium; diversifying supply chain domestically to balance reliance on China vs domest
items.quote: China has capacity and they have ability to supply at a very competitive price. So, I guess that's very difficult to predict. What is easy for me and I have been saying in the past is that I am going to focus on domestic branded business where I have to make sure my product is being used more by the same farmer and on the more crop acres.

items.statement: No specific numerical guidance given; attempt to grow better than market; not in position to give a number for current year growth; export business near-term outlook challenging; domestic business positive outlook on back of good reservoir
items.quote: Well, I think all I have been saying is that our attempt is going to be we grow better than the market. That's our attempt and that's what we are targeting. I am certainly not in a position to give a number.

items.statement: CSM strategy: selective approach, not chasing big deals; multiple conversations with various parties at different stages; getting encouraging response; three contracts in FY24 including Bio-Gene; difficult to put number on revenue share con
items.quote: We are not chasing everybody. I guess big deals I don't think are available at this point of time. We are relatively late entrant in this game. We are having multiple conversations with various parties and the different conversations are at very different stage.

items.statement: Higher effective tax rate in quarter due to unwinding of deferred tax assets from long-term capital gains tax reduction by Union Budget; one-time impact on carry forward losses and long-term capital gains
items.quote: Because of this long-term capital gains tax reduction by the union budget, there was an unwinding of the deferred tax assets created for both carry forward of losses and long-term capital gains. So, that's a one-time impact which has come for the effective tax rate.

items.statement: Portfolio rationalization exercise underway - tail portfolio rationalization where scale-up not met expectations or adding complexity; exercise to be completed in couple of months; not expected to have meaningful bottom line impact; streaml
items.quote: So, I think what we are looking at is tail portfolio rationalization, which is where either the scale up has not happened as per expectation or it's adding to the complexity. We are yet to complete the exercise, but I wouldn't say that it would have a meaningful impact on the bottom line

items.statement: Domestic institutional business sells technicals in bulk to parties but calibrated participation to avoid over-exposure; international business subdued except Metribuzin, Pendimethalin, fungicides; Acephate challenges acknowledged; confiden
items.quote: Now, obviously I have to find the optimal point of make versus buy. So, we keep making those decisions . Obviously, because of many confidential agreements we have with the parties, we are not able to disclose those names and all.

items.statement: Innovation Turnover Index (ITI) published annually tracking new product performance; H1 FY25 tracking in line with expectations; herbicide segment portfolio under-indexed but performed well, followed by fungicide then insecticide
items.quote: I think we published this ITI on an annual basis in Innovation Turnover Index which will reflect but safe to say that in the first half as well it's tracking in line with our expectations. Herbicide as a segment our portfolio is under index, but we have done well followed by fungicide and then insecticide.

items.statement: Rabi outlook positive with increased reservoir levels; IMD predicts Oct-Dec rainfall 112% of long-term average potentially affecting Kharif harvest; La Niña conditions may cause below normal temperatures in north/central India leading to co
items.quote: The IMD predicts October to December rainfall to be 112% of the long- term average, potentially affecting Kharif crop harvest. La Niña conditions, which may cause below normal temperature in northern and central India could lead to cold wave events.

items.statement: Seed business: first move to positive profitability zone (not a drag on company), then keep improving; large CAPEX investment only working capital, no fixed capital; actions showing momentum; cotton highest growth in both top and bottom lin
items.quote: More important is that the seed should not be a drag on the company profitability. So, we have to first move to a positive zone and then keep improving it from there.

items.statement: Multi-purpose plant utilization challenged by global situation; hope to improve as more contracts secured; formulation plant has significant headroom for expansion; Hexaconazole capacity maxed out, debottlenecked and exploring alternate exp
items.quote: Multi-purpose plant, Dr. Shukla alluded there are some challenges in getting higher capacity utilization because of the global situation as well. So, we hope to improve the utilization as we start seeing more contracts for it.

items.statement: Debt reduction target of Rs. 100 crores over FY25 and FY26
items.quote: as we had shared when we started the whole accelerated inventory charge -off that our intent is that in two financial years, which is FY '25 and FY '26, we will reduce the debt by about Rs. 100 crores.

items.statement: New initiatives spend target of Rs. 60 crores for FY25
items.quote: I think we had given at the beginning of the year at about Rs. 60 crores is the annual target.

items.statement: Inventory write-off of Rs. 50-60 crores expected in H2 FY25
items.quote: So, I would assume in the region of between Rs. 50 crores and Rs. 60 crores is what would be charged off as an additional inventory in H2.

items.statement: Traditional media revenue declined 33% YoY in Q2 due to higher base and deal delays
items.quote: Traditional media revenues for the first quarter stood at a round Rs. 95 crores, which declined by around 33% year -on-year

items.statement: Digital media revenue grew 17% YoY in Q2 driven by digital advertising growth
items.quote: Digital media revenues for the 2nd Quarter to rate around Rs. 67 crores, which increased by approximately 17% Y -o-Y

items.statement: Broadcast advertising demand remains sluggish due to consumption economy slowdown
items.quote: Additionally, there has also been sluggish demand for our broadcast advertising due to continued slowdown in the consumption economy.

items.statement: EBITDA loss of Rs. 27 crores in Q2 FY25, adjusted EBITDA loss of Rs. 12 crores excluding new initiatives
items.quote: EBITDA loss for the quarter was around Rs. 27 crores and net loss was reported at approximately Rs. 26 crores.

items.statement: Inventory charge-offs of Rs. 100+ crores over three quarters are accounting entries not affecting monetization potential
items.quote: Our inventory has come down from Rs. 727 crores as on 31st December, 2023, to Rs. 618 crores as of 30th September, 2024, which is about Rs. 100 crores, a little more than Rs. 100 crores in three quarters.

items.statement: Syndication deal closures delayed due to industry transitional changes, expected to materialize in coming quarters
items.quote: there were certain delays in deal closures in our traditional syndication business, which were largely a result of transitional changes in the media industry over the past few quarters. We expect these deals to materialize in the coming quarters.

items.statement: ShemarooMe released 8 new titles including Gujarati movies, web series and theatre plays in Q2
items.quote: In this quarter we released eight new titles which include movies, web series and theatre players, expanding our content portfolio.

items.statement: Launched two original shows Shamshan Champa and Main Dil Tum Dhadkan on Shemaroo Umang
items.quote: During the quarter, we successfully launched two original shows, Shamshan Champa and Main Dil Tum Dhadkan on our channel Shemaroo Umang.

items.statement: Shemaroo FilmiGaane YouTube channel reached 70 million subscribers, 24th most subscribed globally
items.quote: On YouTube, Shemaroo FilmiGaane has achieved a remarkable milestone, becoming the 24th most subscribed channel globally with approximately 70 m illion subscribers

items.statement: General entertainment channels achieved 7.6% viewership share in Hindi GEC genre
items.quote: Our general entertainment channels achieved a viewership share of approximately 7.6% in the overall Hindi GEC genre.

items.statement: New channel launch deferred due to unfavorable advertising demand conditions
items.quote: We have held back since we don't see that bettering of that, because obviously it is additional investment, we'll rather do it at the right time.

items.statement: Received GST show cause notice with demand of Rs. 70.25 crores plus interest and penalty
items.quote: we had received the show cause and we have intimated on the exchanges also, with the demand of Rs. 70.25 crores along with the interest and penalty thereon

items.statement: Debt reduction of Rs. 100 crores targeted over FY25-FY26, on track but H2 timing uncertain
items.quote: our intent is that in two financial years, which is FY '25 and FY '26, we will reduce the debt by about Rs. 100 crores. I believe we have good visibility for that and we are fairly on track.

items.statement: GST case with Rs. 70.25 crore demand plus interest and penalty, company has replied denying charges
items.quote: we had received the show cause and we have intimated on the exchanges also, with the demand of Rs. 70.25 crores along with the interest and penalty thereon, and Company has appropriately replied with repeating all the charges and claims.

items.statement: Movie genre channels and regional channels gaining viewership share at expense of GEC genre
items.quote: there has been a plethora of new movie channels that have come up. So movie genre has taken up a certain amount of viewership share from many genres, including from GEC

items.statement: MarathiBana channel remains free-to-air after exiting Free Dish due to unviable costs, viewership stable
items.quote: the channel continues to remain free to air, it's not a paid channel. What we have done is we have exited from free dish, which was a very high cost option, the price had gone up to an unviable level.

items.statement: Operational costs kept flat YoY while investing in intellectual property and content portfolio
items.quote: We continued to invest in intellectual property, further enhancing our content portfolio to drive long term growth. This has been done while keeping operational costs under check, and at the same level as the previous year.

items.statement: Full-year APE growth outlook revised to 18-20%
items.quote: I think 18% to 20% revision in our outlook on a full year basis is something we feel reasonably confident about.

items.statement: Full-year VNB growth guidance of 15-17%
items.quote: We will continue to deliver on a full year basis in that range. Maybe this could be a little bit lower or higher, but roughly in the 15% to 17% range in terms of VNB growth.

items.statement: H1 VNB margin 24.6%, down from 26.4% due to product mix and repricing deferral
items.quote: Our H1 value of new business was Rs. 1,656 crore, reflecting a 17.4% YoY growth and new business margins of 24.6%.

items.statement: Margin floor expected; H2 margins likely slightly higher than H1 but range-bound
items.quote: on a base case, H2 margins a re likely to be slightly higher than H1 margins given everything else being equal, but it really depends in terms of how some of these things evolve

items.statement: ULIP share to remain range-bound in 30s; non-par savings grew 76% YoY
items.quote: ULIP has seen some intended moderation in this quarter with the proportion reducing from 38% to 35% from Q1 to Q2. We have observed strong growth in non-par savings products, with the segment achieving a 76% YoY increase aided by new product variants launched this year.

items.statement: Retail protection APE grew 27% YoY and 36% 2-year CAGR; credit protect soft due to partner calibration
items.quote: Retail protection APE in H1 and on a two -year CAGR basis saw g rowth of 27% and 36% respectively. We expect the healthy momentum in retail protection to sustain for the rest of the year. The credit protect segment has been soft this year on account of calibration in disbursements across some of our partners and lines of businesses.

items.statement: Annuity growth slower due to aggressive peer pricing; calibrated strategy maintained
items.quote: Our annuity business experienced slower growth on the back of aggressive and unsustainable pricing by some peers. We continue to adopt a calibrated growth strategy, focusing on enhancing our product offerings whilst maintaining pricing discipline.

items.statement: Bancassurance grew 32% H1, 21% in Q2; proprietary channel grew 27%; agency term grew 2x company growth
items.quote: by 32% with deepening relationships across partner banks. Our counter share at HDFC Bank continued to be stable at around 65%. Proprietary channel grew by 27%, with the Agency channel gaining momentum in Q2 on the back of imp roved productivity, thus outperforming the company’s overall growth. Term business in agency grew at over 2x company g rowth

items.statement: Relaunched 40+ products covering 95% of business by Oct 1; 3-month transition for remaining products
items.quote: We have successfully relaunched more than 40 top products contrib uting to about 95% of the business as on October 1, 2024 and we plan t o relaunch other products during the course of the quarter. We are thankful to the regulator in allowing us an additional time of 3 months for transitioning to the new product regulation s.

items.statement: Commission renegotiation with 300+ partners and 2 lakh+ agents underway; expect completion in H2
items.quote: We have adopte d tailored solutions, including commission deferral, reduction or claw back depending on persistency track record and partner preferences. Whilst this transition might take some time, we expect to complete changeover across all our distributors in H2.

items.statement: IRDA intends IFRS rollout from April 2027; 24-30 month implementation window for large insurers
items.quote: As things stand today, we have received the communication from IRDA and we believe some peers have also received communication, which talks about IRDA's intent to roll it ou t from April 2027. So , there is a p hase-wise implementation plan, which we understand will be followed where all the large listed as well as unlisted insurance companies will go into Phase 1. And we basically have this windo

items.statement: Raised Rs 1,000 crore subordinated debt at 8.05%; solvency improved to 192% post raise
items.quote: As we had indicated, we raised subordinated debt of Rs 1,000 cr ore in the last week, thereby improving our solvency to 192% post the sub-debt raise.

items.statement: Embedded value Rs 52,114 crore; operating RoEV 16.0%; PAT up 15% to Rs 911 crore
items.quote: Our embedded value stood at Rs. 52,114 crore as on 30th September, with an operating return on embedded value of 16.0%. Profit after tax has grown by 15% year -on-year, reachin g Rs. 911 crore.

items.statement: 13th month persistency 88% (+120 bps); 61st month persistency 60% (+730 bps)
items.quote: We are pleased to share that persistency for the 13 th and 61 st months materially improved to 88% and 60%, respectively, marking increases of 120 basis points and 730 basis points versus the previous year.

items.statement: HDFC Pension AUM crossed Rs 1 lakh crore; market share 43.6% in H1
items.quote: We are delighted to announce that our subsidiary HDFC Pension crossed the Rs 1 lakh crore milestone in terms of assets under management and is one of the fastest growing pensi on fund management company in the industry, enjoying a market share of 43.6% in H1.

items.statement: Deferred repricing of non-par products due to IT bandwidth for regulatory compliance; 30-40 bps margin impact in H1
items.quote: We could have changed the IRRs on an existin g old product because interest rates have changed, but we chose not to do it because then I would have had to sacrifice a new product in lieu of the old product. So we just took a call that that had an impact for a few weeks, and that translated to 70-odd basis points impact.

items.statement: No repricing due to surrender regulations; normal interest rate repricing ongoing
items.quote: In fact, there was some repricing th at was required to be done, but we had delayed it because of compliance with the product regulations. So, there's no intention to have downwards repricing on account of the chang e in regulations.

items.statement: Peers repricing non-par savings and annuity products downward; gap expected to close by year-end
items.quote: We had some instances of repricing across non -par savings products as well as annuity products downward. And to be fair, it could be a combin ation of responding to the surrender guidelines as well as interest rate changes. So , I think hard for us to say, but we have observed definitely downward repricing on some of these segments.

items.statement: Surrender regulation impact estimated at 100 bps; mitigating via commission renegotiation
items.quote: We have said that there will be a 100 basis points impact at the company level. At the same time, we will try and reduce that impact by renegotiating with 300-plus partners and all our 2 lakh-plus agents, and we are right now in that process.

items.statement: Credit protect facing competitive pricing pressure; may reduce exposure to certain partners
items.quote: Apart from that, there i s some bit of competitive pressure getting built up because the volumes have gone down . So, we might choose to reduce our exposure to certain partners where the competitive pricing is not making sense.

items.statement: Awarded Best Companies for Women in India 2024 (BFSI) and Exemplar of Inclusion 2024
items.quote: HDFC Life was recognised for its inclusivity and employee-friendly policies, being awarded the Best Companies for Women in India 2024 in the BFSI sector and Exemplar of Inclusion (Most Inclusive Companies Indi a 2024) by Avtar & Seramount.

items.statement: GIFT City branch offers 6 USD-denominated products to NRIs and Resident Indians
items.quote: The GIFT Ci ty branch of our Dubai subsidiary, now offers 6 US dollar denominated products to both NRIs and Resident Indians across life and health categories of insurance.

items.statement: Cautiously optimistic about Q3 momentum but expect seasonal headwinds from furloughs and fewer billing days; wage hikes to pressure margins
items.quote: We are cautiously optimistic about this momentum carrying forward into Q3. However, historically, Q3 experiences seasonal headwinds as well due to furloughs and fewer billing days, which could moderate this momentum to some extent.

items.statement: Wage hikes in Q3 expected to impact EBIT margin by approximately 200 basis points, partially offset by operational efficiencies
