items.statement: CCI reviewing petition on Google/Facebook paying for content; matter sub judice
items.quote: Competition Commission of India is reviewing the petition filed by all of us for this issue of Google and Facebook. And since the matter is sub judice, I may not be able to comment on that.

items.statement: Festival season ad spend "good" but not "amazingly" strong; hope momentum continues
items.quote: So, festival so far we have just completed Nav aratri days. I think it's good and I hope this continues. Though let me put the rider there. It is not amazingly that I'm already burning the crackers right now. It's not that good, but it's good and I hope this continues going forward furthermore

items.statement: Radio ad revenue grew 16% YoY to INR 414 crore in Q2; EBITDA up 22% to INR 132 crore
items.quote: In the Radio segment, we experienced good growth with advertising revenue up 16% year-on-year to INR 414 million compared to INR 356 million. EBITDA in this segment grew by 22% to INR 132 million from INR 108 million.

items.statement: Other expenses increased in Q2 due to delayed staff/market spends, digital expansion, circulation drives; may rise further in Q3
items.quote: Multiple things in that thing. Some of the expenses, which we were delaying from last one year, as you would appreciate, a lot many things for the staff, a lot many things for the market need to be done. As in digital, also, we are looking at newer geographies and all that. So, all these expenses put together, we saw that increase over there.

items.statement: Digital growth driven by content quality, tech improvements, and expansion into UP, Bihar, Uttarakhand
items.quote: So, the growth in Hindi h as come from our state s. And also, we opened up market of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, and Uttarakhand for digital presence. And I think we have got a pretty sizable growth from there also

items.statement: Digital subscriber growth from content quality, user-friendly app, and geographic expansion without physical distribution
items.quote: See advantage in digital is that since I'm already having a digital network, So, I can expand to -- anybody who can read Hindi and Gujarati sitting in any part of the country can subscribe to me, can download my app. So, I don't have to set up a distribution system for him.

items.statement: Digital monetisation timeline unclear; management asks for patience
items.quote: I can only say one word, have patience.

items.statement: Cautiously optimistic about Q3 momentum but expect seasonal headwinds from furloughs and fewer billing days; wage hikes to pressure margins
items.quote: We are cautiously optimistic about this momentum carrying forward into Q3. However, historically, Q3 experiences seasonal headwinds as well due to furloughs and fewer billing days, which could moderate this momentum to some extent.

items.statement: Wage hikes in Q3 expected to impact EBIT margin by approximately 200 basis points, partially offset by operational efficiencies
items.quote: So in terms of our wage hike impact, you could take it maybe approximately 200 basis points, which will be partly offset by our continued operational efficiencies, which we had started driving any which way, 2, 3 quarters back and which are continuing.

items.statement: Headcount rose to over 84,000 with 2,500+ net additions including 1,100+ freshers; LTM attrition stable at 14.5%
items.quote: On the people front, our headcount rose to over 84,000 at the end of the quarter as we added 2,500+ employees during the quarter. For the quarter, our LTM attrition remained stable at 14.5% compared to 14.4% last quarter. We onboarded 1,100-plus freshers this quarter.

items.statement: Billed DSO increased to 60 days from 55; total DSO at 81 days vs 78; target DSO approximately 75 days
items.quote: Billed DSO increased to 60 days versus 55 days in Q1 '25, which is still a reduction of 8 days versus Q2 of the prior year. The unbilled DSO, however, reduced by 2 days. The total DSO was at 81 days compared to 78 days in the previous quarter. We continue to focus on our billing and collection efficiency to move towards our aspired target DSO of approximately 75 days

items.statement: Board declared interim dividend of INR20 per equity share
items.quote: The Board of Directors have declared an interim dividend of INR20 per equity share.

items.statement: Revenue grew 2.8% QoQ and 4.7% YoY in USD; constant currency growth 2.3% QoQ and 4.4% YoY
items.quote: Our Q2 revenue stood at US$1.13 billion, a growth of 2.8% sequentially, and 4.7% on a year-on-year basis in dollar terms. The corresponding constant currency growth was 2.3% quarter-on-quarter and 4.4% year-on-year.

items.statement: Net forex gains increased to US$9 million from US$1.6 million; investment income INR212 crores; effective tax rate 25.8%
items.quote: Net forex gains for the quarter increased to US$9 million compared to US$1.6 million in the previous quarter. Leveraging our strong cash position alongside efficient investment management, we achieved an investment income of INR212 crores this quarter.

items.statement: Cash and investment balances at US$1.43 billion (INR11,974 crores); cash flow hedges US$3,907 million; balance sheet hedges US$326 million
items.quote: The cash and investment balances stood at US$1.43 billion or total INR11,974 crores compared to INR11,334 crores in Q1 FY '25. Return on equity for the quarter was at 23.8%. As of September 30, 2024, our cash flow hedges stood at US$3,907 million, hedges on the balance sheet were US$326 million

items.statement: America contributes 75% of revenue, grew 7% YoY; Europe 14.4%; Rest of World 10.6%
items.quote: In terms of geography, America, which contributes 75% of our revenue has grown by 7% on a year-on-year basis. Europe contributed 14.4%, and the Rest of the World contributed 10.6% of our revenue.

items.statement: Ranked 13 across sectors and 5 in IT & Communication in Business World India's Most Sustainable Companies Top 50 for 2024
items.quote: We're pleased to announce that LTIMindtree has attained a rank of 13 across sectors and rank 5 in IT and communication sector, in Business World India's Most Sustainable Companies Top 50 listings for 2024.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY25 revenue growth guidance of 8-10% in constant currency and aspiration of 16% EBIT margin
items.quote: We are thus confident of broad-based growth continuing in the coming quarters and reaffirm our FY25 guidance of 8 -10% revenue growth in constant currency and aspiration of 16% EBIT margin levels.

items.statement: Medium-term ambition to build three $1Bn segments and reach $2Bn revenue with 17-18% EBIT margin
items.quote: Before I close, I do want to reconfirm that we stand strong in wanting to build three $1Bn segments and get to revenues of $2 Bn with 17-18% EBIT margin in the medium term.

items.statement: Q2 EBIT margin at 15.1%, down sequentially due to SG&A investments; H2 margins expected to be better than H1
items.quote: Our gross margin remained flat. However, on account of investments in sales and technology, our SG&A as a percentage of revenue increased by 40 bps sequentially. Hence our EBIT margin for the quarter came in at 15.1%, slightly lower compared to Q1 FY25.

items.statement: Wage hikes planned for Q3 effective November with ~100-125 bps full quarter impact; two months impact in Q3
items.quote: On the wage hikes, yes, we plan them to be in Q3 and will be effective from November onwards. So, we will see likely two months of impact in Q3 for increments. Just to complete, the point, we should likely see in a full quarter an impact of close to about 100 bps to 125 bps on account of increments.

items.statement: SG&A expected to normalize around 10% of revenue; absolute and percentage improvement expected in H2
items.quote: I already talked about that SG&A should normalize at about 10% levels. So, we should see certainly an improvement. And part of that will come because you're seeing growth. Part of that will come in absolute as well, right.

items.statement: Mobility grew 5% QoQ driven by SDV and Hybridization; Q3 expected to be soft due to seasonality/furloughs, rebound in Q4
items.quote: Overall, we see a robust deal pipeline for Mobility. However, Q3 will be slightly soft on account of seasonality. We expect this to rebound in Q4.

items.statement: Sustainability grew 6.5% QoQ with both Process and Industrial performing strongly; growth momentum expected to sustain in Q3 and beyond
items.quote: In summary, for Sustainability, we are seeing a good number of deals in the pipeline – both at Process and Industrial and expect the growth momentum to sustain in Q3 and beyond.

items.statement: Tech grew ~1% QoQ; Hyperscalers and Semcon performed well; transformational deals in Comms/Media could close in Q3; Med-Tech rebounding
items.quote: Overall, with the pipeline in large deals in play, we expect Tech growth to improve in Q3, led by our work with Semcon, Hyperscalers and Med-Tech.

items.statement: Won two $20M deals, four $10M deals, and two significant empanelment agreements across segments in Q2
items.quote: We won two $20 Mn deals, four $10 Mn deals and two significant empanelment agreements. These wins have been across segments.

items.statement: Pipeline growing healthily with large deals in $25-100M range; expecting good closures in Q3 and early Q4
items.quote: Our pipeline continues to grow at a very healthy pace with a good number of large deals in the $ 25 - 100 Mn range. We are tracking these deals closely and expect a good number of closures in Q3 and early Q4.

items.statement: $30M accounts increased to 7 (up 1 QoQ, 3 YoY); $10M accounts increased to 33 (up 2 QoQ and YoY)
items.quote: The number of $30 Mn accounts has increased to 7 now, up by 1 QoQ and 3 YoY. Similarly, the number of $10 Mn accounts has increased to 33 now, up by 2 QoQ and YoY.

items.statement: Maharashtra cybersecurity project is fixed-price, milestone-based; capex execution ongoing over next 3-6 months followed by 5-year O&M phase
items.quote: Maha cyber as a project, this is a fixed price project, right? And all these milestones are planned, and all revenue recognition is tied to those milestones being achieved. And we are, in fact, on target in terms of achieving those milestones, which, of course, will trickle down in terms of revenue.

items.statement: Q2 DSO at 99 days (vs 102 in Q1); unbilled days at 17 (vs 23); combined DSO 116 days within target range of 115-125
items.quote: Our Q2 DSO was at 99 days compared to 102 days in Q1, unbilled days was at 17 days in Q2 compared to 23 days in Q1. The combined DSO, including unbilled, stood at 116 days compared to 125 days in Q1, which is within our target range of 115 to 125 days for the year.

items.statement: Q2 free cash flow at ₹417 crores; YTD free cash flow at ₹328 crores; expect H2 free cash flows better than H1 similar to FY24 pattern
items.quote: As a result of improvement in DSO, our Q2 free cash flow came in at a healthy ₹ 417 crores, leading to YTD free cash flows at ₹ 328 crores. We will continue the effort to improve cash flow during the rest of the year.

items.statement: Board approved interim dividend of ₹17 per share; final dividend of ~₹349 crores paid in Q2
items.quote: As you would have seen today, the Board approved an interim dividend of ₹ 17 per share.

items.statement: Headcount at 23,698 in Q2 (up from 23,577 in Q1); attrition slightly down; FY25 fresher hiring target of ~2,000 (vs ~1,500 in FY24)
items.quote: For FY25, we planned around 2,000 freshers to be hired. We've been implementing that. So accordingly, we've seen freshers in Q1 and Q2, that intake has indeed happened. In fact, this year, our fresher intake will be higher than what it was last year. Last year, we did close to about 1,500 freshers hiring.

items.statement: Offshore percentage at 58.3%; targeting gradual improvement to 60% aspiration
items.quote: The Onsite:Offshore mix was at similar range as compared to Q1. Offshore percent age now stands at 58.3%. We continue to work on measures to gradually improve this metric to our aspiration of 60%.

items.statement: Launched LTTSiDrive framework for SDV implementation (won 2 programs in US/Europe); launched Factory Next framework for Industry 4.0 (2 US deployments started); launched GenIQ platform for AI/GenAI applications
items.quote: We launched LTTSiDrive – our proprietary framework for accelerating SDV implementation, applicable for both Auto and Trucks and Off Highway. We've already won 2 programs – one each in US and Europe leveraging LTTSiDrive.

items.statement: Filed 51 patents in Q2; cumulative filings at 1,394; ranked leader by HFS (IoT), Avasant (Digital Engineering), Zinnov (Data & AI)
items.quote: engineers added a total of 51 patents filings in Q2 and our cumulative filing s stands at 1,394. • The innovation is also reflected in the rankings we have been ranked as leaders by: o HFS and IoT services. o Avasant in Digital engineering Services o Zinnov in data and AI

items.statement: Signed partnership with Etihad Rail for digital solutions and intelligent transportation system; large deal with O&G customer for digital twin of refinery; empanelment as projects engineering partner for new plant with command center
items.quote: We signed a partnership with Etihad Rail for the development of digital solutions and creati on of an intelligent transportation system. We have multiple solutions in Rail leveraging AI and augmented reality that have been successfully deployed by customers.

items.statement: Client advisory council of 16 members with combined $2T market cap and $400B revenue validated LTTS differentiated solutions and positioning
items.quote: This priority was further validated during our recent concluded client advisory council meeting, which consists of 16 members, with combined market cap of $2 Tn and a revenue of $400 Bn.

items.statement: OEM revenue share increased significantly vs Tier 1s over last year; Tier 1s facing challenges but LTTS creating deals to help them; no slowdown seen at US/Europe/Japan OEMs
items.quote: We had a strategy about 8, 12 quarters ago that we will start to improve our OEM dependency and reduce our dependency on Tier 1s. That has played out well for us because now, the percentage revenue from automotive and Trucks & Off Highway that we do with OEMs has seen a quantum shift towards OEMs as opposed to Tier 1s.

items.statement: US election uncertainty causing some deal delays; automotive furloughs in Q3 (Detroit/Europe phenomenon); no major furloughs expected in Tech or Sustainability
items.quote: We are seeing furloughs in automotive, like I said, and that's why we said it will be a little soft. The other areas don't get so impacted by furloughs, but this is a work in progress. We are fairly comfortable with the stage, like I said, but there is an election uncertainty that we'll go through, and we'll see where it goes.

items.statement: Revenue: ₹2,573 crores (4.5% QoQ, 7.8% YoY); $ revenue growth 3.9% reported, 3.4% constant currency; Net income ₹320 crores (1.3% YoY, 12.4% of revenue)
items.quote: Our revenue for the quarter was ₹ 2,573 crores, a growth of 4.5% on a sequential basis. Our YoY growth for Q2 FY25 came in at 7.8%.

items.statement: Company targets 1.5x industry volume growth, implying ~9% for FY25
items.quote: We, at Dalmia, have laid a strong foundation to grow volumes by at least 1.5x of the sector.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton sustainable at INR 900-1,000 for FY25, long-term target INR 1,100-1,200
items.quote: I think INR900 to INR1,000 /T at least this year should be sustainable. And again, it depends on how the demand also behaves. So we think that in the long term, the guidance that we've given of INR1,100 to INR1,200 should be doable

items.statement: FY25 capex guided at INR 3,000-3,300 crores, FY26 at ~INR 2,500 crores
items.quote: During the full year, we expect to spend about INR3,000 crores to INR3,300 crores, which is largely towards capacity expansion, including land for future projects and certain cost reduction projects, including renewable energy and coal blocks.

items.statement: Maintenance capex ~INR 250-300 crores per annum
items.quote: It's close to about INR250 crores to INR300 crores per annum.

items.statement: Current capacity 46.6 mt, on track for 49.5 mt by end FY25; 75 mt target by FY28
items.quote: On the capacity side, we are currently at 46.6 million tons and on track to reach 49.5 million tons by the end of financial year '25.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA/t INR 650, H1 INR 782; expect improvement in H2 with price recovery
items.quote: Our EBITDA during the quarter declined by 27% Y-o-Y to INR434 crores, which works out to INR650 on a per ton basis.

items.statement: Cement prices down 5-7% QoQ and 10-12% YoY in South/East; Oct prices flat vs Q2 avg
items.quote: The cement prices declined during Q2 due to weak demand scenario, particularly in South and Eastern markets. These markets saw a decline of 5% to 7% Q-o-Q and about 10% to 12% on Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Power & fuel cost down 11.3% YoY to INR 1,012/t; fuel cost INR 1.36/kcal; RE share 39%
items.quote: The power and fuel cost declined 11.3% Y-o-Y to INR1,012 per ton of cement production, mainly due to a $26 decline in the fuel consumption cost to about $101 on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Target INR 150-200/t cost savings: INR 50 logistics, INR 100-150 from coal blocks & renewables
items.quote: Logistics will be about INR50 and balance INR100 to INR150 will come from coal blocks as well as renewables.

items.statement: RE capacity 202 MW operational; 278 MW group captive signed; target 341 MW operational by FY25 end (45% RE share)
items.quote: In total, we have signed 278 megawatts of long -term renewable power agreements under the group captive arrangement so far. The commi ssioning of these renewable power plants is expected to begin from next quarter onwards, and by end of FY'25, we should have operational RE capacity of 341-megawatt

items.statement: Incentive outstanding INR 779 cr; FY25 accrual & collection target INR 300 cr; INR 46 cr received in early Oct
items.quote: Our incentive outstanding on 30th September was INR779 crores. For FY'25, we expec t total incentive accruals and collections of INR300 crores

items.statement: Gross debt INR 4,784 cr, net debt INR 644 cr; net debt/EBITDA 0.25x; policy to keep net debt/EBITDA ≤ 2x
items.quote: As of 30th September, our gross and net debt marginally increased to INR4,784 crores and INR644 crores, respectively. Hence, our net debt to EBITDA Dalmia Bharat Limited. October 21, 2024 stood at 0

items.statement: Interim dividend INR 4/share declared; capital allocation policy: up to 10% of free cash flow as dividends
items.quote: Lastly, the Board has declared an interim dividend of INR4 per share.

items.statement: H1 industry growth muted at 2-3%; H2 expected 7-8% YoY on govt infra spend catch-up, real estate, private capex
items.quote: Infrastructure spending of the government is only at 27% of the budgeted allocation till August 2024. This percentage in FY '24 was at 39% for the first 5 months. There is no reason to believe that the government will not spend the budgeted amount given the robust collections.

items.statement: Central region dealer network from Jaypee tolling largely retained; serving from Eastern plants
items.quote: I think most of them, are still continuing when we are currently doing the operations through our Eastern plants.

items.statement: Top 4 players share to reach 60% by FY27; consolidation raising entry barriers
items.quote: We also think that the top players are expanding faster than the smaller players and there is increased M&A in the sector. So the share of top four will go to 60% by financial year '27.

items.statement: Industry utilization ~67%; Dalmia Q2 utilization 58% (seasonally weak)
items.quote: for this quarter we had a capacity utilization of 58%, but we expect it to go up in the coming quarters because this was a seasonally weak quarter. Industry is also I think currently about 67% or so.

items.statement: Jaypee tolling discontinued in Q2; INR 113 cr impairment taken last quarter; no further exposure expected
items.quote: Since we have done the tolling operations in the last 1.5 years, so we had to give some advances to Jaypee for clearing the past defaults of taxes , etc or power payments, et c without which the plant could not have started. So since we could not recover, that money was to be adjusted in the acquisition of the assets. So since the company has gone into IBC, considering the uncertainty of realizati

name: Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy Ltd

items.statement: Full-year order inflow guidance of INR 8,000 crores and revenue guidance of INR 8,000 crores for FY25
items.quote: We have continued to build on the strong ordering momentum of Q1 by announcing an additional INR 2,044 crores worth of new orders in Q2. Our total new order inflow this fiscal have touched INR 4,214 crores thus far, and are happy to report that we remain on track to meet our full year order inflow guidance of INR 8,000 crores.

items.statement: Unexecuted order value at INR 10,549 crores, highest in company history, 78% domestic
items.quote: Our unexecuted order value now stands at over INR 10,500 crores, and it is the highest in the company's history.

items.statement: Q2 order inflow of INR 2,044 crores, all domestic; H1 total INR 4,214 crores
items.quote: We have continued to build on the strong ordering momentum of Q1 by announcing an additional INR 2,044 crores worth of new orders in Q2. Our total new order inflow this fiscal have touched INR 4,214 crores thus far

items.statement: Key order wins: JSW 2x250MW AC BESS (1 GWh) in Rajasthan, JSW 20MW floating solar, Brookfield 633MW DC BOS, repeat orders from ENGIE and AMPYR, NTPC 250MW AC turnkey
items.quote: One of our key order wins this quarter was the LOI for 2 x 250-megawatt AC standalone BESS plant at Rajasthan by JSW. This project till date is India's largest battery energy storage project and one of the very few projects of gigawatt -hour scale in single location globally, which shall be executed by 2025.

items.statement: Domestic gross margin ~9% reported, ~10.5% adjusted for cost-equal-revenue projects; guided 10-11% range for FY25
items.quote: However, it is important to note that while our domestic margins was lower at 9%, approximately 10% of this domestic revenue that was booked in this quarter was cost equal to revenue in some projects, which were yet to achieve the POCM threshold. If you adjust for the same, the blended gross margin for the domestic segment turns out to roughly about 10.5%.

items.statement: O&M gross margin 28% in Q2 (lower expenditure), expected to normalize to ~25% steady state
items.quote: Our O&M gross margin at 28% was higher than average due to lower expenditure that was incurred in Q2. However, we anticipate these margins to normalize due to post monsoon maintenance that is likely in the second half of this year. Recurring O&M margins are trending towards more steady-state margins of approximately 25% that we have guided to previously.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 7-8% going forward as revenue scales with stable overheads
items.quote: We can expect between 7% to 8% EBITDA number going forward because heavy rationalization on overheads are going on. And we'll come back with exact numbers when the heavy revenue quarters will be there in the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: No specific capex guidance; execution scale-up funded by IREDA loan, restored non-fund limits, and vendor open credit
items.quote: We plan to achieve this execution scale up through the new INR500 crores loan facility that we had availed from IREDA, fresh sanctions and restoration of non-fund-based limits with the credit rating upgrade that happened last night, and also through negotiation for open credit with large key vendors.

items.statement: IREDA sanctioned INR 500 crores loan at 11.6%; credit rating upgraded to BBB- (investment grade) by ACUITE
items.quote: The recent INR500 crores loan sanctioned by IREDA and the credit rating upgrade received last night, moving us to investment grade, will go a long way in helping us achieve our revenue guidance.

items.statement: Total net debt ~INR 326 crores as of Sep 2024; INR 109 crores indemnity proceeds billed, expected by Nov 30
items.quote: Total net debt stands at roughly INR326 crores as of September '24. On the indemnity proceeds, there are approximately INR 109 crores, which has been billed and it is largely expected to take care of debt repayments due in the second half of this fiscal year.

items.statement: Non-fund-based limits constrained in Q2; expect fresh limits within 30-45 days post rating upgrade; targeting to double LC limits
items.quote: Anywhere in the next 30 to 45 days, I think we should be having most of the incremental facilities that we're talking about in place. And like I mentioned, this is not a -- it happened yesterday last night, and then therefore, we are now going to start initiating.

items.statement: Over INR 2,000 crores open credit agreed from key vendors (modules, trackers, cables) to support H2 execution
items.quote: Some of our key suppliers, key components, including the module supplier, tracker supplier and some of the most reputed cable supplies in the country are looking at our improving balance sheet and the order book have agreed to offer us very good attractive open credit terms, which will help us significantly ramping up the revenues in next 2 quarters.

items.statement: Strong bid pipeline: ~23 GW likely to be awarded in next 6-12 months in India; H1 addressable market ~INR 16,000-17,000 crores
items.quote: We are continuing to see a very strong bid pipeline in place for India with over 23 gigawatts of projects likely to be awarded in the next 6 to 12 months.

items.statement: Competitive intensity rising with market growth and new entrants; company selective with 46% bid success rate and 27% market share of addressable market in H1
items.quote: So as market is growing significantly, there is -- like market is exploding completely. And as market is growing, more new players are also entering into the market. So competitive intensity is going up, but we have been very careful in picking up the orders.

items.statement: Strategic shift to turnkey projects (including module supply) for PSU bids; modules sourced from Tier-1 Indian suppliers with back-to-back contracts
items.quote: Yes, turnkey projects because as you have seen in some past quarters also that some of the projects we have taken, which include the supply of modules. So that's what we mean by the turnkey projects.

items.statement: Largest standalone BESS project (1 GWh) won; working on multiple hybrid projects in India and abroad
items.quote: As of now, no, but we are working on standalone BESS projects, but we are working on multiple hybrid projects in India and abroad foreign markets, international markets, which will materialize soon.

items.statement: H1: 11 of 12 orders from private IPPs; PSU bids finalizing in Q3/Q4; repeat orders from ENGIE, AMPYR; breakthrough with Brookfield; NTPC relationship strengthening
items.quote: In H1, 11 out of 12 projects that we have won have come from private sector. Our existing private customers have exciting growth plans, and we are confident of growing the order book with them in H2.

items.statement: Reliance pilot project completion expected this quarter; bigger rollout in Q4 FY25 or Q1 FY26
items.quote: So, as I discussed in my last earnings call that we are working on pilot project for Reliance in which they are testing multiple technologies and multiple combinations, and we expect to complete that project in this quarter. And bigger rollout will take place after that.

items.statement: O&M portfolio at 7.8 GW as of Sep 2024; expected to grow as EPC projects commission
items.quote: Our O&M portfolio outlook remains strong and portfolio stands at 7.8 gigawatts as of September 2024. The benefit of a larger portfolio is expected to bear fruit in the coming quarters as our EPC pipeline will continue to feed a large portfolio of O&M projects over the next 12 to 18 months.

items.statement: CFO Bahadur Dastoor exited for personal reasons; external search underway, strong internal team in place
items.quote: I think our CFO, Mr. Bahadur Dastoor, has been a very valuable and long-term associate with the company. He has contributed in all the aspects of the functioning. But it's a part of, I think, one's personal aspiration, personal reasons and career growth, I think, which he has taken.

items.statement: Five execution teams deployed (2 PSU, 2 IPP, 1 Reliance); reinforced with senior leadership and strong engineering team; retention via ESOPs and appraisals
items.quote: So, we have, in parallel, five execution teams, which are handling and they have been reinforced significantly. So -- and they are being backed up by one of the strongest engineering teams in the country.

items.statement: Nigeria project on track, no cancellation risk; signing delayed by domestic politics but NDPHC board approved; US EXIM Bank support with $120B Congressional allocation
items.quote: No. Actually, we are -- like Nigeria project is on track, and it is definitely coming. So there is no question of cancellation of Nigerian order.

items.statement: Indemnity-backed legacy projects: ~INR 800 crores cash out, full crystallization over 24-36 months
items.quote: The company continues to remain cash out on approximately INR 800 crores of indemnity-backed legacy projects, which we believe will crystallize fully over the course of the next 24 to 36 months.

items.statement: Promoter Khurshed Daruvala reaffirmed long-term commitment, no further share sale planned
items.quote: So, as you must have read in papers, our most active promoter, Mr. Khurshed Daruvala has reiterated his position, that he's going to continue and is a long-term investor in the company, and he's going to be there. And there is no plan of any further sale of shares by him.

items.statement: Refined metal production guidance unchanged; confident of achieving it
items.quote: Refined metal production, we are confident on achieving the guidance and would like to keep it unchanged.

items.statement: Cost of production guidance kept unchanged at $1,050-$1,100 per ton; confident of delivering towards lower end
items.quote: But I'm sure we have a better cost in terms o f what we are predicting, but would like to keep it unchanged between $1,050 to $1,100 that has been overall given, but we are confident that we will be delivering towards the lower end of the cost band

items.statement: Capex guidance kept intact
items.quote: Coming to the closure, we keep our cost and capex guidance intact, and now I open the floor for your questions.

items.statement: New 160,000 tpa roaster in Debari and 510,000 tpa fertilizer project on track; final commissioning targeted Q4 FY25 and Q2 FY26 respectively
items.quote: Progress for the new 160,000 tons per annum roaster in Debari and the 510,000 tons Hindustan Zinc Fertilizer Private Limited project is on track with final commissioning targeted by quarter 4 of this year and quarter 2 of next year, respectively.

items.statement: Targeting at least 1.2 million tons refined metal production next financial year
items.quote: Yes, yes, of course. Of course, we will try. We will -- at least 1.2 million ton next financial year.

items.statement: Expansion to 2 million ton mine run rate feasible; global mining contractor to be appointed by end of November
items.quote: So by the end of November, we should be able to fix the global contractor, whom we will appoint for starting the mine development because that is the first part is the mine development, then only we can produce.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin over 50%, highest in 8 quarters, up 450 bps YoY
items.quote: The resultant financial numbers have been the best in terms of EBITDA margin clocking over 50%, highest in last 8 quarters with 450 bps Y-o-Y increase in margin.

items.statement: Q2 zinc cost of production before royalty $1,071/t, down 6% YoY and 3% QoQ; H1 COP $1,089/t, 4-year low

items.statement: H1 refined metal production 524,000 tons (+5% YoY)

items.quote: We are very confident that after this shutdown, the fumer will come back in the way it will operate and we know exactly how to operate now. So we should get fantastic results starting from quarter 3 into quarter 4.

items.statement: All-women surface rescue teams established (30 employees); first all-women underground mine rescue team won World's Second Best Women's Taskforce at international competition

items.quote: It's not on the table.

items.quote: Going forward, we definitely expect that the turnover would be in this range, maybe a little modest growth but will be in this range.

items.quote: We are hoping that the steel prices will stabilize. And if that happens, then we may see that we may go back to the original close to 19% EBITDA margin.

items.quote: One thing that seems to be very clear from this result, that in the last 2 years, there is a clear break from the EBITDA percentage, which used to be around 12% to 14%. Now we are in the range of 18% to 19%.

items.quote: The debt, just to go over the figures. Currently, it stands at long -term debt, INR1,185 crores. Working capital, INR2,226 crores, which is total INR3,411 crores as compared to INR3,992 crores of the June quarter.

items.statement: Working capital debt at INR 2,226 crore, down from June quarter; decline attributed to completion of export orders which have higher working capital cycles.
items.quote: One reason that we are seeing a decline in the working capital is also because now the export orders have been finished. So export orders typically tend to have higher working capital cycle.

items.statement: Capex modest: coke oven battery renewal at Mundra (INR 300-350 cr over few years), Nashik capacity expansion 40-50% (INR ~200 cr over 2-3 years), Haresamudram debottlenecking (INR ~200 cr over 2-3 years); all phased to keep term loan ~INR 1

items.statement: Solar glass demand robust; lithium softness; flat glass okay; other chemical demand okay; container demand softness offset by solar glass worldwide
items.quote: Solar glass demand has continued to be robust. The issue remains in terms of lithium, there has been a bit of softness. The flat glass has been okay. items.statement: US contract discussions for 2025 ongoing; demand balanced with bias at balance level; hopeful long-term trends continue; watchful on contracting
items.quote: So, in terms of contracts, let them settle. items.statement: China moderation in lithium market taken up by solar glass; expect more balanced situation in H2 as constrained supplies may come on stream; US exports filled China shortfall

items.statement: US operations producing better than past; postponed September shutdown to October; expect ahead of last year in volume; peak load production lowers effective cost improving margin
items.quote: So, as far as the U.S. is concerned, because of operational issues and other issues in our geographies including, we did postpone our US shutdown, which would have come in the month of September to October. items.statement: US export pricing believed to have bottomed out; cannot get worse from here

items.statement: India cost increase ~Rs.2,000/ton ($30/ton); expect Rs.1,500/ton recovery; Rs.500/ton higher cost to stick for next two quarters

The Rs 500 per tonne will stick in there as higher cost and that is at least our line of sight for the next two quarters.

items.statement: New India capacity (2.25 lakh tons soda ash, 140,000 tons bicarb) expected to be placed in market by end of Q3 or early Q4; no market demand issues anticipated
items.quote: We don't anticipate by the time we finish this quarter or the beginning of next quarter, we will have any issues in terms of market with this. Obviously, we are in the process of making sure we are able to place the product and market demand has not been an issue in India.

items.statement: UK loss due to negative spark spreads from high wind energy; wheeled power at challenged margins; hopeful to resolve by end of Q3
items.quote: Yes, UK had a bit of a wobble this quarter mainly because of negative spark spreads. This has continued because of high wind energy. We wheeled power into the grid, and these were done at margins which were fairly challenged, and we are hopeful that by the time we finish the third quarter, we should be out of this problem.

items.statement: Global soda ash pricing at bottom; exporters selling at cost or below cost; no headroom for further reduction unless distress sales (not seen)
items.quote: Most people are, if they export, they are exporting at cost or below cost. So, I think we don't believe that there is any headroom for further reduction in pricing unless some people are sitting on inventory and there is a distress sale which we haven't seen.

items.statement: Anti-dumping investigation by DGTR on soda ash imports from Iran, Russia etc.; quasi-judicial process; will submit data; hopeful unreasonable pricing at/below cost will be addressed
items.quote: See, the investigation is being done by DGTR in Ministry of Commerce. We will let that process continue. It's a quasi-judicial process. So, I would not want to make a comment on it. It has been taken up, suo-moto on the basis of surge in imports mainly coming from Iran and Russia etc.

items.statement: Silica expansion: 60,000 tons (3 modules of 20,000 tons) approved this quarter; execution 24-36 months; first stream ~24 months, then 6-month intervals; revenue run-rate ~Rs.500 crore at full capacity
items.quote: So, that is part of the presentation. I have already highlighted that we are adding 60,000 tons of silica business at which point of time this is likely to be having the run rate of about Rs.500 odd crore in revenue. And this project will get a formal approval somewhere in this quarter and it will be three modules of 20,000 tons each.

items.statement: Next phase soda ash expansion: 0.316 MT soda ash and 2.3 lakh tons salt; part of presentation circulated
items.quote: The next phase of soda ash expansion also is underway which also goes for formal approval, and we will come back to you, but we have already highlighted the next phase is 0.316 MT of soda ash and another 2.3 lakh tons of salt.

items.statement: US expansion: 400,000 tons on schedule; regulatory clearances expected by March 2025; design engineering and logistics tie-ups underway

items.statement: Kenya expansion: 300,000 tons modular capacity using electric calcination (lower carbon); implementation underway; ~36 months timeline
items.quote: The Kenya capacity is going to be a modular capacity because we are trying out for the first time electric calcination, which is much lower in carbon intensity. So, we are first testing it out and then the overall modular capacity expanded in about 36 months will be another 300,000 ton out of Kenya.

items.statement: Total ~1 million tons expansion across India (3.2 lakh), US (4 lakh), Kenya (3 lakh) over ~30-36 months
items.quote: Yes, 3 lakh capacity in Kenya and about 4 lakhs in U.S., and 3.2 lakh in India, so all put together a million ton across these three states.

items.statement: Global soda ash capacity shifts: ~100,000 tons pullback in US offset by ~100,000 tons debottlenecking elsewhere; net balanced

items.quote: So, this is what I mentioned that in case that capacity is fully absorbed, and those issues stabilize, the imports will tend to moderate into China. So, we must watch for that and it's mainly that has played a big role in the increased exports into China.

items.statement: Soda ash long-term demand positive due to sustainability theme; customers demanding lower carbon soda ash; pivot to renewable electricity and electric calcination (trial in Kenya)
items.quote: Firstly, the long-term demand trend for the soda ash business is positive because soda ash plays into sustainability theme. items.statement: FY25 capex guidance of at least Rs 10,000 crore
items.quote: we will be able to close this year with a capex of about Rs 10,000 crore at least.

items.statement: EBITDA growth expected to exceed 15% in FY25
items.quote: Now, this will surely bring the growth in EBITDA that we projected, which will be more than 15%.

items.statement: EBITDA growth expected to exceed 20% over next couple of years
items.quote: Therefore, the growth is going to correspond to that kind of capex, which it will be in excess of 20%.

items.statement: Transmission under-construction projects to reach Rs 45,000 crore with EBITDA over Rs 5,500 crore
items.quote: We also expect to add another Rs 15,000 crore at least to this kitty, so it will reach to about Rs 45,000 crore of project under implementation. With that, we will have EBITDA more than Rs 5,500 crore.

items.statement: Smart meter installation target of 40-42 lakh meters by end of FY25
items.quote: We expect to add about 30 to 35 lakh meters in next six months. So, we will close year with the installation of about 40 to 42 lakh meters.

items.statement: Smart meter deployment rate target of 16,000-20,000 meters per day from next quarter
items.quote: We have already reached upto 10,000 meters per day from 4,000 meters per day and expect to take it up to 16,000 meters per day to 20,000 meters per day.

items.statement: Smart meter installation target of ~1 crore meters in FY26 and balance in FY27
items.quote: at least we will be able to add about 1 crore meter next year and balance one in the subsequent year.

items.statement: C&I business targeting 5,000 million units volume by year-end with Rs 150 crore annualized EBITDA
items.quote: By the year-end, we will be able to close, or we'll have a volume of about 5,000 million units. And that will contribute on an annualized basis of about Rs 150 crore of EBITDA.

items.statement: C&I business targeting 7,000-10,000 million units in a couple of years
items.quote: what we are targeting is about 7,000 million to 10,000 million units in a couple of years.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected at 20% for H2 FY25 and going forward
items.quote: We are expecting an effective tax of around 20 percentage which will continue as a third half.

items.statement: Transmission under-construction projects increased to ~Rs 31,000 crore from Rs 17,000 crore
items.quote: we have secured four new transmission projects and with that our under-construction projects have reached to ~Rs 31,000 crore from Rs 17,000 crore.

items.statement: Expect to win Rs 15,000-20,000 crore transmission projects in next 6 months at current market share
items.quote: Even if we take the current market share, then we hope to get about Rs 15,000 crore to Rs 20,000 crore worth project more in next six month's time.

items.statement: Smart meter awarded contract of 2.3 crore meters; 6.73 lakh installed so far
items.quote: what we have got right now is about 2.3 crore meters. We will complete about 45 lakh meters in the current year.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 capex deployment of ~Rs 3,000 crore, 2.5x YoY; H1 FY25 capex of Rs 4,400 crore, 1.7x YoY
items.quote: We deployed capex of ~Rs 3,000 crore in the current quarter, which is 2.5 times of the capex that we deployed same quarter last year. The total capex of first half of the current year, which is Rs 4,400 crore, is 1.7 times of the capex that we deployed in the same period last year.

items.statement: FY25 capex breakdown: distribution Rs 1,600-1,700 crore, smart metering Rs 3,000 crore, rest transmission
items.quote: Out of this Rs 10,000 crore, the distribution would be around Rs 1,600 crore to Rs 1,700 crore, smart metering around Rs 3,000 crore, and the rest will be from the transmission side.

items.statement: AEML annual capex of Rs 1,700-1,800 crore, adding Rs 800-1,000 crore to RAB yearly
items.quote: We do capex of about Rs 1,700 crore to Rs 1,800 crore and minus depreciation Rs 600 to Rs 700. So, around Rs 800 to Rs 1,000 crore addition of RAB every year.

items.statement: Smart meter business margin 80-85%, may dip to 75% in initial ramp-up years
items.quote: The smart meters have a margin of around 80% to 85%. In the initial years because of the initial ramp up, the margins may come down to around 75%.

items.statement: C&I business margins range from 10 paise/unit for service contracts to higher for complex contracts
items.quote: if it's only a service contract then would be in a simple back-to-back contract then it could be around Rs 10 paise, but if it is a complex contract, a lot of stitching to be done and position is to be taken, then obviously those margins will be in a higher range.

items.statement: Distribution electricity sales grew 7%; distribution losses reduced to 4.85%
items.quote: the growth in electricity sale was to the tune of 7 % and continuously with our endeavour, we have been able to reduce distribution losses to 4.85%.

items.statement: Mumbai HVDC project capex ~Rs 7,000 crore, commissioning by August 2025
items.quote: Expected capex is about Rs 7000 cores. And the project is progressing very well. And we will be able to commission within timeline, which is August 25.

items.statement: Raised Rs 8,300 crore equity through QIP in Q2 FY25
items.quote: During the quarter, AESL raised equity of Rs 8,300 crore through QIP.

items.statement: Regulatory receivables liquidation ahead of schedule; Rs 900 crore remaining as of Sept 2024, full liquidation by March 2025
items.quote: the regulatory deferral account which was there of Rs 1,600 crore is in the course of complete liquidation. Currently, we have the out of the Rs 1,600 crore only around Rs 900 crore which is left by the end of September.

items.statement: On-ground resistance from motivated factors during smart meter rollout, but not a key delay reason
items.quote: There is resistance, not mainly from a customer, but all those m otivated factors on the ground, but that's a part of business. We have to deal with that and find your way in implementing

items.statement: Full-year FY25 revenue expected above Rs 2,000 crore with at least 16% EBITDA margin
items.quote: And if you talk about the top line revenue, that will be also more than 2000 crores.

items.statement: FY26 top-line growth guided at 20% year-on-year
items.quote: 26 we are expecting 20% growth in the top line.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 gross margin expanded to 34% from 26% a year ago
items.quote: we saw an improvement in profitability with our gross margins expanding from 26% to 34% year on year.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin at 19% driven by stable raw material prices and higher branded sales
items.quote: our Q2 FY25 E BITDA excluding other income was around Rupees 147 crores, enhancing the EBITDA margin to around 19

items.statement: B2C gross margin 40-45% versus B2B 20-25%
items.quote: B2C margin is near about gross margin, we can say 45% or 40% and where our B2B business we talk about that will come around or 20-25%.

items.statement: Branded business now 65% of revenue with 35% volume growth in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Our focus on strengthening our branded business is yielding positive results. So, our branded business is now accounting for 65% of our overall revenue.

items.statement: Rs 80-90 crore brownfield capex for backward integration from preferential allotment proceeds
items.quote: Mostly we are expanding our backward integration as technical and intermediate in that we are giving almost 80 to 90 crore

items.statement: Capex completion expected in 2-3 quarters; commercial production by Q1-Q2 FY26
items.quote: I would say within two to three quarters, we will be able to complete the plant.

items.statement: Nemagen targeting Rs 100 crore sales in first full year
items.quote: we look forward to doin g 100 crores plant business in this full year of induction itself

items.statement: Expect strong rabi season supported by reservoirs at 88% capacity, 14% above normal
items.quote: we are expecting a good rabi season, upcoming rabi season.

items.statement: Chinese dumping stabilised as factories stop production below cost
items.quote: now I would say the situation is ther e where prices have fallen down a lot and now the situation is that the factory has to stop because they cannot run at that

items.statement: Operating cash flow improved to Rs 125 crore in H1 FY25 from Rs 5 crore a year ago
items.quote: We have seen a significant improvement in the cash flows from operating activities rising from 5 crores in H1 FY24 to 125 crores in H1 FY25.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity improved to 0.59 as of Sep 2024 from 0.90 in Mar 2024
items.quote: our debt-to-equity ratio has improved to 0.59 as of September 30th, 2024 compared to 0.90 on March 31st, 2024.

items.statement: Preferential allotment of Rs 200 crore approved; 25% expected within 15 days of regulatory approvals
items.quote: We are expecting an in-principal approval for the preferential allotment and we'll be hoping to complete the preferential allotment and 25% payment will be received within 15 days of receipt of all regulatory approvals.

items.statement: Income tax search proceedings closed with no extra demand expected
items.quote: We have fully updated with the proceedings and as of now, we don't have any extra demand whatever is our regular, we are paying that on time always that is our advantage and everything and according to us, there is no demand we are expecting for this income tax, no extra demand, I mean.

items.statement: China subsidiary incorporated for supplier collaboration and R&D; registrations underway in Brazil, Australia
items.quote: This year, we have incorporated a subsidiary in China as a strategic decision. This subsidiary will be focused on developing deeper cooperation with our suppliers and increasing ou r collaboration for R&D in new technical and intermediates

items.statement: Patented product volume grew 38% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: the growth of the patented molecule in our in Q2 even that has grown up to 38% that is in our PPT also you can see which we hav e uploaded there

items.statement: Pan-India distribution strengthened; strong presence now in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
items.quote: Today I can say confidently we have a good strong presence in Andhra, Telangana and with the completion of the, you know the southern market, which is a very important part of the Indian geography and the market, we hope to be able to have that complete Pan India presence.

items.statement: Provision for sales returns increased conservatively; actual returns expected well below provision
items.quote: this year in Conservative we have taken the good provision for that, which is a provision is more than last year, but again provision is more, but the expectation is less to return back because return back is not that much

items.statement: Sale of IndoStar Home Finance to EQT for INR1,750 crores on fully diluted basis, subject to RBI approval and other conditions
items.quote: IndoStar Capital Finance announced the sale of its wholly owned subsidiary, IndoStar Home Finance Private Limited, to Witkopeend BV, an affiliate of BPEA EQT Mid-Market Growth Partnership, a global private equity investor, for INR1,750 crores on a fully diluted basis.

items.statement: CRISIL upgraded long-term rating to stable from negative while reaffirming CRISIL AA- rating
items.quote: On September 9th, 2024, the long-term rating of IndoStar Capital Finance Limited's facilities and instruments was upgraded by the rating agency CRISIL to stable from negative while reaffirming the rating at CRISIL AA-.

items.statement: Raised INR266 crores through maiden public issue of secured redeemable non-convertible debentures
items.quote: During the last quarter, the company raised INR266 crores through its maiden public issue of secured, redeemable, nonconvertible debentures.

items.statement: CV industry growth to moderate due to high BS-VI vehicle costs and new AC cab rules, used CV demand to remain strong
items.quote: Despite the strong revival of the monsoon in the second phase, we believe the CV growth in the current year will moderate, driven by the high cost of the new BS-VI vehicles, which continues to rise, and with the new air-conditioned driver cab rules coming into force in March next year, we see no respite in the rise of the vehicle cost.

items.statement: Significant investments made in end-to-end digital loan origination system and expanding operations in Tier 3/4 locations
items.quote: Recognizing the increasing importance of technology, we have made significant investments in our end-to-end loan origination system, which is now digitally driven. Additionally, we are also expanding our operations, particularly in Tier 3, Tier 4 locations, with an emphasis addressing the rise in rural demand due to good monsoon.

items.statement: CV disbursement reached INR1,499 crores in Q2 FY25, up 53% YoY; consolidated disbursement INR1,724 crores
items.quote: The commercial vehicle disbursement for Q2 FY'25 reached INR1,499 crores, showing a growth of 53% over the previous year of INR948 crores.

items.statement: Standalone GNPA at 4.97%, net Stage 3 at 2.5%; CV EMI collection efficiency 89%, including overdue 93%
items.quote: Currently, our GNPA stood at -- stands at 4.97% for FY'25 Q2 for the stand-alone entity. We have also launched our new small business loan division with a focus on micro loans against property, particularly targeted at Tier 3, Tier 4.

items.statement: Consolidated NIM at 5.6%; standalone CV disbursement yield improved to 18.5% from 17.5% a year ago
items.quote: During the quarter, our consolidated net income from operations was at about INR 218.5 crores, showing a 14% increase on a quarter-on-quarter basis and showed a net interest margin of about 5.6%.

items.statement: Incremental borrowing cost reduced from 12.7% in Q4 FY22 to 10.1% in Q2 FY25; NCDs issued at 10.3-10.7% coupon
items.quote: Over the last 3 quarters, incrementally funds are being raised at lower levels as the confidence of the bank and the other investors -- other lenders on IndoStar has improved. Our incremental cost has come down from about 12.7% that was there in Q4 FY'22 to 10.1% in Q2 FY'25.

items.statement: Raised INR2,361 crores incremental funding in Q2 including INR1,391 crores from banks; repaid INR1,300 crores debt
items.quote: In terms of funding, we have made substantial progress in improving our liquidity position by improving incremental funding -- raising incremental funding of about INR2,361 crores in the second quarter, including INR1,391 crores which came from bank, either in the form of term loans or working capital demand loan or securitization.

items.statement: Standalone employee count increased from ~3,500 to ~4,000; added senior management and field staff
items.quote: We have actually increased the total number in the standalone from about 3,500-odd to close to 4,000-odd.

items.statement: Targeting INR9,000 crores AUM for FY25 and INR12,000 crores for FY26 company-wide (excluding housing)
items.quote: FY '25, we will end up at around INR9,000 crores overall. And '26, I believe we should end up at around INR12,000 crores company-wise.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained at 2% range for full year FY25 despite Q1/Q2 uptick
items.quote: We had always said that it would be in the 2% range on an overall basis. We'll stick to that and we'll continue to maintain that.

items.statement: Cash and equivalents INR791 crores plus INR512 crores in bank/trust for securitization; total collections INR993 crores in Q2
items.quote: As on 30th September, we maintained a cash and cash equivalent of about INR791 crores. Additionally, about INR512 crores was kept in bank and trust towards securitization deals as security deposits.

items.statement: Capital adequacy 25.9%, debt-equity 2.26x; significant headroom for growth and borrowing
items.quote: Our capital adequacy stood at about 25.9% and the debt equity is at above 2.26x, both of which gives ample idea to anyone who looks at the numbers that there is ample headroom for further growth and for further borrowing.

items.statement: HFC GNPA at 1.41%, 90+ DPD at 1%, 1+ DPD at 3.9% as of September 30, 2024
items.quote: Our gross Stage 3 assets, GNPA, stood at 1.41% as on September 30, 2024.

items.statement: HFC sale proceeds expected March-April next year to be used for core CV and small business lending
items.quote: We expect it sometime in March, April next year. But really our plan is to really use it for the business, for our core business. So the money will be used for our core business which is CV and small businesses.

items.statement: HFC ROA nearly 3% for H1 FY25; capital adequacy 55.7%, debt-to-equity 3.2x
items.quote: Our return on asset as a result stood at nearly 3% for H1 FY25. We maintain a strong capital adequacy of 55.7% and a debt-to-equity ratio of 3.2x.

items.statement: Extended monsoon impacted collections; ECL model captures macro factors including erratic monsoon patterns over 5-year horizon
items.quote: See, in our ECL model the macroeconomic factors like all these has a -- it's a factor. So it gets captured there. And monsoon in India is something which is known for many generations. We all know that during this period, there is going to be an impact. So that gets captured in the ECL model.

items.statement: 99% of CV disbursement in used CV space; Focus4 strategy targeting Tier 3/4, LCV and smaller assets for better yields
items.quote: Notably, 99% of our CV disbursement is in the used CV space, which permits us to get better yields.

items.statement: No co-lending with ICICI Bank since May 2022; focus on growing own balance sheet rather than sourcing for others
items.quote: We were doing co-lending only for CV with ICICI Bank. Typically, it was a sourcing and servicing arrangement. We suspended it in May '22. We are not keen to do that business.

items.statement: RBI Governor warned against 'growth at any cost' approach for NBFCs; tighter bank funding norms impacting NBFC access to funds
items.quote: The RBI Governor, in his address, pointed to the high growth the NBFC sector has witnessed in the last few years and urged caution when he said, I quote, "A growth at any cost approach would be detrimental."

items.statement: Valuation completely outsourced to three Pan-India agencies like Mahindra First Choice; collections in-house, only repossession outsourced
items.quote: Valuation is completely outsourced. It is with Pan-India agencies. We have tie-up with three major agencies who are doing the valuation, like Mahindra First Choice kind of companies who are reputed, who are there Pan-India.

items.statement: HFC disbursement INR261 crores in Q2 FY25; AUM INR2,561 crores, up 13% YTD; customer base 32,500+
items.quote: Despite the lean seasonality, we continued the growth momentum from Q1 to clock INR261 crores disbursement numbers for Q2 FY'25. We are delighted to inform that we've made strong progress across most business matrices. During the quarter 2, with a total disbursements of INR261 crores, our assets under management reached INR2,561 crores, representing a robust growth of 13% on a YTD basis.

items.statement: HFC raised INR495 crores in Q2 mainly through bank term loans and PTCs; cash position INR369 crores
items.quote: On the liability side, we successfully raised INR495 crores during the quarter, majorly through term loans from banks and PTCs. We're also pleased to report a strong liquidity position with INR369 crores of cash on the balance sheet.

items.statement: Revenue target of Rs 200 billion to be achieved in FY25, one year ahead of original FY26 timeline
items.quote: With ₹100 billion of revenue achieved in the first half, we are set to achieve our Project LEAP goal of ₹ 200 billion revenues a year ahead of the targeted FY 26 timeline.

items.statement: Capex guidance of Rs 10-11 billion for FY25, similar run rate expected for FY26 and FY27
items.quote: Furthermore, our capex for Q2 FY 25 stood at ₹ 2.9 billion, accumulating to ₹ 5.7 billion for the first half of the year, in -line with our guidance of doing ₹ 10 billion to ₹11 billion of capex during the year.

items.statement: Wires & Cables EBITDA margin guided range of 12% to 14%
items.quote: It is pertinent to note that in spite of the contraction, the Wires & Cables business continued to generate margin within the guided EBITDA range of 12% to 14%.

items.statement: Strong demand momentum expected to continue in H2 FY25 across Wires & Cables, driven by government spending, real estate, and private capex recovery
items.quote: To summarize the key takeaways, we expect the demand momentum to remain strong in the Wires & Cables business , with second half to be better than the first half.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin at 11.5%, down ~90 bps sequentially due to FMEG A&P spends, employee costs, wire margin compression, and higher institutional mix
items.quote: EBITDA grew by 4% Y -o-Y with EBITDA margin at 11.5%. The sequential decline in EBITDA margins of ~90 bps was on account of 3 reasons: first, decline in FMEG segment margins due to increase in advertising and promotional (A&P) spends relative to the first quarter.

items.statement: RDSS order book at Rs 48 billion as of end-September, to be executed over next 2-3 years
items.quote: So, as of now, as at end of September, the open order book of the RDSS scheme for us was roughly about ₹48 billion. That is something that we have to execute over the course of next 2 to 3 years

items.statement: Cables & wires capacity utilization at 60-70% in Q2 vs 70-75% in Q1 due to new capacity addition and inventory liquidation
items.quote: if you recall, in quarter 1, we had mentioned that we are operating at 70% to 75% of our capacity utilization. This quarter, the utilization rate is somewhere between 60% and 70% because a part of newer investment of capex that we did, the capacity came up fo r us.

items.statement: Wire margin compression in September due to 10-12% copper price spike; competitors cut prices to gain volume despite rising input costs
items.quote: In the last part of the quarter, specifically in September when the prices went up by almost 10% to 12%, the distributors, obviously, they wanted to cash in on this benefit because they wouldn't want to wait until October when the price pass -on would happen

items.statement: Wires grew ~2x cables in Q2; wires volume growth 20-25%, cables early teens; wires value growth ~40%, cables ~20%
items.quote: As far as the volume growth is concerned, in Wires it was between 20% and 25 %, and within Cables, it was in early teens. As far as value growth is concerned, for Wires, it was close to 40%, whereas in Cables, it was about 20-odd percent.

items.statement: Institutional sales grew faster than channel in Q2 due to copper price correction in July; channel sales were almost non-existent in first month
items.quote: in the first month of this quarter because the copper correction was there in the handle of 12% to 15%, the channel sales were almost nonexistent.

items.statement: No heightened competitive intensity in cables; industry capacity additions expected to fall short of demand growth over next 3-5 years
items.quote: we genuinely believe that even the capacities which are being put up right now, those will fall short. So we don't envisage a scenario in which a similar thing plays out in cables, which ha s played out in wires in this quarter.

items.statement: International business grew 36% QoQ to 6.1% of revenue; H2 exports expected to be better than H1; Middle East and Australia key growth geographies
items.quote: The international business registered a 36% quarter -on-quarter increase, resulting into improvement in its contribution to the Company's top-line to 6.1% in this quarter compared to 5.3% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improved to 44 days in Q2 FY25 from previous quarter due to FG inventory clearance and higher payable days
items.quote: our working capital cycle improved to 44 days, facilitated by the clearance of finished goods inventory buil t-up in the Wires & Cables business at the end of the previous quarter and improvement in payable days

items.statement: Net cash position improved to Rs 24.3 billion in Q2 FY25 from Rs 16.4 billion in Q1 FY25
items.quote: our net cash position improved to ₹ 24.3 billion, compared to ₹ 16.4 billion in Q1FY25.

items.statement: Wires & Cables domestic distribution-driven business grew 28% YoY with mid-teen volume growth
items.quote: The domestic distribution -driven business, while slow in the first couple of months, picked up pace during the end of the quarter. Institutional business continued its strong growth momentum on the back of robust demand.

items.statement: BharatNet Phase 3 tenders applied for all 16 packages; optical fiber contribution currently low single digit but could become meaningful over 2-3 years if orders won
items.quote: We have applied for all 16 packages. While, of course, winning it or not is something that we will have to see when the results come out. But as of now, we do have optical fiber manufacturing capacity at our plant.

items.statement: US election outcome unlikely to derail export growth due to diversification across 80 countries and multiple cable types beyond solar
items.quote: irrespective of which candidate comes and what is the focus on, specifically on renewables, there is a lot of investment happening in the other piece s as well. For example, the power transmission and distribution for the U.S. is getting upgraded after almost a century

items.statement: Added manpower to create vertical-wise sales teams in FMEG, increasing employee expenses
items.quote: Over and above that, increase in employee expenses, as we added manpower to create vertical -wise sales team, also negatively impacted the margin s.

items.statement: Next 5-year goals being worked on, to be disclosed by end of current financial year
items.quote: The Company is confident of achieving the ₹ 200 billion top-line goal in the current year itself and is working on its next 5 -year goals, which we intend to disclose by the end of the current financial year.

items.statement: Management expects low double-digit top-line growth of 12%-13% for FY25 and EBITDA margins of 13.2%-13.5% for the year.
items.quote: I think I still expect that we will grow at that number around 12%-13%, I still anticipate that growth is going to be there, because if you see the H1 number, we are already around 11% top line growth . I think the second half should be better than that. I still expect that 12 %-13% is what we will grow.

items.statement: Institutional cleaning business targets Rs. 250 crore revenue for FY25; H1 achieved Rs. 130 crore.
items.quote: If you see for the first half we have done about Rs. 130 crore in the institutional business. Our take-off Rs. 250 crore, which we have said I think we are in line with that.

items.statement: HPPC domestic volumes flat; export focus increased due to limited EO availability and peak ethoxylation capacity.
items.quote: On the domestic front, if you see in the HPPC , I think the FMCG Home Care, the volumes were pretty flat. And with the RM prices coming down , we also had some pressures on softening our prices to pick up some volumes.

items.statement: Textile domestic volumes grew 6-7% YoY but pricing fell 6-7%; exports to Bangladesh and Egypt slowed due to geopolitical and banking issues.
items.quote: In the Textile side the domestic volumes were pretty good . Good in the sense volumes were better than last year. The volume growth was about I think 6 -7%, but we had a pressure on the pricing side and the prices had come down by about 6 -7%.

items.statement: Animal Health Q2 seasonally weak; expects 1.5x normal sales in Q3 vs Q2 and strong H2.
items.quote: Going forward , Quarter 3 and Quarter 4 are traditionally the strong quarters for Animal Health, and we expect like our marketing says 1.5x the normal sales for Quarter 3, via-a-vis Quarter 2 or Quarter 1.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 253 bps YoY on product mix and operational optimization despite higher costs from new verticals.
items.quote: Our gross margins improved by 253 basis points this quarter on the back of our product mix and our efforts to optimize operations. The improvement comes despite higher costs associated with new growth verticals including the institutional cleaning chemical business.

items.statement: EBITDA margin stable at 13.2% YoY; gross margin gains offset by higher freight, employee and professional expenses from global expansion.
items.quote: Our overall EBITDA increased by 3.6% to Rs. 65.9 crore up from Rs. 63.6 crore last year with EBITDA margins of 13.2%, stable despite the additional investment in these emerging segments.

items.statement: Exports grew 32% YoY in H1 FY25 to Rs. 248 crore, now 25% of total sales; Q2 exports Rs. 130 crore, Q1 Rs. 118 crore.
items.quote: Exports for this quarter was about Rs. 130 crore. In Q1 we did Rs. 118 crore and Q2 last year was about Rs. 107 crore. And on H1 basis, our total exports was Rs. 248 crore vis-à-vis Rs. 187 crore last year H1.

items.statement: Board approved additional Rs. 18.25 crore capex, raising total project budget to Rs. 146.25 crore for Unitop and Dahej; Rs. 60-65 crore spent so far, similar amount over next 6 months.
items.quote: In the unit of CAPEX, the Board has approved additional investment of Rs. 18.25 crore enhancing the budget of the project to up to Rs. 146.25 crore. The additional budget is required on account of some design modifications , which were necessary to meet the revised project specifications and structural integrity.

items.statement: Loop reactors at Dahej expected functional by end-November/early December; Reliance to supply additional EO from Q4 start.
items.quote: The loop reactors will become functional by I think end November or early December. Then again the ethoxylation capacity will not be an issue.

items.statement: New capacity at Unitop and Dahej expected to deliver asset turns of 3-4x.
items.quote: Both the projects are being executed efficiently on ground and are expected to deliver asset terms of 3 to 4x.

items.statement: Rossari Global DMCC established Rossari Biotech Trading FZE in JAFZA, UAE for export distribution; agreed to acquire 100% of Unistar Thai Company Limited for specialty chemicals manufacturing.
items.quote: Global DMCC , a wholly -owned subsidiary, has established Rossari Biotech Trading FZE in the Jebel Ali Free Zone (JAFZA), UAE . This new entity will focus on trading activities, managing the distribution and sales of chemicals and consumer products for export market s, further enhancing our international presence. Additionally, Rossari Global DMCC has agreed to acquire 100% of the equity share cap

items.statement: Acquired 39,101 sqm land plot adjacent to Dahej facility for future expansion.
items.quote: Furthermore, we have acquired a 39,101 square meter plot of land adjacent to our Dahej facility, earmarked for future expansion and the development of our manufacturing capabilities.

items.statement: Freight costs surged unprecedentedly in last 6 months, borne by company for new export customers; plan to pass through over time.
items.quote: The freights have actually gone up a little unprecedented in the last 6 months. That's actually hitting us. But I think slowly we will be able to push most of these freight expenses back to the customers.

items.statement: Domestic pricing pressure from RM cost declines (acetic acid, butyl acrylate, styrene, silicones) led to finished goods price softening.
items.quote: However, since you know that the prices of certain raw materials dropped like acetic acid, butyl acrylate, styrene or silicones because of which there was pressure on the finished goods product pricing and that is where you see a loss in revenue basically.

items.statement: Key export sectors: home care, personal care, cosmetics, agro; key geographies: Europe, South America, Middle East, Turkey, Vietnam, North Africa, Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Philippines.
items.quote: Sectors, I think, majorly home care, personal care, cosmetics and also on the agro side, these are the key sectors in HPPC and the key geographies I think continue to be Europe, South America. We are also now exploring some countries in the Middle East and Turkey is one of them.

items.statement: Net working capital days stable vs March 2024; inventory up strategically, receivables declining; Bangladesh collections sticky but improving.

items.statement: Receivable cycle higher in H1 due to agro season; expected to improve by March.
items.quote: I think the first half is generally higher given that we just passed the agro season where the payment stretches a little longer, probably towards the end of the year by March I think it should be much better than what we are as of September.

items.statement: Appointed Mr. Gurudas Aras as Additional Non-Executive Independent Director effective Oct 19, 2024; 40+ years textile experience including robotics and automation.

With over 40 years of experience in the Textile industry, Mr. Aras brings a wealth of knowledge, including expertise in advising on robotics and automation.

items.statement: Institutional cleaning revenue Rs. 70-73 crore in Q2; H1 Rs. 130 crore.
items.quote: Institutional sales during this quarter is about Rs. 70 – Rs. 73 crore, around that number.

items.statement: Ethoxylates/Propoxylates constitute 60-70% of HPPC revenue.
items.quote: Ethoxylates is the major chemistry for us, surfactant, everything linked to surfactant. 70% of HPPC is all EO-based products.

items.statement: Bangladesh banking/LC issues caused voluntary export halt for 2 months; collections still sticky but expected to improve by December.
items.quote: In Bangladesh, in fact, in the last two months, the off-take was very, very less. While there were orders but given the conditions that were there and the LCs, et cetera, not coming through, a lot of the banking issues cropped up.

items.statement: Propylene oxide (PO) supply challenges due to import dependence and storage constraints at current consumption scale.
items.quote: Yes, if you do not plan well enough and there are some storage issues also because we are not a very large consumer of propoxylates, I mean propylene oxide. There are some challenges, but once we become large enough, probably then we can have some storage at the ports.

items.statement: Sustainability initiatives: 5 KWP solar capacity installed, water consumption reduced by 12,142.5 KL, 18,505 KL treated/disposed, 1,500 trees planted, 3R waste management policy.
items.quote: We have installed 5 KWP of solar energy capacity at our plants, reduced water consumption by 12,142.5 KL and responsibly treated and disposed 18,505 KL of water. Additionally, we have planted 1,500 trees around our facilities to promote biodiversity.
