items.statement: Portfolio composition stable: 57.2% home loan, 10% LAP, 19.6% LRD, 11.7% developer finance, 1.7% others
items.quote: In terms of a portfolio composition, it remains by and large stable with 57.2% as a home loan and close to 10% as loan against property, 19.6% lease rental discounting, 11.7% developer finance, and 1.7% other by and large in the same range, which had been there.

items.statement: Gross spread stable at 1.9% QoQ, down from 2.3% YoY; NIM improved to 4.1% from 3.9% QoQ
items.quote: On the gross spread basis, on a Q2 FY '25, we had 1.9% gross spread, which was stable from the last quarter, which was a Q1, 1.9%. Of course, on a year on year basis, the gross spread was 2.3% in Q2 FY '24. NIM at 4.1% in Q2 improved marginally from Q1, which was at 3.9%.

items.statement: Cost of funds increased 5 bps QoQ to 7.92% and 28 bps YoY; borrowing mix 44% bank, 45% money market, 11% NHB
items.quote: Cost of funds came in at 7.92%, which was five b ps higher than Q1 FY '25 at 7.87 %, and year on year, 28 bps increase, which has been there. Borrowing mix, largely 44% : 45%: 11%. 44% to the bank, 45% on the money market, and National Housing Bank at 11% has been the mix.

items.statement: GNPA 29 bps, NNPA 12 bps; credit cost 2 bps due to overlay release, normalized 14-16 bps
items.quote: GNPA and NNPAs already called out. Loan loss to average loan assets, 0. 02% as of 30th November. However, net of overlay release credit cost is 14 bps.

items.statement: Stage 1 assets stable at 99.21-99.39% over last 6 quarters; Stage 2 declined from 0.57% to 0.32% YoY
items.quote: Stage 1 assets remaining by and large stable, 99.21% from Q4 FY'23 to 99.39%, 99.37%, 99.35%, a stable range over last six quarters. Stage 2 assets coming down from a year -on-year perspective from Q4 FY'23 from 0.57 % to 0.32%.

items.statement: PCR on Stage 3 assets range-bound at 57-59%; Stage 1 provisioning varies by product mix
items.quote: Provisioning coverage ratios, PCR on Stage 3 assets, remains range bound on 57%, 58%, 59%. GNPA, NNPA numbers we have spoken about.

items.statement: ROA stable at 2.5% in Q2 FY25 vs 2.6% YoY; ROE declined to 13% from 16% due to capital raise
items.quote: On a RO A, 2.5% in Q2 FY '25, nearly same ROA of 2.6% in Q2 FY '24. ROE, given the capital raise in this number, coming down at 13% in Q2 FY '25 versus 16% in Q2 FY '24.

items.statement: IPO proceeds INR 3,560 crores, INR 1,500 crores unutilized as of Sep 30, expected deployment in Oct 24
items.quote: Completed IPO process, got listed on 16th September. As of 30th September, out of IPO proceeds of INR 3,560 crores, what was for the company's primary raise, INR 1,500 crores was yet to be deployed and they remained in the monitoring account. It's expected to be utilized during October 24.

items.statement: Credit cost normalized corridor 14-17 bps; overlay reduced to INR 10 crores remaining
items.quote: Remaining overlay is only INR10 crores, so 14 bps to 17 bps is the buy and large the credit cost corridor if you look at last four -five quarter normalizing overlay release.

items.statement: Retail disbursements expected to pick up as affordable/near-prime segment scales; no major changes seen
items.quote: We are not seeing any major changes in the disbursements as we go forward. In fact, our view is that we should be as our SBU of a near prime and affordable is kicking in, we should see a growth picking up a bit towards in the retail segment.

items.statement: On-role employees down 252 in H1 FY25; contractual staff up 700, net increase ~400-450 total deployed
items.quote: So, the reduction in the on-role employees, if I have to call out in last six months, would be close to 252 because of normal attrition and all new roles which get created or get refilled or gets created on the contractual side, while on the contractual s ide increase would be 700. So net increase of close to 400 450.

items.statement: Home loans pure term loans; Flexi only in LAP/LRD top-ups; LRD average ticket ~INR 103 crores, developer finance ~INR 17 crores/project
items.quote: In home loan as a regulatory construct, you cannot do Flexi, because if the customer pays back to you, then it gets to be classified as a non-home loan. Only in few of the loans, if it is a balanced transfer and you are opting for a top -up, in a top-up, it can be offered as a OD piece.

items.statement: 451 unique developer relationships for 693 projects in developer finance; 264 unique LRD relationships
items.quote: Generally, lease rental discounting and developer book is not much of over 20, panel number 26 which gives the active developer relationships of 451. So 693 projects represented by 451 developers.

items.statement: Indicative yields: home loan 8.8-9.2%, LAP 10-10.5%, LRD 8.5-9%, developer finance 11.5-13%
items.quote: I'm sorry I cannot share this data, but broadly, I can say on the yield would be in the home loan, between close to 8.8% to 9.2%, on loan against property between 10% to 10.5%, broad, on lease rental discounting between 8.5% to 9%. That's what, and the developer finance between 11.5% to 12.5% or 13%.

items.statement: No cap on LRD growth; regulatory cap at 60%+ residential assets limits non-residential to ~37-38%
items.quote: So, there is no cap we have as far as we look at from a lease rental discounting, but there is a different kind of a cap which comes for us because as a regulatory norm, 60% plus of our total assets, which means close to 62% to 63% of our loan assets have to be in the residential space.

items.statement: Developer finance mix not to exceed ~15% of AUM; primarily a funnel for home loans
items.quote: Our internal view as of today would not to exceed 15 odd percent kind of a mix in this business as we even go forward. That is what I repeat to all.

items.statement: Portfolio attrition stable in retail; construction finance drives volatility due to pre-agreed sweep ratios
items.quote: The attrition rates in the retail side are by and large stable. The plus and minus of the attrition rate, what we have seen would be driven by in the construction finance portfolio at some point of a time, if the sweeps are in a quarter, if the attrition is lower, the attrition overall might, you may calculate in a reverse way.

items.statement: Participated in PMAY CLSS previously; will mobilize under new PMAY guidelines but current mix significantly above eligibility threshold
items.quote: So last time also when the PMAY CLSS -Credit Linked Subsidy scheme was there, we were a participant. We may not have been a very large participant because by definition, our larger amount of our customers are above the 25 lakh loan criteria, what are there. But all government schemes, we participate heartily and we try to mobilize as much as possible.

items.statement: LRD provisioning 0.61% on Stage 1 despite zero Stage 2/3; developer finance 0.62%; tested 1000+ projects with only 4 issues historically
items.quote: In lease rental discounting at a INR14,000 crores book, the provisioning in the stage one is INR85 crores, which is from a historic point of view, since we do not never had any stage two or a stage three asset, I think 0.61% kind of a ECL provisioning is significantly higher provisioning than whatever ECL models do that.

items.statement: ROA trajectory stable 2.3-2.6% over last 2-3 years excluding FY23; leverage target 8x sustainable
items.quote: I think that ROAs had been in the range of between 2.3% to 2.5% by and large over the various – if I exclude FY23, it is largely in the stable range of between 2.3 % to 2.5%, 2.6% ranging between in a quarter going up or going down slightly a bit.

items.statement: Prime home loan competition remains intense but unchanged for 6-7 years; no change in competitive stance or appetite
items.quote: Competition in the home loan, in the prime home loan remains very intense, which all of us remain. But that had been the status from last six seven years, ever since we started the business and expected to remain intense. We don't see any change in the competitive stance or our competitive stance or our appetite to grow or our ability to grow.

name: CG Power and Industrial Solutions Ltd

items.statement: Net margin impact of surrender regulations estimated at 100-200 bps on run-rate basis, majority to be mitigated over next few quarters
items.quote: As guided earlier, we anticipate a net margin impact on a run rate basis, full year run rate basis of between 100 and 200 basis points. Majority of it, I believe, will be mitigated in the medium term, medium term defined as over the next few quarters.

items.statement: Individual adjusted FYP grew 34% YoY in Q2 FY25, outperforming private sector (24%) and industry (21%); H1 APE grew 31%
items.quote: In the second quarter of FY '25, our individual adjusted first year premium exhibited a very strong growth of 34% outperforming both the private sector and overall industry growth rates of 24% and 21% respectively.

items.statement: VNB grew 23% in Q2 with NBM 23.6%; H1 VNB grew 16% to Rs 766 crore with NBM 21.2%
items.quote: All our efforts in distribution expansion along with product innovation resulted in a significant increase of 23% in our VNB for Q2 with an NBM of 23.6%. And with that, our first half VNB growth is now 16%.

items.statement: Q2 NBM 23.6% vs Q1 17.5%; 600 bps QoQ improvement driven 500 bps by operating leverage and 100 bps by rider attachment
items.quote: From quarter 1 to Quarter 2 walk, the 600-basis point improvement that you see, 500 basis point of that comes out of operating leverage and also strong volume growth that we have continued experience in the quarter. And around 100 basis point is a mix of the riders which we have been successfully able to actually attach across our product forms.

items.statement: ULIP share rose to 47% of APE in Q2 from 35% a year ago; retail protection grew 49%; rider attachment ratio reached 45% in H1 vs 31%
items.quote: With the same objective in Quarter 2, we introduced a Nifty 500 Momentum Fund predominantly for e-commerce customers, a move to leverage opportunities in the current equity market. This led to 74% growth in the ULIP segment at company level, with the ULIP share in our product mix increasing from 35% total APE last year to 47% in Quarter 2 FY '25.

items.statement: Annuity APE: retail Rs 173 crore, group Rs 12 crore in H1; retail grew 18%, group declined 60% due to one large deal last year
items.value: Rs 173 crore retail, Rs 12 crore group
items.quote: So, around 173 is retail and 12 odd crore is group annuities for Super annuation annuities, on APE basis. This is APE, right?

items.statement: Proprietary channels grew 45% in Q2 and 51% in H1; e-commerce share rose to 15% from 9%; agency ~22%, CAT ~9%
items.quote: The agency has at an overall level contributed around 21%, 22% last year. It has a similar level this year as well. The CAT channel also contributed around 9% last year. It is at similar levels this year as well. And the e-commerce contribution is actually up from 9%. It has moved to 15%.

items.statement: 20 new partners onboarded in Q2 including India Post Payments Bank, 10 GCL partners, 5 brokers, 3 corporate agents; partnership channels grew 22% in Q2
items.quote: Further, in our ongoing efforts to broaden distribution , we have successfully onboarded 20 new partners during Quarter 2 FY '25 including two banks, Indian Post Payment Bank is one of them, 10 GCL partners, 5 online and offline brokers and 3 corporate agents.

items.statement: New business strain increased due to higher sales in protection, group credit life, and ULIPs which have intrinsically higher strain than participating products
items.quote: The reason for the strain increase, one obviously is higher sales in protection, group credit life, and ULIPs which actually intrinsically have higher NB strain. And that's largely the reason why the strain has grown.

items.statement: Brand name change requires ROC and IRDAI approvals; no RBI approval needed; targeting launch within next quarter (~45 days)
items.quote: As far as the approval of branding is concerned, as you know, we need to go to ROC, followed by an approval from IRDAI for the name change. Those are two approvals which are required. We don't require any approval from RBI. So, hopefully, the turnaround time to do that will be close to 45 days.

items.statement: 13th month persistency at 87% (up 309 bps); 61st month persistency at 58%; NPS rose 5 points to 61
items.quote: We maintain our leadership in 13th month persistency for number of policies, with our regular and limited premium for extensive reaching its highest ever level at 87% up 309 basis points, while our 61st month persistency stood at 58 for the period ending September 2024.

items.statement: Operating RoEV 16.8% annualized; total RoEV 24.2% excluding capital infusion; positive operating variance Rs 9 crore from mortality experience
items.quote: The annualized total return on EV, first half FY '25, excluding the capital infusion of Rs. 1,612 crore is 24.2%, and the annualized operating RoEV stands at 16.8%. In the annualized operating RoEV, there has been a positive operating variance of Rs. 9 crore.

items.statement: Non-PAR pricing adjusted at various points in response to yield curve movements; competitive intensity considered in rate decisions
items.quote: The non-PAR pricing has been adjusted at various points in time, though the movement in the last month has been a bit sharper. But keeping an overall view of competitive intensity and competitive actions, we will also continue to take those calls with respect to adjusting our non-PAR rates for the customers as well.

items.statement: Generative AI co-pilot launched for 4,000 frontline sales personnel and supervisors in Q2 for real-time query and objection handling
items.quote: We also launched a generative AI-based co-pilot for our 4,000 frontline sales personnel and supervisors in Quarter 2 to assist with real-time sales query and objection handling.

items.statement: Structure simplification process ongoing, no timeline visibility; expected to take next few quarters
items.quote: I think the moment we have visibility to timelines, we will come back to you. It is going to be a time-consuming process, and I think we will make an attempt to do that over the next few quarters is the way I will put it.

items.quote: It's generally 10% conversion rates is what we observe. Prashant Tripathy: And it varies by channels also. items.statement: Economic variance: two-thirds from equity gains, one-third from debt gains
items.quote: Last question you asked was on the economic variance. What proportion? Two-third of that is attributable to equity gains and one-third to the debt gains.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 gross margin target of 50%
items.quote: I mentioned that Quarter 4 gross margin should be 50%.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin target of 12%
items.quote: EBITDA margin of 12% for the Quarter 4.

items.statement: H2 FY25 volume-value growth gap to narrow to 8-10%
items.quote: In case of second half, I am confident that our volume growth and value growth difference should not be 18% but it should be between 8% to 10%.

items.statement: FY26 full year gross margin target of 55%
items.quote: FY26, yes full year quite possible.

items.statement: Debt reduction target of Rs 100 crore by March 2025
items.quote: What we said is Rs. 100 crore given by reduction in by March '25 a minimum reduction what we aim for in the overall debt.

items.statement: BCG project to deliver Rs 40-50 crore P&L benefit in FY25
items.quote: Rs. 40 to Rs. 50 crore of the initiatives will come into P&L this year, and more of it in Quarter 4.

items.statement: Festival and wedding season demand strong in Q3 and part of Q4
items.quote: If I have to talk about demand indicators, it looks fine with festival around and als o upcoming wedding date which also looks to be very strong in Quarter 3 and a part in Quarter 4

items.statement: Gross margin fell 1000 bps YoY due to brand and channel mix, soft luggage liquidation, lower Bangladesh production
items.quote: If you look at gross margin, this is where the major pressure was seen. However, sequentially it grew by 80 bps, but if you look at year-on-year, there is a dip of 1000 basis point, mainly on account of brand mix and channel mix, also coupled with soft luggage inventory reduction and lower production at Bangladesh.

items.statement: Sequential gross margin improvement of 80 bps in Q2 FY25
items.quote: However, sequentially it grew by 80 bps, but if you look at year-on-year, there is a dip of 1000 basis point, mainly on account of brand mix and channel mix, also coupled with soft luggage inventory reduction and lower production at Bangladesh.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to reach 3-4% in Q3 FY25 and jump significantly in Q4 FY25
items.quote: As we speak it's a journey in progress so probably from the 0% of EBITDA margin we will move around 3%, to 4% near Quarter 3, and you find a significant jump getting into the Quarter 4, because by then my most of the initiatives will start giving the results out of it.

items.statement: Market share among three organized players improved from 36% to 40% over two quarters
items.quote: Our market share has improved so, two quarters ago, our market share between three organized players had reached 36%, today it stands at 40% and for this quarter, we are yet to get the numbers, but I am quite confident that even this quarter, we will gain some market share.

items.statement: Bangladesh factory now running full-fledged and will show profits from Q3 FY25
items.quote: Bangladesh factory is now running full fledge and from Quarter 3 onward, it will also start showing profits.

items.statement: Bangladesh capacity reduced, no wage cost increase expected
items.quote: No, so we have reduced our capacities already there. In fact, we want, at this point of time, a little bit reduction only. It won't increase from where it is today.

items.statement: Aggressive e-commerce pricing by portals during Big Billion Day and GOAT sale hurt offline channel
items.quote: Overall revenue growth for the quarter was muted, mainly due to low uptake from the traditional channels, due to aggressive pricing by e-commerce during Big Billion Day and GOAT

items.statement: Implementing pricing guardrails for VIP and Skybag on online portals to prevent discounting below MOP
items.quote: It will be a pricing guardrail for VIP and Skybag, which is our premium brand. They cannot sell below a particular MOP, a similar thing which had happened some three, four years back in the mobile industry, that's where we are heading towards, and we are already in talks with them to give this to us in writing before they sell going forward.

items.statement: Hard luggage contributes over 60% of revenue and is fastest growing category
items.quote: Hard luggage again continued to be the fastest growing category contributing to over 60% of the organization overall revenue.

items.statement: Premium portfolio target increased from 54% to 60% over next 3-4 quarters
items.quote: Secondly, we definitely are looking at increasing our premium portfolio which is today around 54%, my aim will be to reach 60% over next three to four quarters, and that is where the profits will have a meaningful swing.

items.statement: Offline channel under pressure; e-commerce grew 54%, institutional grew 40%+ in Q2 FY25
items.quote: If you have to talk about channel wise performance, e-commerce continued to do a good performance at 54% growth. Offline channel, as I said was under pressure. Institution again, showed a 40% plus growth for Quarter 2 and similar for H1 as well.

items.statement: D2C players with funding burning cash creating pricing pressure in hard luggage
items.quote: However, in the other area which is hard luggage also there is a pricing pressure which is we are reacting to multiple things, it's not only one thing, but see there are lot of D2C players which are coming into the market, and starting to sell, now all these players have enough money to burn, which we don't have, so that's where we are little bit playing on the pricing.

items.statement: Inventory reduced by Rs 174 crore in H1 FY25; one more quarter to reach normal holding cost levels
items.quote: One more quarter to get to the normal level.

items.statement: Slow-moving soft luggage inventory at Rs 180 crore; 7-8 lakh units remaining
items.quote: Current quantum would be somewhere in the range of Rs. 180 odd crore.

items.statement: Debt at Rs 580 crore as of March 2024; Rs 35 crore already reduced, targeting Rs 100 crore reduction by March 2025
items.quote: Rs. 580 crore we had a debt as on March '24. What we said is Rs. 100 crore given by reduction in by March '25 a minimum reduction what we aim for in the overall debt.

items.statement: Interest cost to reduce 10-12% in Q4 FY25 vs current levels
items.quote: In Quarter 4, you may find a reduction of almost 10% to 12% than what you are seeing today in the overall value.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 volume growth 18% (4.4 million units) vs flat value growth
items.quote: Volume growth stands at 18% for the quar ter, and for H1 it is at 14.4

items.statement: E-commerce volume grew 73% in Q2 FY25 while modern trade volume declined 8%
items.quote: On a volume side, the MT actually has seen a de-growth of 8% on volume and e-commerce on a volume front has shown a growth of 73% for the Quarter 2.

items.statement: Bangladesh insurance claim settlement expected over 8-12 months; Rs 5 crore expected in Q3 FY25
items.quote: We know the political scenario of Bangladesh, so I don't want to say that give me everything at once. I may not get this also so today.

items.statement: BCG transformation project 15 months, 3 waves completed, Rs 250 crore bottom-line benefit target
items.quote: BCG project is a 15 months project, it is divided into five waves, three months wave each, two waves are over, we are in the third wave. Whatever work we have done in the first two wave, the result will start from October and then additional third wave, fourth wave, fifth wave. Overall, it's a Rs. 250 crore benefit to the bottom line project and we are on track.

items.statement: Management maintains long-term EBITDA margin target of 7-8% and does not promise 9-9.5% range
items.quote: We have always maintained that , we are aiming to keep our EBITDA in the range of 7% to 8%. And that's our long -term outlook and this is something that we have maintained.

items.statement: Milk volume growth target 5-6% for near future; VAP volume growth target mid-teens
items.quote: Our objective will be to keep it at this level, 5 to 6 percentage range, for the near future.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 8.16% vs 4.6% YoY; H1 FY25 EBITDA margin 8.63% vs 4.3% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA the quarter was INR83 crore, representing a 77% year -on-year growth with EBITDA margins at 8.16%.

items.statement: Employee cost increased to INR75 crore in Q2 FY25 from INR59 crore YoY due to variable pay and new hires
items.quote: Actually, as compared to Q2 to Q4, there is actually around INR55 crores of employee cost last year, INR59 crores. Now it has gone up to INR75 crores because the profitability has gone up by more than 100%.

items.statement: Underlying demand strong; VAP growth impacted 3-4% by adverse weather (60% higher rainfall) affecting curd, drinkables, ice cream
items.quote: In fact, in the first half of the year, we have seen roughly around 60 percentage increase in rainfall in absolute millimeters of rainfall. And you must have read about this in all news articles. and rainfall impacts at least 3 of our value -added product categories, which is primarily curd, drinkables and ice creams.

items.statement: Milk sales volume grew 5.11% YoY to 1.19 million liters/day in Q2; VAP revenue grew 16% YoY to INR298 crore, contribution 30% vs 27%
items.quote: Milk sales volume continued its steady growth in Q2, increasing by 5.11% year -on-year to 1.19 million liters per day.

items.statement: Heritage Nutrivet (feed) revenue grew 18% YoY to INR86 crore in H1; PAT up 117% to INR4 crore
items.quote: Heritage Nutrivet Limited, the wholly owned subsidiary, experienced robust top line growth of 18% year-on-year, reaching INR86 crores during H1 with a healthy 117% increase in PAT totaling to INR4 crores.

items.statement: Investing INR200+ crore in new greenfield ice cream plant expected to commission by end of 2025
items.quote: We are anyway looking at capturing all possible opportunities, which is why we have gone ahead with the capital investment of INR200-plus crores in this particular category. So we are going to set up an ice cream plant which will come up roughly around the same time next year, maybe towards the end of 2025 we'll see that.

items.statement: Investing in human assets (feet on street), marketing assets (0.8-0.9% of revenue), and capital assets for VAP and procurement capacity
items.quote: at this point in time on 3 things as we continue to drive growth in the long term, right? Because that's the single -minded objective -- long-term profitable growth is a single -minded objective that we are working with. The 3 things are: number one, we are investing in human assets. So we are increasing the quality of people. We are increasing feet on street, which will keep our growth momentum t

items.statement: No pricing or grammage actions taken in Q2; revenue per liter flat for last 5 quarters
items.quote: The last 5 quarters, our prices are stabilized, and we have not increased prices. Here and there, that might happen. But overall, our revenue per liter is same, flat.

items.statement: Feed raw materials: BRB, maize, molasses, rice DDGS, rapeseed; strategic purchasing at low prices to improve profitability
items.quote: So feed business, critical raw materials are like BRB, maize, molasses, rice TDGS, rapeseed, these are the critical raw materials. And we keep some of the raw materials do the strategic purchase. We buy at the right time when the prices are extremely low and we stock it in our warehouses. So we gain some advantage because of that. and that helps in improving our profitability.

items.statement: VAP contribution rose to 30% of revenue in Q2 from 27% YoY; sweets growing ~40% YoY in Q2
items.quote: VAP contribution to total revenue rose to 30% compared to 27% in Q2 of FY '24.

items.statement: Curd volume growing ~11% YoY; ice cream identified as category with huge headroom (low per capita consumption)
items.quote: We are growing curd at around 11%.

items.statement: Launched in Kolkata and South Bengal in August; expanding distribution; e-commerce/modern trade ~15-16% of sales
items.quote: We launched in Bengal in the -- not Bengal, Kolkata, you could say, and Southern part of Bengal in August. So it's been 2 months. We have appointed a certain number of distributors and we are expanding distribution.

items.statement: HUL restructuring ice cream business (not exiting); Heritage sees opportunity and investing INR200+ crore in new plant
items.quote: First of all, I'm not sure if Unilever said that they're exiting the ice cream. They said they are restructuring the business is my understanding, which could be probably in the way the company is structured. Yes, ice cream, is a last player. I believe they are the #2 player in India. And I think their business will continue is my understanding.

items.statement: Bulk fat sales dropped to INR26 crore in Q2 from INR72 crore YoY; consumer fat business growing 50%+ reducing bulk liquidation
items.quote: INR26 crores is the revenue from bulk fat in this quarter.

items.statement: Provision for fat losses nearly exhausted; only INR1-1.5 crore remaining from last year's provision
items.quote: I think almost except INR1 crores, or INR1.5 crores everything has been taken.

items.statement: Cow milk procurement ratio 83% in H1, 85% in Q3; higher cow milk reduces surplus butter/bulk fat
items.quote: We are actually procurement of our cow milk contribution is going is up. Yes so it is about -- currently, it is about -- Q3 is about 85%. H1, it is 83% cow milk ratio.

items.statement: Weather risk: 60% higher rainfall in H1 impacted curd, drinkables, ice cream; may cause air pockets in growth
items.quote: We might hit air pocket in the middle sometime due to weather because -- at least 3 of our value -added product categories are weather-dependent, curd drinkables, primarily, whether it is butter milk, flavored milk and all, milk shakes and ice creams. If it continuously rains and if there is flood and all of that, we might have a little bit of a slowdown in growth rate.

items.statement: Q2 PAT loss on fat business INR7.5-8 crore (roughly equal bulk and consumer); overall profitability up 117% YoY due to lower milk prices and reduced bulk fat sales
items.quote: It is about INR7.5 crores to INR8 crores, yes. That's right.

items.statement: Peak revenue potential at current pricing is Rs 1,700-1,900 crore
items.quote: Currently, we are at a run rate as you can see from our financials, we finished the H1 at almost 700 crores. So, we are at a rate of about 1400 crores. And we think this, at the current prices and so on we could, Sachin we could add another 300, 400 crores, 1700, 1800 crores?

items.statement: No major growth capex planned for FY25; focus on R&D building, maintenance, debottlenecking, and evaluating SB latex expansion
items.quote: There is no CAPEX, no major growth CAPEX plan for this year. There is going to be capital expenditure, but we are focusing more on the future so we are building a new R&D building for example, it won't be that much, but obviously that's one CAPEX that we are looking forward to, and then it is going to be more maintenance CAPEX and debottlenecking CAPEX, some small projects here and there.

items.statement: Board approved in-principle investment in solar and wind over next 1-2 years targeting 60-70% renewable power consumption
items.quote: We will start the project in the next three to six months, over the next one to two years, to invest in solar and wind with the objective obviously, one is savings, but the other is also we expect that our power consumption would be anywhere between 60% to 70% renewable, and our target is there within the next two to three years around 60% power consumption to be through renewable sources, which t

items.statement: Nitrile latex capacity utilization at ~60%; SB latex capacity sufficient for 1.5 years; evaluating expansion at Taloja, Valia, or third location
items.quote: The margins will remain low, capacity utilization currently is about 60% odd, approx. (+/- 60%).

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 7.83% (down from prior year); H1 FY25 EBITDA margin 8.60%; ocean freight impact ~0.75-1% on margins
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was Rs.28 crore, which declined by approximately 13% on year-on-year basis. The EBITDA margin stood at 7.83%

items.statement: Nitrile latex EBITDA slightly negative (0 to -1%) but positive gross contribution; breaking even at ~60% utilization
items.quote: It's a little bit negative EBITDA, but positive on the overall gross contribution.

items.statement: SB latex margins lower by ~15-20% in H1 FY25 vs H1 FY24 due to carpet and paper pressure
items.quote: My guess is about 15%, 20% lower.

items.statement: Butadiene prices in Asia 25-30% higher than Europe; expected to correct in H2; butadiene ~30-40% of total raw material cost
items.quote: As far as Europe and Asia is concerned, it continues to be, Asia prices continue to be maybe 25% higher, 25% to 30% higher than Europe. Things are expected to turn but last six months we have seen this is the situation, but from all analyst reports.

items.statement: Acrylonitrile and styrene prices up slightly QoQ and significantly YoY; unable to fully pass on cost increases due to weak paper and carpet demand
items.quote: They have all gone up a little bit compared to Q1 and certainly this first half has been a lot higher than the first half of last year. Quarter-on-quarter also, there's been a slight increase, on average.

items.statement: Q2 FY25: highest ever quarterly volume (+12% YoY) and export volume (+31% YoY); H1 FY25 volume +13% YoY, export volume +22% YoY
items.quote: In Q2 FY25 we witnessed highest ever quarterly volume and export volume, which grew by 12% and 31% year-on-year basis respectively.

items.statement: Paper industry facing demand weakness and dumping from China; pressure expected to continue in Q3
items.quote: And that looks like it's at least, I can't speak for H2, but at least in the next, in Q3 that we expect the challenge to continue.

items.statement: Glove industry in Southeast Asia now profitable after losses last year; US anti-dumping duty on Chinese gloves (50% from Jan 25, 100% from Jan 26) may improve supply-demand for latex in Southeast Asia
items.quote: The glove industry is definitely doing much better than they were last year in Southeast Asia. They were making losses last year let me put it that way, they were making losses till last year at least they are now in the green.

items.statement: Export revenue surged 48% YoY in Q2; exports 32% of H1 sales by value; SB latex export value grew 16-17% YoY in H1
items.quote: Subsequently, we also achieved the highest quarterly revenue driven by increased volume and product mix with export revenue surging by 48% on year-on-year.

items.statement: Revenue growth driven by volume and product mix; higher realization products include NBR, vinyl pyridine latex for tire cords (+30-40% vs SB latex), and construction specialties (+15-20%)
items.quote: So, NBR for example, NBR we have grown reasonably well in this quarter compared to Q2 of last year or first half compared to last year. So, NBR being a solid rubber product the pricing is higher. I am just talking about revenue and not margins. Then tire cords for example, latex for tire cords, we make a latex called vinyl pyridine latex for the tire cord industry. There the pricing compared to SB

items.statement: NBR facing dumping from Korea (China slowdown) and Russia (sanctions); anti-dumping case initiated, final findings in 8-12 months; NBR expansion on hold pending outcome
items.quote: So, the case has just been initiated. Of course, we have been working at it for the last few months providing all the data. So, the initiation is also an important part of the step, which means it's prima facie they feel that we do have some sort of case, and therefore they have accepted and decided to go ahead with the investigation. From what I am told, the investigation takes about nine months

items.statement: Nitrile latex margins pressured by overcapacity from China, Malaysia, and new entrants; US anti-dumping duty on Chinese gloves may help Southeast Asian supply-demand
items.quote: The other small silver lining we will have to see how it plays out, as the US has recently imposed a 50% anti-dumping duty on gloves from China. So, pre-COVID, China was hardly 5%, 7% market share. Now they are up to 25% market share for gloves. And so they have created gloves and latex capacity to that extent very quickly. Now this anti-dumping duty from the US, which is the largest market, maybe

items.statement: Ocean freight rates on key export routes (India-Turkey, Egypt, UAE) 6-10x higher YoY in Q2; corrected ~20% in October but still 6-7x higher than year ago
items.quote: Routes that used to be $500 now in Q2 were at $3,500, $4,000 per container just to give you an example, now they have come down to $2000, $2,500.

items.statement: Power cost reduced by shifting Gujarat plant from captive co-generation to grid power
items.quote: We have moved on to grid because the power cost is much more lower than generating the power. So, that has supported us in reducing the power cost.

items.statement: Other expenses down 5% YoY despite volume growth due to power mix change and controlled discretionary spend (repairs, maintenance, printing)
items.quote: So, the power mix cost has come down in our case. So, that is helping us to also reduce the cost. Major of the cost which is power and fuel has come down compared to what it was in the last H1, so that has supported us.

items.statement: Debt ~Rs 200-220 crore (long + short term) vs Rs 120 crore liquid investments as of 30 Sep 2024; conservative balance sheet
items.quote: Today we have, as on 30th September, we have probably around 210 crores or so. Sachin, correct me, if I am wrong, but about 200 to 220 crores of debt, all including long term and short term debt. Against that, we have about 120 crores of liquid investment.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty case on NBR initiated; investigation expected to take 8-12 months; industry re-applied after 2020 DGTR recommendation not notified by Finance Ministry
items.quote: We had earlier in 2020 DGTR had recommended a duty, but the finance ministry had not approved it or not notified it. So, we had gone into the courts, along with many others who were in the same boat. But now the strategy has changed, and the entire industry has decided to reapply. And now there is a good understanding with the finance ministry as well.

items.statement: Current environment most challenging in 4 years due to combined headwinds: ocean freight, nitrile latex overcapacity, excess SB latex capacity in India, butadiene cost disadvantage vs Europe
items.quote: But in the long run we are quite still the competitive intensity of the industry is not significantly changed, as far as except for nitrile latex. Nitrile latex will come to, but the rest of it is the same, in NBR we are the only manufacturer here in India. We are facing dumping for the last year, year and a half mainly due to geo political reason from China and Russia. And the other two, three th

items.statement: Target ROCE ~25% with EBITDA margins 13-15%; current margins 8-9% unsustainable for industry long-term
items.quote: We don't need margins of 20%, 30% EBITDA margins to have good ROCE and even 13% to 15% ROCE, and that's our main goal to have margin of 13% to 15% so ROCE is around 25% and if we can do that, we are in good shape and we continue to grow and we can have sustainable growth that was ROCEs and EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Export sales mix: direct to manufacturers + distributors (commission agents); carpet exports mostly direct with distributor commission; nitrile latex exports to Southeast Asia glove makers
items.quote: it's a combination of the two, direct as well as with a distributor. See, today we don't have any sales, people outside for carpet. So, we do work through distributors, and they work on two levels. One they act like our sales agents, where we just pay them a commission and they take care of the sales relationship of course, our guys from India also, our sales and marketing team, we have a strong s

items.statement: Strong sales and marketing team based in India with relationship managers for each export customer; visit key markets every few months
items.quote: We have a strong sales and marketing team based out of India, and they go visit once every few months. There is a relationship manager in charge of each customer, but day-to-day like if you are in Egypt or Turkey some of our distributors have local offices, so that only helps with day-to-day relationships and day-to-day logistics that they help us with, and we give them a commission for that.

items.statement: FY25 revenue target of 550 crores
items.quote: We remain committed to achieving our target of 550 crores during FY24-25 and look forward to fully utilising the incremental capacity in FY26.

items.statement: FY26 revenue potential of 750-800 crores at full capacity utilisation
items.quote: This can result into a turnover of 750-800 crores.

items.statement: Commercialised 3500 MVA incremental capacity in August 2024, total installed capacity now 7500 MVA
items.quote: we have successfully commercialised an incremental 3500 MVA capacity in August 2024, taking our total installed capacity to 7500 MVA.

items.statement: Existing land parcel can support 25,000-30,000 MVA installed capacity
items.quote: in terms of MVA, we can have install capacity of almost 25,000 to 30,000 MVA. If we utilize the complete land parcel, what we already have right now.

items.statement: Decision on further expansion expected in next two months (December or January)
items.quote: we may take a call in coming December or January, whether to go for an expansion, further expansion and at what capacity. So we will be taking a call in next couple of months.

items.statement: New 5000 MVA capacity can be operational in less than one year once decided
items.quote: suppose that we decide on setting up a 5,000 MVA new capacity, we can, you know, up and running in less than one year.

items.statement: Strong domestic and export demand outlook for next four to five years driven by renewable energy and grid investments
items.quote: we are, you know, expecting a demand for coming, you know, next four to five years for sure

items.statement: Domestic demand expected to grow significantly due to government renewable energy push; export demand also increasing
items.quote: The demand in local market is going to increase quite a bit and even in export market, as I said in my opening remark, that those export demand is also increasing quite a bit.

items.statement: Confident of maintaining current EBITDA margins (around 30%) for next couple of years despite future pricing pressure
items.quote: Yes, we are quite confident on that. Okay.

items.statement: Export sales have higher margins than domestic sales; domestic margins improving due to higher demand
items.quote: export sales have much more, you know, margin than the domestic sales. Though domestic margins are also improving because of the higher demand.

items.statement: Renewable energy transformers (IDT) contribute ~60% of revenue; electronic/telecom transformers <5%
items.quote: I would say almost 60 percent.

items.statement: Export revenue ~45% of sales in H1, mainly to North America (US, Canada) and Middle East; European market breakthrough recently
items.quote: almost 45% of our sales came from export, and we are mainly exporting to North American countries like US, Canada, and Middle East countries.

items.statement: Target domestic-export mix to remain around 50-50 (can vary 60-40 or 40-60) for next 2-3 years
items.quote: Yes, I mean it can vary like I would say 60-40 or 40-60 something like that, but pretty much in that ratio only.

items.statement: All orders at fixed price; commodity price risk hedged by booking raw material immediately upon order receipt
items.quote: all the orders what we received is at fixed price and we have to hedge our risk which we do it very efficiently and we don't take any risk. I mean, as soon as we get the order, we book the raw material.

items.statement: CRGO supply available but prices increased slightly due to BIS import restrictions; company uses advance license for imports
items.quote: there is a restriction of BIS for the import of CRGO and that has created a temporary shortage. Now, the material is available, only thing that prices have gone up slightly

items.statement: ~15 organized suppliers and 20-30 small suppliers in India for <66kV IDT segment; existing suppliers preferred due to track record
items.quote: in organized sector, there are maybe around, you know, good 15 different suppliers. But then there are a lot of small suppliers who cater to these small projects or small solar projects. And that number can be anywhere between, you know, 20 to 25, 30 suppliers all over India.

items.statement: Peer capacity addition not expected to impact margins or orders for next couple of years due to strong demand
items.quote: I don't think so. I mean, because there is a lot of demand right now, I don't think there will be any impact on any, you know, orders or any margins, at least not for coming, you know, couple of years.

items.statement: Majority of customers are repeat customers; new customers added but priority given to existing customers
items.quote: majority of our customers are repeat customers but we do add new customers as well. But right now, the priority goes to our existing customers only.

items.statement: Per MVA realization roughly 10 lakh rupees
items.quote: In our case, it is roughly 10 lakhs rupees.

items.statement: Solar installations require 1:1 transformer capacity (10 GW solar needs 10 GW transformers)
items.quote: if you are installing, say, 10 gigawatts, you need 10 gigawatts of transformer. If you are installing 25 gigawatts, you need 25 gigawatts of transformer. So, there is no incremental or anything.

items.statement: Old capacity fully utilized; new capacity utilization started September 2024, expected full utilization in FY26
items.quote: the old capacity we are fully utilizing. The new capacity we started utilizing from month of September only and we are expected to utilize fully in year 2025-26.

items.statement: No major risk anticipated currently; business always carries risk but everything looks good
items.quote: Business is always a big risk, but right now, I think everything is looking good. I don't expect any major, you know, risk at the moment.

items.statement: Onboarding and training significant new talent to meet expanded operations requirements
items.quote: we are also onboarding and training a significant amount of new talent into the company to meet the requirement of our new set of operations.

items.statement: Considering NSE listing; decision expected next quarter
items.quote: we are seriously thinking on this line also. Of course, decision has not been taken, but we will be again taking decision, you know, maybe next quarter.

items.statement: New competitor supply expected from Q4 FY26; may create some margin pressure but not substantial reduction
items.quote: from last quarter of year 25, 26, the new capacity will start coming into the market. That's what my estimate is.

items.statement: Expect credit growth to reach industry level and slightly above by FY25 end
items.quote: Now you have started seeing the improved credit growth both in the first half and second half and numbers are framing up. And we are taking all our steps to ensure that we touch the industrial growth rate and probably, a small growth over and above that before the year-end is what we are trying to expect.

items.statement: Net NPA expected between 1% and 1.25% by FY25 year-end
items.quote: We conveyed that expected slippage in the financial year '25 would be about INR800 crores during Q4 financial year '24 con call. We are on track. As per the trend, we should be reaching between 1% to 1.25 % net NPA for the year-end.

items.statement: NIM expected at 3.6% plus or minus 10 bps for FY25
items.quote: discussed in the earlier call, the margin should be at the 3.6 % plus or minus 10 basis points, as we discussed during multiple times in the past.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio expected to moderate between 48-50% going forward then decline continuously
items.quote: So as suggested in the earlier con call, we should start seeing the cost-to-income ratio, moderating between 48 to 50 % going forward and then showing a continuous decline.

items.statement: Slippages expected around INR800 crores for FY25
items.quote: We conveyed that expected slippage in the financial year '25 would be about INR800 crores during Q4 financial year '24 con call. We are on track.

items.statement: Gold loan demand strong; bank fine-tuned rates and converted floating to fixed rate
items.quote: So we did some fine tuning on that front, like converting the floating rate of our gold loan into fixed rate and also fine-tuning the rates depending upon the requirement. And it is helping us not to go to the riskier segment of unsecured retail at this point of time.

items.statement: NIM improved to 3.67% in Q2 FY25 from 3.54% in Q1 FY25; H1 FY25 at 3.60%
items.quote: Our net interest margin for Q2 financial year '25 had improved to 3.67 % as compared to 3.54 % in Q1 financial year '25. And for H1 financial year '25, it stood at 3.60 %.

items.statement: Yield on advances improved to 9.81% in Q2 FY25 from 9.77% YoY due to gold loan repricing and rate transmission on renewals
items.quote: Our yield on advances stood at 9.81 % for Q2 financial year '25 against 9.77 % for the same period last year.

items.statement: Advances grew 12% YoY to INR48,422 crores; sequential growth 5% (INR2,100 crores) in Q2 FY25
items.quote: We had registered a 12 % advanced growth for Q2 financial year '25 year-on-year, and our advance increased to INR48,422 crores from INR43,688 crores in Q2 financial year '24.

items.statement: Deposits grew 9% YoY to INR57,369 crores; sequential growth 5% (INR2,512 crores) in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Our deposits had grown by 9 % and stood at INR57,369 crores growth for Q2 '25 as compared to INR52,714 crores for Q2 financial year '24.

items.statement: Gross NPA fell to 3.54% in Q2 FY25 from 3.88% in Q1 FY25; net NPA fell to 1.62% from 1.87%
items.quote: our gross NPA % has sequentially decreased from 4.66 % on last year, 30th September, 4.47 % in December 2023, 3.99 % for the 31st of March 2024, and 3.88 % in 30th of June 2024, and now further reduced to 3.54 % for the current quarter, 30th September 2024.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 slippages INR176 crores vs recoveries INR265 crores; H1 FY25 slippages INR354 crores vs recoveries INR501 crores
items.quote: For Q2 financial year '25, the total slippages is INR176 crores, while the total recoveries is crores, consisting of INR201 crores from live NPA accounts and INR64 crores from the technically written off accounts, resulting in the slippages falling below the recoveries

items.statement: SMA-2 to advances at 2.03%, trending down
items.quote: Overall, SMA 2 to the advances currently stands at 2.03 %. As we have been discussing in the past we are seeing this number coming down.

items.statement: Restructured book reduced from INR929 crores to INR858 crores in Q2 FY25; provision write-back decision at year-end
items.quote: So the number has come down from INR929 crores to INR858 crores in the September quarter.

items.statement: Incremental retail business expenditure ~INR30-35 crores already largely incurred
items.quote: So you will be having around about INR30 crores, INR35 crores will be, by and large, the incremental business expenditure, which is already the greater part is observed in the overall scheme of things.

items.statement: Retail vertical soft launch in Q4 FY25; meaningful contribution from FY26; tech ready, hiring underway
items.quote: So by the beginning of the fourth quarter, we should be having the executive team for that policies. And also the grass root level people, everything will be ready by the, beginning of the fourth quarter. So some amount of minor initial progress will be seen in the fourth quarter, but actual line-up of growth you will be seeing in the next year.

items.statement: MSME digital lending turnaround improved to 3-4 days for loans under INR7.5 crores; 50-60% cases still need manual intervention
items.quote: at least 75 to 80 % of the MSME lending less than, say, INR7.5 crores, we are able to make between 3 to 4 days which is a very big improvement compared to whatever we have been doing in the past.

items.statement: Loan mix: 50% EBLR, 30-35% MCLR, remainder fixed; gold loan 25-30% converted to fixed rate
items.quote: 50% is the EBLR. About 30%-35% is our MCLR. Remaining is fixed.

items.statement: Retail focus on secured lending (housing, LAP, micro LAP); unsecured to stay under 4-5% of portfolio long-term
items.quote: Right from the beginning, when we started, we were very clear about two things. One, we are not entering into the unsecured in a big way. Our entire start in the retail is going to be on the secured retail lending portfolio per se.

items.statement: Retail sourcing: branch/employee-led in South; third-party/DSAs in North and West
items.quote: We will also have new-to-bank customers. Predominantly, we will use our employee sourcing in South, our branch sourcing in South and this is our presence. For North and West, we can use third party.

items.statement: LCR at 121% as of Sep 30, 2024; steps taken on liability and asset side including non-callable deposits and FCNR conversion
items.quote: As per the latest LCR guideline, our LCR is calculated as 121 % for 30th September 2024. We had taken steps both on liability side and asset front like going for some non-callable deposits, converting some foreign currency deposits on maturity into liquid securities and things like that.

items.statement: Cost of deposits stable at 5.73% for H1 FY25; expected to continue in H2 FY25
items.quote: Cost of deposits stood at 5.73 % for H1 financial year '25 which is almost similar to the last quarter, that is Q1 financial year '25.

items.statement: ROA stable at 1.55% for H1 FY25 vs 1.54% YoY; no specific full-year target
items.quote: Our ROA for the first half is at 1.55 % compared to 1.54 % in the corresponding period last. And as stated in the earlier con call, the ROA is stable for the past few quarters.

items.statement: PAT grew 8% YoY to INR550 crores in H1 FY25
items.quote: So we had achieved a PAT growth of 8 % that is current PAT for the H1 stands at INR550 crores against the INR508 crores for H1 FY 24.

items.statement: Recovery from technically written-off accounts volatile; total recovery may vary +/- INR20-25 crores per quarter
items.quote: See, by and large, the total recovery numbers will be plus or minus INR20 crores, INR25 crores. When we take effort, we don't differentiate between which is live and which is technically written off.

items.statement: Provision coverage ratio low on live NPA basis; exploring ways to improve PCR while targeting net NPA 1-1.25%
items.quote: We understand that we are outliers in the provision coverage ratio. We will explore the possibilities of increasing the provision coverage ratio also this year.

items.statement: FY25 credit growth guidance 11-13%
items.quote: We had set a guidance of 11% to 13% credit growth for the FY '25.

items.statement: FY25 deposit growth guidance 9-11%
items.quote: We had given a guidance of 9% to 11% and we have stuck to that guidance.

items.statement: FY25 NIM guidance 2.8-3%
items.quote: We were given guidance at the beginning of the year that the NIM would be in the range of 2.8% to 3%.

items.statement: FY25 gross NPA target below 4% by March 2025
items.quote: Asset quality continues to improve with gross NPA reducing to 4.36%, aligning closely with our target of below 4% by March 2025.

items.statement: FY25 recovery target Rs 16,000 crore
items.quote: In H1 FY '25, we achieved a gross recovery of Rs. 7,300 crores, in line with our annual target of Rs. 16,000 crores.

items.statement: FY25 slippage guidance Rs 11,500 crore
items.quote: Total slippages stood at Rs. 7,537 crores as against our guidance of Rs. 11,500 crores.

items.statement: FY25 credit cost target 1% or below
items.quote: Credit cost, we would like to keep it at 1% or below 1% anytime and that is how it was behaving for all these quarters.

items.statement: Treasury income growth target 20-25% for next two quarters
items.quote: We are hopeful that we have positioned ourselves in the coming days to take advantage of the market. Whatever the things have happened based on the projection, we have booked the profit. In the next two quarters also, we take a defensive and positive view of all those factors and give a decen t 20% to 25% growth in the treasury income

items.statement: Credit pipeline Rs 75,000 crore pending sanctions and disbursements
items.quote: have almost about Rs. 75,000 crore credit for disbursement and sanctions. Out of which Union Bank of India October 22, 2024 Classification: Public Rs. 36,000 crores is pending for disbursement and Rs. 39,000 crores of sanctions are pending for sanctions actually

items.statement: Q2 sanctions Rs 76,000 crore with Rs 36,000 crore pending disbursement
items.quote: If you see our sanctions, in this quarter we have got about Rs. 76,000 crores of sanctions for the current quarter and out of this, Rs. 36,000 crores is pending for disbursement.

items.statement: NIM 2.97% H1 FY25 and 2.90% Q2 FY25
items.quote: Our NIM stood at 2.97% for H1 FY '25 and 2.90% for quarter ended in FY '25, aligning with our guidance of 2.8% to 3%.

items.statement: No fund raise planned; sitting on cash for acquisitions or shareholder returns
items.quote: if we get something which fits our strategy and also fits our price, we will go for it. Else, we are happy to either sit on cash or even return the cash to our shareholders

items.quote: We paid INR94 crores to acquire

items.statement: Two-pronged acquisition strategy: brands in existing therapies or businesses with field force in new sub-chronic therapies
items.quote: Brands within the therapies we are in or businesses with field force if we were to get into additional therapies. But our therapy choice will be sub-chronic

items.statement: Blueloop contribution steady at 27-28% of sales. Adverse product mix due to servicing lower-margin customer demand; new sustainable product introductions below expectations due to customer qualification delays.
items.quote: The blueloop contribution continued to be around 27%, 28%. But this quarter, we saw that apart from the blueloop, there is a challenge on the end customer demand, which basically revolves around the product mix.

items.statement: Focus on protecting share of wallet and market share amid subdued end-consumer demand; large FMCG customers squeezing prices. Food and daily essentials is core focus area.
items.quote: And in this quarter, the focus was more on to protect the share of wallet and market share where the end consumer demand was subdued for various reasons. And as you would have seen, most of the large FMCG companies have also reported similar challenges in the end consumer demand.

items.statement: Blueloop capacity invested globally and in India at large scale; no competitor has invested similar scale. New products replacing foil/PP/PET-based structures; incremental sales still low.
items.quote: The amount of capacity invested by Huhtamaki globally and in India is I would say not a single competitor had invested in such a large-scale capacity. So, there are 2 clear differentiators. One, products clearly differentiated, so both areas, we are far ahead of the competition.

items.statement: Working capital improved YoY and QoQ due to various levers across payables, receivables and overall management.

items.statement: Customer sustainability pledges (2030 targets) and evolving regulations driving blueloop adoption; adoption faster in markets with stricter legislation. Some customer pledges slightly delayed causing near-term headwinds.

items.statement: Competitive intensity high due to excess capacity and flat demand; peers facing similar margin pressures. Blueloop products first-to-market with differentiated portfolio and unmatched capacity investment.
items.quote: When you look at the demand and supply situation, definitely, there is a capacity in the market and demand is not growing. In that context, we have seen even the third quarter, demand is not coming from other market, and also there -- definitely there is a pressure and the competitive situation is really, really becoming more aggressive.

items.statement: Uncertainty in economic environment; inflation may persist even if demand improves gradually. Red Sea supply chain disruptions, raw material inflation, customer sustainability goal delays, competitive pricing pressure.
items.quote: Things are uncertain and even if demand may improve gradually, inflation may still continue that may have impact on the margins. So, there are a lot of uncertainty in the marketplace into the economic environment at this point of time.

items.statement: Net sales INR6.3B in Q3 (-1.5% YoY, +2% QoQ); 9M net sales INR18.5B (-2.5% YoY). EBITDA margin compression; EPS INR1.45 for quarter, INR7 for 9M.
