items.quote: The yield that we've got is around 38%. Originally we had anticipated 35%, so 38% is a little bit improvement on that. I would say that this 38% is an optimum figure.

items.statement: Long-term iron ore supply-demand mismatch expected by 2030 as steel capacity grows 7-8% annually but mine expansions lag
items.quote: Given the pace of the iron ore mining increase in the past few years, we do not see that keeping pace, so we see a mismatch. Some of this mismatch will be covered by other beneficiation projects which are being thought about. But we don't know the extent of that.

items.statement: Pellet trading started as seed marketing for future high-grade pellet exports; marginal loss due to low export margins and prior quarter carryover
items.quote: Pellet trading we have started for three, four directional reasons. The primary reason is that it becomes our seed marketing effort for our higher grade pellets. That we will be coming into the market very shortly so that we can export with a better knowledge of the market when we are fully commercial.

items.statement: No specific management changes or key hires mentioned; ongoing efficiency improvements across projects
items.quote: Within the plans that we are doing, there is a continuous effort to improve efficiencies, improve marketability, improve costs and things like that. So that is an ongoing process.

items.statement: Consolidated annual volume growth guidance of 20% and EBITDA margin of 15%-16% for FY25
items.quote: So overall, we'll continue to maintain our consolidated annual volume growth guidance. We have been talking about 20% and I'm confident of achieving that and also maintaining EBITDA at 15%-16% for the year.

items.statement: India bead wire volume grew 23% and total wire sales grew 10% in H1 FY25
items.quote: So, we have done an impressive volume growth in India of 23% of bead wire and the total wire sales have grown by 10%.

items.statement: Thailand volume grew 32% in H1 FY25 despite Chinese competition
items.quote: We have done a very big growth in Thailand, 32% volume growth in Thailand in the first half of this year

items.statement: India EBITDA margin close to 18%; Thailand EBITDA margin 11%-12% in H1 FY25
items.quote: This coupled with restriction on import from China and again has led to improvement in the EBITDA margin in India also, which is close to 18%. Even our Thailand business has reported healthy EBITDA margin of 11% to 12%

items.statement: India and Thailand plants running at 80%-85% utilisation
items.quote: It's almost 80%, 85% utilization we are running both in Thailand and India.

items.statement: Chennai facility sold ~1,000 tons in Q2 FY25; targeting 2,000 tons/month exit rate and 30,000 tons next year
items.quote: So, we have done around 1000 tons of sales from Chennai this quarter, which is going to grow in the coming months.

items.statement: Chennai FY25 volume target 14,000 tons (PLI commitment); must achieve at least 80% (11,200 tons) to retain PLI benefit
items.quote: Yes. So we will lose the PLI benefit. I think we have to achieve 80% of our commitment. So at least 80% of 14,000 has to be achieved.

items.statement: Chennai capex ~INR300 crores for 60,000 tons capacity; 60% assets capitalized, balance in CWIP
items.quote: Around, 60% of the assets are capitalized. And balance are in the WIP. And gradually everything will get capitalized.

items.statement: Operating cash flow weakened in H1 due to Chennai startup; inventory and receivables up; expect correction in next 6 months
items.quote: I agree with you that it has gone up because of the Chennai startup. I'll say Chennai startup has not reached the desired level of volume to start tightening the screws on outstandings and inventories and all of that.

items.statement: India market share ~42%; Thailand market share >30%; new capacity from Tata Steel, Arti Steel (~30,000 tons), Bansal Wire
items.quote: So last quarter, our market share was 42%. We also do collect information about the competition and how much is the total sales of bead wire happened in that particular month. So our calculation indicates that we were at 42% of market share in India and we were a little higher than 30% in Thailand.

items.statement: Chinese dumping in Thailand pressuring margins; Kiswire selectively competitive; Chinese domestic tyre utilization at 60%-70%
items.quote: Definitely. That's the only factor where we are losing on margins. There are a lot of places where there are no margins, but to keep our fixed costs in control, we need to keep certain volumes up and running.

items.statement: BIS quality control order reduced China imports to India from 3,000-3,500 tons/month to 400-600 tons/month
items.quote: So the volumes which had gone up to 3000 tons a month, or 3500 tons a month in one month, have come down to 400, 500, 600 tons maximum import numbers we see now.

items.statement: One major customer approved 100% supply from Chennai starting this month; more approvals every 15-20 days; Bridgestone Thailand biggest factory audit in December, 20% allocation from Q4
items.quote: One major company has given approval to supply 100% from Chennai facility, which will start this month. Okay. We're starting now. And more -- I can say every 15, 20 days or a month, we'll add on one more customer to the list.

items.statement: Approved supplier to Bridgestone, Michelin, Continental, Goodyear in Southeast Asia and India; pursuing approvals for US and Europe factories
items.quote: The companies like Bridgestone, Michelin, Continental, Goodyear are the ones that we are in discussion with. We are already suppliers to their factories in Southeast Asia and India.

items.statement: Freight savings ~INR3,000/ton by supplying from Chennai to South India vs cross-country from Pithampur
items.quote: So in India, typically 65% of tyres are made in South India and we are in the western part of the country or in the central part of the country. So we are paying extra cost of freight of around INR3,000 per ton, which should be saved when we supply from Chennai to those locations.

items.statement: Export prices to Europe/US structurally 15%-20% higher than Southeast Asia; freight volatility impacted recent profitability
items.quote: Structurally, the prices are definitely much better, 15%, 20% higher than Southeast Asian market, but last two quarters there had been a lot of volatile situations.

items.statement: Chennai facility dedicated to bead wire; no plans for other products to protect quality culture; Pithampur does small black wire volumes
items.quote: No, honestly, this facility cannot be used majorly for making any other product. We will spoil the culture, we will spoil the quality culture.

items.statement: Target consolidated sales of 180,000 tons from three locations (Pithampur, Chennai, Thailand) in coming years
items.quote: Definitely next two years might be a challenge. But in the longer run, we are still confident of selling 180,000 tons from these three locations.

items.statement: Chinese competition in Thailand may limit margin expansion; freight volatility affects export profitability; new competitor capacity may pressure market share
items.quote: If we look at our competitors balance sheet internationally, whether it is Bekeart or Kiswire or a Chinese company, nobody is reaching a double-digit number in EBITDA. While your company is able to do that, that demonstrates our competitiveness.

items.statement: TPM certification audit for Pithampur in November; targeting certification by end of FY25; TPM projects started in Chennai and Thailand
items.quote: Our Indore facility has been audited for TPM certification and the final certification audit will be in November and we are hopeful of getting, you know, TPM certificate for Pithampur facility by end of this financial year.

items.statement: Chennai breakeven at 18,000-20,000 tons when supplying to prime customers; currently supplying to cycle market at no profit
items.quote: No, I think with current expenses and major saving in the transportation costs, it should break even at 18,000 to 20,000 tons volume when we are supplying to prime customers.

items.statement: Board declared interim dividend of INR5 per share
items.quote: I am pleased to begin by announcing that the Board has decided to declare an interim dividend of INR5 per share.

items.statement: Net debt to equity at 0.39x, below guidance range of 0.5x
items.quote: As of 30th September, our net debt to equity stands at 0.39x, well within our guidance range of 0.5x and reflects the strength of our balance sheet.

items.statement: Operating net working capital days at approximately 104 days of sales
items.quote: Operating net working capital days at the end of 30th September is approximately 104x days of sales.

items.statement: R32 capacity expansion capex INR84 crores expected completion by February 2025
items.quote: Additionally, the expansion of R32 capacity with a capex of INR84 crores is proceeding as scheduled and is expected to be completed by February 2025.

items.statement: AHF project capex INR450 crores on track for commissioning by end FY25 or early FY26
items.quote: Our AHF project, which involves an investment of INR450 crores, is on track, and we anticipate commissioning by the end of FY 2025 or early FY '26.

items.statement: Agro specialty plant at Dahej capex INR540 crores under commissioning, commercial production by November 2024
items.quote: Our upcoming agro specialty plant at Dahej with a planned capex of INR540 crores is under commissioning jointly with our customers to ensure a safe and efficient start-up and commence commercial production by November '24.

items.statement: Surat project capex INR30 crores commissioned, first dispatch November 2024
items.quote: Simultaneously, our Surat project with an outlay of INR30 crores is commissioned, and the first dispatch will be in November 2024.

items.statement: cGMP4 Phase 1 capex INR160 crores progressing, target commissioning by end Q3 FY26
items.quote: Phase 1 involving an outlay of INR160 crores is progressing as planned, and we aim to have it commissioned by end of quarter 3 FY '26.

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals has firm orders for Q3, Q4 and calendar 2025 for high-volume products
items.quote: So to give you the feedback, these are the firm numbers because we have entered into the supply understanding for most of the spechem (Inaudible) molecules, which we are talking for the not only quarter 3, quarter 4, but for the calendar year 2025

items.statement: CDMO has strong order visibility with firm orders for H2 FY25 and customer projections strong for FY26
items.quote: We have a strong order visibility with firm orders for the second half of FY '25. Additionally, our strategic focus on late stage and commercial molecules continues to give positive results with the business continuing to witness higher levels of customer inquiries than previously.

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals Q2 revenue declined 15% due to cautious global demand and competitive pressure
items.quote: Sales in this sector were affected by the current global situation, leading to cautious demand behaviour amid continued competitive pressure being witnessed globally.

items.statement: HPP grew 23% driven by higher R32 sales and better R22 realization
items.quote: The growth is mainly attributed to higher R32 sales and better realization for R22.

items.statement: CDMO revenue grew 41% YoY with strong late-stage molecule traction
items.quote: CDMO revenue has increased from INR48 crores in quarter 2 FY '24 to INR68 crores in quarter 2 FY '25, reflecting a growth of 41% year-on-year.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin 20.7% vs 20.8% YoY, up sequentially from 19.2%
items.quote: Operating EBITDA margin stood at 20.7% as against 20.8% in Q2 of FY '24 and improving sequentially from 19.2% in Q1 of FY '25, reflecting higher realizations in HPP as also benefits from efficiencies secured within the businesses.

items.statement: H1 EBITDA margin 19.9% vs 22.1% YoY
items.quote: Operating EBITDA margin for H1 stood at 19.9% as against 22.1% in the same period last year.

items.statement: Board-approved capex continuing into FY25-26: R32, AHF, cGMP4; new project decision by mid-late FY26
items.quote: So the capex that will continue into '25 and '26, of what I can tell you now, are only the Board-approved projects, which are R32, AHF and the cGMP4, yes. Those are continuing. Like we said before, there are several projects we are working on in the hopper. Some of that will mature, and we do hope to look at progressing at least one of those options by middle of next year, middle to late middle.

items.statement: MPP plant operating at 70-75% of peak annual revenue capacity, expected to increase with order visibility
items.quote: But in terms of value, we have talked about saying that, that MPP would be somewhere around -- we would be in the range of about 70%, 75% in terms of the peak annual revenue.

items.statement: CDMO target $100 million revenue by FY27 reaffirmed
items.quote: I've already -- there is a guidance out there of the $100 million by FY '27. We stand to it, yes.

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals order book 50-50 blend of new products launched in last 6-8 months and traditional molecules
items.quote: So, Ankur, this is basically a mix of both. And rather, I will say, the old molecules as well as -- means, we are talking of all 3 old molecules, order visibilities there, rather it is better than what we have seen in the current financial year.

items.statement: European CDMO commercial supplies already started, 2 new late-stage intermediates secured for Q4 supply
items.quote: No, no, the commercial supply for the European CDMO MSA has already started, okay? It's already started. We have now firmer order positions, which I'm saying will show you the growth in Q4 and in the coming quarters.

items.statement: US major client scale-up order received for Q3 FY25 supply
items.quote: For our U.S. major clients, we have received scale-up order for supplies in Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals will see pricing reduction but absolute EBITDA protected via higher capacity commitments
items.quote: And like I said, there will be a reduction in pricing, but the absolute EBITDA will be protected or increased because we've now got higher capacities that we are committing to them.

items.statement: Late-stage CDMO molecules carry portfolio risk - not all may materialize to commercial scale
items.quote: So the idea here is that one of these will come in, and like we've talked at the site visit also, the fact that these are late stage and they are all innovator, they're all blockbusters. So not necessarily all will come. One could come, not necessarily even one could come.

items.statement: HFO plant running at optimal capacity meeting ~80% of demand, debottlenecking options being worked on
items.quote: Remember on the HFO project, we've always said that what we are doing today is we've got the plant running to optimal capacity that's still meeting about 80% of the demand. So there is growth over there, too, right? So there is stuff happening on that front. Plus even within the R32, there are options to build, which we are working on to debottleneck and get greater capacities, but that's still wo

items.statement: Biosecure Act creating opportunity for Indian CDMO as pharma seeks China alternatives
items.quote: And we know the macro in the industry with the Biosecure Act that there is greater emphasis to -- for the large players to look at optionality other than China, and India tends to be more competitive in that space once you step out of China.

items.statement: Targets full-year ROA of 1% in FY26 as a milestone before next growth phase
items.quote: We are looking at a full year ROA of 1% in the year 25-26. That is what we are gunning for.

items.statement: Expects cost-to-average-assets to improve to around 2.6% in next full financial year (April-March)
items.quote: Actually, not for Quarter 3 and Quarter 4, but for the next full year, what we want to be is around 2.6%.

items.statement: NIM at 3.27% is at bottom end; expects improvement as one-offs are done and execution shows results
items.quote: I strongly believe that we are at the bottom end of the NIM and cost to deposits is continuing to hold at the current levels.

items.statement: Structural shift from penal interest to penal charges causes single-digit bps NIM reduction ongoing
items.quote: Like I told you, you can't charge penal interest anymore, so it will come as penal charges and as soon as you collect it, you will get it. So, you will have a single digit bps change happening between NIM and fees

items.statement: Cost of funds flattened at 7.17% and cost of deposits at 7.09%; sees peak cost of deposits
items.quote: So, cost of fund is kind of flattened out at 7.19 coming down to 7.17 and cost of deposit is 7.10 coming to 7.09. I don't see this falling off. I mean even now if we have to look at the way the liabilities, the deposit market is, the reduction happening in the cost of deposit. So, probably we will see a longer play of similar lines.

items.statement: Sees good market for continued growth at current pace; not rushing into high-yield MFI despite yield hit
items.quote: We see a good enough market for it. And the question is how do you make these guys successful rather than how do we go by the fast route.

items.statement: MFI+BC book reduced from 18% to 16% of AIB book (which is 25% of overall book) in Q2
items.quote: 16% of the AIB book is MFI plus BC and that book is 25% of the overall book. So, you can do the math yourself, 16% and 25%. And I'll tell you how to read this. You look at the previous investor presentation and see what the MFI and BC percentage was and I'll tell you what it was. It is actually 18%. That 18 has come down to 16 now.

items.statement: Mortgage stock 50-50 home loan vs LAP; incremental business loan (LAP) now exceeds home loan
items.quote: On the stock 50-50, on the incremental, we are trying to ensure that the BL is more than the HL and that has turned around.

items.statement: Aims to increase average ticket size from 28-30 lakhs to 40-50 lakhs within risk framework
items.quote: We're also working to ensure that this, the average ticket size which currently hovers around 28 lakhs to 30 lakhs is hitched up to between 40 lakhs to 50 lakhs.

items.statement: Gross NPA improved from 3.36% to 3.29% YoY; Net NPA from 1.28% to 1.17%
items.quote: Gross NPA coming down from 3.36% to 3.29% over the last one year and Net NPA shedding 11 bps, 1.28% to 1.17%

items.statement: MFI delinquencies not significantly moved (322 to 333 bps); early action taken on portfolio reduction
items.quote: So, publicly what we share is what you see in page number 26. So, you could possibly see that, you know, the momentum changes on AIB. So, not so far 322 to 333, that's not a big movement yet.

items.statement: Mortgage GNPA rise due to 2023 sourcing quality issues; new vintages performing better after LTV/income norm changes 4-5 months ago
items.quote: Our sourcing in '23 was not the quality that we aspire for. We have made some changes. And the new vintages are behaving better. But specifically, within home loans, the mortgage sourcing in 12 to 24 month bracket was not the kind of quality that we wanted it to be.

items.statement: Collection efficiency steady: bucket zero 98.9% to 98.5% (4 bps deterioration); home loans 3 bps deterioration; sees as business as usual
items.quote: You look at bucket zero behavior. Bucket zero behavior across three big products, I am not including SME in it, but 54%, maybe 55% of the entire book is there in these three lines. This basically determines our overall performance. So, bucket-zero performance has been fairly steady. So, between 98.9 to 98.5, you had a deterioration of four bps. And in home loans, you have a deterioration of 3 bps.

items.statement: Core fee income grew QoQ from Rs 114 cr to Rs 139 cr (5 quarters continuous growth); driven by engagement strategy, savings growth 27% YoY, OD focus, wealth distribution
items.quote: Core fee income was 107 going up to 124 to 136 to 143 to 205. Such quarter-on-quarter for five continuous quarters, that kind of rise does not happen by coincidence. It is because of specific actions that we have implemented on the ground while you are seeing the growth happening on the overall fee line.

items.statement: Upgraded Finacle, transaction banking, FinOne lending, treasury management, SIEM, AML compass, behavioral biometrics over last 12-18 months; benefits expected over next 6 quarters
items.quote: The bank has upgraded Finacle system, th e transaction banking system , the lending system, FinOne, the treasury management system from TCS, the SIEM system for cyber security, a compass system for AML, behavioral biometrics. We have put in the hard yards on technology over the last 12 to 18 months, and we will see the benefit of that on a go -forward basis

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio improved QoQ from 67.8% to 64.3% (almost 3% reduction)
items.quote: Net -net, we have had 11 bps improvement in ROA. In our journey where the next stop is a yearly RO A of 1%. Our ROE has moved from 10.93% in Q1 to 12.65%. So, you are seeing some of the effort converting it to result, and you'll be able to see more of it in the not-too-distant future

items.statement: CASA ratio improved marginally from 25.04% to 25.61% YoY; savings deposits grew 27% YoY
items.quote: Our CASA ratio has marginally improved from 25.04 to about 25.61 in the year. But that may be unremarkable as it is, but what is remarkable is our savings growth. Savings has grown by 27% year-on-year clearly showing the effort leading to the desired result.

items.statement: ROA improved 11 bps QoQ to 0.93%; ROE improved from 10.93% to 12.65% QoQ
items.quote: Net -net, we have had 11 bps improvement in ROA. In our journey where the next stop is a yearly RO A of 1%. Our ROE has moved from 10.93% in Q1 to 12.65

items.statement: Promoter infusion of $10 million expected to close in Q3 FY25; documentation in final stages
items.quote: We are kind of dotting the i's and crossing the t's on that. So, there is some documentation which is being asked for. So, we are providing all that. So, getting that loop. We are almost at the tail end of it. While it's not substantial in itself, it is symbolic, so it'll be good to see that happening. If you ask me, it'll happen in Q3.

items.statement: MFI environment may take at least a year to normalize; will not rush into high-yield MFI assets; will only do to meet PSL targets
items.quote: The MFI environment I would tend to presume will take a year at least to get back to normal. I could be wrong. Okay, but that's just an educated, rather uneducated guess. So, there are two elements. So, that being the way it is, I don't see ourselves rushing headlong into high yield MFI assets which would have otherwise done.

items.statement: Mortgage 2023 vintage quality issues will cause delayed NPA recognition but no denial; LTV/income norms tightened 4-5 months ago
items.quote: So, in mortgages, we have made some changes on our LTV and income assessment norms for certain segments. So, that change we made about four to five months back. But the errors that we made earlier will have an impact. And we will have to go through it. So, there will be a delay, but I don't think there'll be a denial.

items.statement: RBI circular on interest charging from demand draft handover date caused one-off NIM hit in Q1-Q2; fully implemented now
items.quote: Reserve Bank of India had sent a communication to banks, I think banks and NBFCs, I could be wrong, but definitely to banks, where interest charged to customers, to customers who had taken loans should start from the time the demand draft was handed over to customers.

items.statement: Rebalanced borrowing strategy to align cost of funds with cost of deposits; used short-term CDs to match short-term assets
items.quote: So, what we did is we went back and reworked our borrowing strategy and ensured that the cost of funds is more or less in line with the direction the cost of deposit takes, which is why you are seeing a correlated movement of cost to funds and cost to deposit happening in this quarter, 719 coming to 717 and 710 coming to 709.

items.statement: Does not see SME stress emerging; bucket-zero collection efficiency steady across major products covering 55% of book
items.quote: Not really, and I'll tell you why. Look at the collection efficiency chart, for bucket zero and for all buckets put together. That's a very revealing chart. Okay, that is page number 28. Yes, yes. Right, I'll tell you why it's so revealing. You look at bucket zero behavior. Bucket zero behavior across three big products, I am not including SME in it, but 54%, maybe 55% of the entire book is there

items.statement: Balance sheet grew 19.49% YoY with similar advances and deposits growth; top 20 depositors stable at 6.89%
items.quote: We have grown the balance sheet by 19.49%. Similar kind of percentage growth in advances and deposits. On the deposit front, the growth of 19.86% Y oY has been recorded in reasona bly tough times of liquidity, I should say. And what is heartening is this growth is in a scenario where our top 20 depositors remain at a very comfortable 6.89%, very similar to the 6.88% we had last year

items.statement: Full-year sales guidance of INR17,000 crores maintained; confident of achieving it despite Q2 shortfall
items.quote: we still maintain a first half total sales -- presales of about INR7,000 crores and continue to be strongly poised for achieving our sales guidance for the year.

items.quote: In RERA, what we have filed right now is the total revenue of about INR26,000 crores for Dahlias based on the prelaunch price that Aakash has. items.statement: Targeting weighted average embedded margin in late 40s; Dahlias at 70%+, other new projects at 40%+
items.quote: I think with Dahlias baked in, you will see this number approaching our target number of the late 40s, frankly. items.quote: We anticipate comfortably to be at INR2,500 crores plus collection machine for Q3 and hopefully an even higher number for Q4. By the way, this excludes One Midtown collection, because that is not consolidated, and that's now going at a very strong clip as well.

items.statement: Net debt already zero; gross debt zero target on track in next 3-4 quarters unless significant opportunity arises
items.quote: if there's no other significant opportunity that is pursued, I think that's a target which remains on track frankly in the next three to four quarters.

items.quote: Our NRI business has grown from 3%, 8% to about almost now 28% this year. So we will continue to make sure that not only in India, but across the globe, we will continue to market DLF products.

items.statement: One Midtown JV cash flows to start from Q3 FY25; balance P&L to accrue from Q3 onwards post OC receipt

items.statement: RentCo PAT growth expected at 20%+ on sustained basis
items.quote: Actually, the PAT growth in the RentCo business will be 20% plus on a sustained basis here, yes.

items.statement: Demand outlook for next few quarters remains strong; expect continued delivery momentum
items.quote: demand outlook for the next few quarters continues to be strong and we expect to continue the delivery momentum

items.statement: Added 3,748 macro towers and 4,308 collocations in Q2; total macro towers 229,658 and collocations 379,236
items.quote: In Q2, we added 3,748 m acro towers and 4,308 corresponding collocations . O ur total m acro towers and collocations base stood at 229,658 and 379,236, each increasing by 12.5% and 7.3% year -on-year respectively

items.statement: Net co-location additions including leaner towers were 4,490 in Q2 vs 6,832 in Q1
items.quote: Including leaner towers, our net co-location additions were at 4,490 in Q2 versus 6,832 in Q1.

items.statement: Energy margins impacted by seasonality in Q1/Q2; expect recovery in Q3/Q4
items.quote: Typically Q1 and Q2, the energy margin is impacted by the seasonality which we expect to recover in the Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Implementing technological solutions for remote monitoring to enable infrastructure rationalization and cost efficiencies
items.quote: With regards to capex, we are working towards implementing technological solutions at our sites which would enable remote monitoring of sites on real-time basis and provide requisite data.

items.statement: Solar site count increased to over 25,000 with quarterly additions close to 4,000
items.quote: renewable energy portfolio continues to expand with our solar si te count increasing to more than 25,000 and quarterly additions being close to 4,000

items.statement: 5G BTS deployed now over 450,000; India witnessing one of fastest 5G rollouts globally
items.quote: The total number of 5G Base Transceiver Stations or BTS deployed now stands at over 4,50,000, with India witnessing one of the fastest 5G rollouts in the world.

items.statement: 100% collection against monthly billing from major customer sustained; past overdue collections improved further
items.quote: I am pleased to report that in line with the trajectory of the previous three quarters, we sustained 100% collection against monthly billing from a major customer while our collections against past overdue improved further during the quarter.

items.statement: Collected over Rs 23 billion in past 12 months from major customer; provision for doubtful debt reduced to ~Rs 35 billion
items.quote: We have collected a total of more than Rs. 23 billion in the last 12 months. This has resulted in our provision for doubtful debt reducing to about Rs. 35 billion.

items.statement: Expect incremental tenancies from other major customers in near term; anticipate growth from in-building and small cell solutions
items.quote: In addition to the rollouts of one of our major customers, we are anticipating incremental tenancies to flow through from other major customers as well in the near term, which we believe will act as a fillip to our growth.

items.statement: No impact seen from tower industry consolidation; focus remains on own performance and market share capture
items.quote: To be honest, I mean we have not seen any such thing. I think we continue to be driving tower tenancy growth from our customers so I have not seen any impact as such in terms of any change in the competitive dynamics.

items.statement: Diesel consumption reduced 2% YoY in Q2; reduction lower due to weather disturbances
items.quote: Our diesel consumption reduced further by 2% in Q2 on a year-on-year basis. The reduction in diesel consumption was lower primarily due to weather disturbances I had alluded to earlier.

items.statement: Renewal framework from FY2022 remains consistent; discount levels similar to previous framework
items.quote: The framework is very consistent, so just as a recap we had signed a renewal framework in FY2022 and that was the time when we had really a bulk sort of a renewal, thereafter there has not been any major lumpy renewal in the last two financial years but pretty much the framework remains consistent and the discount levels are also very similar to what we had worked out.

items.statement: Net finance cost fluctuates with interest collection on overdue; gross finance cost stable
items.quote: The finance cost is largely the cost of borrowing and I do not think there is anything major that has changed there. If you are looking at the net finance cost number then obviously there is a bit of fluctuation in our finance income which is driven by the fact that we are trying to collect interest on the overdue as well from one of our customers.

items.statement: Completed buyback of 56.8 million shares at Rs 465 per share; Bharti Airtel shareholding increased to >50%
items.value: 56.8 million shares at Rs 465 per share
items.quote: During the quarter, the Company successfully completed the buyback of 56.8 million shares at a price of Rs.465 per share. Post this, shareholding of Bharti Airtel in the company increased to more than 50%.

items.statement: Dividend policy directs distribution of free cash flow; Board will decide at year-end based on collections and cash flow
items.quote: we have a very clear dividend policy which directs u s to distribute the free cash flow so at the end of the year the Board will take a call in line with the policy

items.statement: Gender diversity improved to 14.3% in Q2 from 11.2% in Q1; launched women leadership program 'Shakti' with IIM Indore
items.quote: our focused hiring programmes have led to our gender diversity improving to 14.3% in Q2 compared to 11.2% in Q1. During the quarter , we also launched our women leadership development program me, ‘Shakti’, in collaboration with IIM Indore

items.statement: Tenancy ratio industry-leading at 1.65
items.quote: Our tenancy ratio continues to be industry leading at 1.65.

items.statement: Average data consumption per user 26 GB/month, up 17% YoY; 5G data consumption grew 28% QoQ to 11.4 billion GB
items.quote: The average data consumed per user per month increased to 26 G B in the same period, growing by 17% year -on-year. Additionally, as per TRAI, 5G data consumption grew 28% quarter -on-quarter to 11.4 billion GB

items.statement: GST show-cause notice on passive infrastructure assets; liability considered remote and matter sub-judice
items.quote: The show-cause notice that we have received is basically putting a question on the GST credit on passive infrastructure assets like the diesel generator, AC, and battery bank that we deploy and based on our assessment, we believe that the liability currently is not evolving on the company, and we consider this as remote.

items.statement: Income tax contingent liability of Rs 41 billion is legacy matter from 2010-2012; separate from GST issue
items.quote: The contingent liability for direct tax or income tax that you are referring to is a legacy matter that has been going on for a long time and that is basically goes back to almost 2010, 2011 and 2012.

items.statement: Expect ongoing rollouts of major customer plus start of rollouts and 5G loading by other major customer to drive near to medium term growth
items.quote: We expect the ongoing rollouts of a major customer coupled with start of rollouts and 5G loading by the other major customer to continue to drive our near to medium term growth.

items.statement: New towers are low capex with lower ARPT than legacy portfolio; mix drag offsets loading upside on ARPT
items.quote: The new towers that we are doing are basically low capex and the ARPT relating to those new towers are also lower than the legacy portfolio, so to that extent there is a bit of a drag.

items.statement: Vodafone Idea active equipment deal rollout expected mid-to-end of current quarter; tenancies to follow equipment deployment
items.quote: We see this coming towards the mid-to-end quarter is what indications we get from the customer so hopefully this quarter will see some things rolling out.

items.statement: Board approved raising up to ₹14 billion via subordinated NCDs over next 12 months to augment solvency and aid growth
items.quote: The Board at its meeting today has approved raising additional capital by issuance of non-convertible debentures of upto ₹ 14 billion , in the nature of subordinated debt instruments in one or more tran ches, over the next 12 months , on a private placement basis.

items.statement: Products redesigned per new surrender value regulations; customer benefit impact minimized except where yield curve changes necessitated
items.quote: I am also happy to share that our available to sell products have been redesigned in line with the new product regulations, keeping the interest of customers, shareholders, and distributors in mind.

items.statement: VNB margin 23.7% in H1 FY2025; movement driven by shift to ULIP mix and limited ability to align non-linked/annuity rates with declining G-Sec yields
items.quote: The movement in margin is primarily due to two factors. One is the shift in the underlying product mix towards unit -linked on account of the continued market buoyancy and the decline in the non-participating business.

items.statement: Starting October, aligning non-linked and annuity product rates with prevailing G-Sec yields after limited ability to change rates in Q2 due to regulatory product changes
items.quote: Starting October, we have started aligning product rates with prevailing G-Sec yields.

items.statement: RWRP grew 33.9% YoY in Q2 and 39.2% YoY in H1 FY2025, outperforming private and overall industry; gained 1.1% private market share to 10.3%
items.quote: We delivered RWRP growth of 33.9% year-on-year in Q2-FY2025 and 39.2% year-on-year in H1-FY2025, outperforming both the private and overall industry over the last four quarters.

items.statement: ULIP share of APE rose to 51.6% from 42.4%; non-linked savings fell to 18.1% from 26.6%; protection and annuity together 48.2% of new business premium
items.quote: Contribution from linked savings product to overall APE increased from 42.4% in H1-FY2024 to 51.6% in H1-FY2025 on account of customer preference shifting towards ULIP products from non -linked products given market buoyancy.

items.statement: ICICI Bank premium consistent at ₹100-110 crore monthly; focus on protection and annuity growing significantly
items.quote: ICICI Bank is now quite consistent at ` 100 crores- ` 110 crores on a monthly basis. So, they've been quite consistent.

items.statement: Partnership distribution retail APE weak temporarily due to non-linked prioritization; added 90+ partners in H1; expect recovery post surrender guideline settlement
items.quote: We have added 90+ partners within H1-FY2025, which is added to our overall width of distribution. And we believe that after the surrender guideline changes settling down and markets normalizing with other businesses picking up, partnership distribution will come back on track overall.

items.statement: Added over 29,000 agents in H1 FY2025; 45 bank tie-ups with ~22,000 branches; 1,200+ non-bank partnerships
items.quote: We continue to build capacity and have added more than 29,000 agents during H1 -FY2025 spread across geographies. We have tie -ups with 45 banks with access to approximately 22,000 bank branches and more than 1,200 non-bank partnerships.

items.statement: Cost to TWRP 29.4% in H1 (down from 32.6% in Q1); savings line cost to TWRP 17.9% (down from 19.2% in Q1); investing in people, tech, process for future operating leverage
items.quote: Cost to TWRP stood at 29.4% in H1-FY2025, which came down from 32.6% in Q1-FY2025. Our Cost to TWRP on the savings line of business stood at 17.9% in H1 -FY2025 which has come down from 19.2% in Q1-FY2025

items.statement: VNB grew 4.2% YoY to ₹10.58 billion in H1 FY2025; Embedded Value grew 19.4% to ₹460.18 billion; AUM ₹3.2 trillion; solvency 188.6%
items.quote: VNB grew by 4.2% year -on-year to ₹ 10.58 billion in H1-FY2025. With an APE of ₹ 44.67 billion, the margin stood at 23.7%. Embedded value grew by 19.4% and stood at ₹ 460.18 billion in H1-FY2025.

items.statement: Annuity APE grew 99.5% YoY in H1; retail protection grew 17.2% YoY; credit life non-MFI robust, MFI slowdown; group term pricing pressure
items.quote: Annuity business contribution increased from 6.2% in H1-FY2024 to 9.7% of overall APE in H1-FY2025. Protection and annuity are our focus segments which together constitute 48.2% of the new business premium and we expect it to continue doing well.

items.statement: Commission structure talks with partners ongoing: clawback, deferral, progressive commissions, reductions; expect market to settle this quarter
items.quote: The conversations with distributors are on the three lines that Amit also spoke of, deferment of commissions, progressive commission structures, clawback of commissions where required, and of course, where needed, we have actually proposed reduction in commissions.

items.statement: Sub-debt raise of ₹14 billion to increase solvency ~20%; current ₹12 billion outstanding; negative carry marginal
items.quote: So, Gaurav, if we raise the ₹ 14 billion, that should increase the solvency roughly 20%. This is the cap that we have hit at this point.

items.statement: Renewal premium growth subdued (~3%) due to maturing 10+ year policies, ULIP lock-in expiries (FY18-19 vintage), and past muted growth phase (pre-2022); expect improvement as recent growth feeds through
items.quote: There are two elements to this. One is that we do have some of our policies which are of a longer tenure, typically 10 years and above, which are now hitting the point of maturity, where, of course, these are in some sort of planned outgo.

items.statement: Variable annuity product under exploration; no product ready yet; evaluating structures and hedging strategies
items.quote: But frankly, at this point, we don't have a product. We continue to explore what are the structures that we could put in place to provide this product to our customers.

items.statement: Agency and Direct channels grew 45.7% APE YoY in H1; proprietary channel investment in capability, micro-market strategy, and learning architecture gives confidence for 2-3 year sustainability
items.quote: Agency and Direct business, we have been speaking on the investment in capacity that we have been doing for last 2 to 3 y ears now very consistently, both in terms of people that we have deployed, capability that we have created, the formal learning architecture that we have institutionalised now.

items.statement: Non-par and annuity margins impacted by yield curve decline in Q2; participating doing better than non-par; margin movement Q1 to H1 negligible
items.quote: The impact of the yield curve has been felt on the non -par as well as the annuity product line. That's true.

items.statement: 13th month persistency 89.8%, 49th month 69.9% in H1; claim settlement ratio 99.3% with 1.2 day avg TAT for non-investigated claims; 48% policies issued same day
items.quote: Our 13 th month persistency stood at 89.8% and 49 th month persistency stood at 69.9%, a testimony to our customers' continued trust in us.

items.statement: ULIP Platinum product with trail commissions gaining traction in agency/direct; not biased toward any product; customers choose based on suitability
items.quote: It will remain stable, like I said, Gaurav. At a Company level, from a strategy perspective, we don't have a bias for any specific product. We are only creating options.

items.statement: Group term pricing pressure from increased competition; underwriting focused on risk-reward expectations; not chasing unprofitable business
items.quote: Coming to the group term business, there has been a continued and significant trend of price reduction in this area, largely attributable to increased competition.

items.statement: Commission expense increase YoY due to new structures implemented Q1 last year, fully effective by Q3; sequentially commission rates broadly stable at product level
items.quote: Quarter one last year is when we started implementing the new set of commission across partners. Quarter one was quite low to that extent, but these commission structures started to get implemented over quarter two. And they got into full force in quarter three.

items.statement: APE grew 26.8% YoY to ₹44.67 billion in H1; retail APE grew 32.7% to ₹38.27 billion; policies up 12.5% YoY
items.quote: The overall APE grew by 26.8% to ₹ 44.67 billion and number of policies increased by 12.5% year-on-year in H1-FY2025.

items.statement: Added over 1 lakh agents in last 2.5 years; focus on distinct advisor profiles matching customer segments; licensed advisor base grew ~60% in H1
items.quote: So, over the last 2.5 years, I think we have added over a lakh of agents. So, that is the first number that comes to mind.

items.statement: ICRA and CRISIL reaffirmed AAA/Stable rating on existing ₹12 billion subordinated debt program
items.quote: ICRA and CRISIL, the domestic rating agencies, have reaffirmed the rating of our existing ₹ 12 billion subordinated debt program as [ICRA] AAA (Stable) and CRISIL AAA/Stable respectively.

items.statement: Retained MSCI AA ESG rating; highest rated Indian insurer per leading ESG agencies; awards for digitalization, customer service, claim management
items.quote: We continue to be the highest rated Indian insurer as per the two leading ESG rating agencies. We successfully retained our "AA" ESG rating from MSCI, which also makes us one of the top-rated life Insurer in India.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 EBITDA margin target of around 20%
items.quote: we committed to achieve around 20% EBITDA for the entire financial year

items.statement: H2 FY25 expected to be significantly better than H1 with Q4 CDMO project deliveries
items.quote: Currently, we believe we are on track to deliver what we committed for growth in H2

items.statement: Net debt expected to stay below INR3,000 crores
items.quote: we will not breach the INR3,000 crores range

items.statement: Capex allocation: biocatalysis ~INR225 crores, FDF CMO ~INR200 crores, rest CDMO, API lower
items.quote: Bio, arou nd INR225 crores, and CDMO will be the major, and then probably FDF another INR200 crores

items.statement: New small molecule R&D center at IKP Hyderabad commenced operations in October 2024
items.quote: we have commenced operations at our new small molecule R&D center in October 2024

items.statement: Fermentation site R2 expanded with new pilot plant to optimize capacity and debottleneck R1
items.quote: We also expanded our capabilities at our fermentation site, R2, by adding a new pilot plant

items.statement: Larger fermentation capacity build on track for GMP manufacturing opportunity
items.quote: The plan to build larger fermentation capacity is on track to capitalize on GMP manufacturing opportunity

items.statement: Contract manufacturing formulation capacity to start Q1 FY26
items.quote: We will start Q1 FY '26. We are investing more into manufacturing lines and packaging lines

items.statement: CDMO working on over 90 active projects (70+ Human Health, ~20 Animal Health and Crop Production)
items.quote: We are working on over 90 active projects in total, over 70 in Human Health and about 20 in the Animal Health and Crop Production

items.statement: ARV order book encouraging, maintaining leading share in first-line HIV treatment
items.quote: The current order book for product basked looks encouraging, and we continue to maintain a leading share in the first-line HIV treatment

items.statement: CDMO demand positive with rising complex compounds in clinical phases, healthy growth expected in FY25
items.quote: the outlook within small molecule service industry is positive. And then specific, there is good demand for specialized expertise with rising number of complex compounds in the clinical phases

items.statement: Gross margin maintained at 55% in Q2 and H1 FY25
items.quote: Gross margin maintained at a healthy level for Q2 at 55%, and for H1, it is at, same, 55%

items.statement: EBITDA margin suppressed at 15% in H1 due to lower asset utilization and growth project dilution
items.quote: EBITDA margins remained subdued at 15%. This is due to lower asset utilization and dilution from growth projects initiatives in cell and gene therapy as well as both Human Health and Crop Sciences

items.statement: Operating deleverage nearing end, leverage expected to kick in within few quarters
items.quote: Maybe we are at the end of the deleverage. If you ask me, when we will leverage, maybe we have to wait a few quarters, but we at the end of the deleverage right now

items.statement: R&D pipeline of 62 products under review or development with significant addressable market
items.quote: We have a total of 62 products in the R&D pipeline, either under review or under development, having a significant addressable market size

items.statement: Filed 4 DMFs in H1 (3 non-ARV), total 87 DMFs filed to date
items.quote: During H1, we filed 4 DMFs. Out of these, 3 are in non-ARV category. With this, total number of DMFs filed so far is 87

items.statement: 42 ANDAs filed cumulatively (21 final approvals, 14 tentative approvals)
items.quote: Cumulatively, we have a total of 42 ANDAs filled to dat e. Of these, we have a total of 21 final approvals and 14 tentative approvals so far

items.statement: KRKA collaboration progressing smoothly, tech transfer initiated for multiple products
items.quote: our collaboration with our partner, KRKA, is progressing smoothly, and the capacity expansion remains on track to meet their strategic capacity needs. We have already initiated tech transfer for multiple products under this arrangement

items.statement: Existing CDMO customers increasing pipeline, discussions for Phase II/III molecules to add new vendor
items.quote: Existing customers are increasing their pipeline toward us. That's the positive what we are seeing

items.statement: Passed 76 quality audits in H1 without critical observations, including successful US FDA inspection of Hyderabad API facility
items.quote: In H1, the company underwent close to 76 quality audits by multiple regulatory agencies and several customers. The company has successfully passed audit inspections without any critical findings

items.statement: LSPL plant Import Alert lifted after FDA inspection and response
items.quote: today, that site, they have lifted the Import Alert. We have no Import Alert on that site

items.statement: Net debt at INR2,679 crores, debt-to-EBITDA at 3.4x, expected to improve in H2
items.quote: Our net debt stood at INR2,679 crores, and debt to EBITDA is around 3.4x. This we expect to improve based on H2 performance

items.statement: Net working capital elevated in H1 but expected to reduce by March
items.quote: H1, actually, we have a higher number as an NWC, but March, definitely, it will come down

items.statement: R&D spend at 5.4% of sales in H1 FY25, up 25% YoY
items.quote: On R&D front, our overall spending to sales for the first half of this financial year was at 5.4%, which was increased by 25% year-on-year

items.statement: ROCE at 5.6% in H1 FY25 due to lower profitability and continued capex
items.quote: Our ROCE was around 5.6%. This is because of lower profitability and the capex and continued capex investment for the growth projects

items.statement: Lenacapavir disruption not expected in access markets for 5 years, pursuing sterile manufacturing capabilities
items.quote: typically, the delta between approval in Europe, U.S. versus bringing that regimen to access markets is 3 years. So no therapy regimen disruptions will happen in the next 5 years

items.statement: Targets double-digit growth for the full year if market improvement continues; digital initiatives expected to show results in Q4
items.quote: We believe some of our digital initiatives that we have put in, which got -- last of that got over at the end of the second quarter. We'll start showing results maybe in the fourth quarter of the year and as a team, we changed the double-digit growth for the organization.

items.statement: Digital business expected to deliver 30%+ margins versus 20-22% for radio
items.quote: We are about 20%, 22% of the margins that we talk about. We will be a 30% plus on digital, which is a good 10%, 20%, 15% more.

items.statement: Industry slowdown in July-August with recovery from September; Q3 start looks good
items.quote: The slowdown, obviously, I know in my speech also, I mentioned was for the month of July and August and second half, which is starting September, slightly showing recovery. And the start of the quarter for the third quarter looks good.

items.statement: Advertisement yield grew 8% year-on-year in Q2
items.quote: We have increased, I told you, 8% over last year's similar quarter.

items.statement: Digital revenue contribution at 11% in Q2 with 33% YoY growth; revenue split 65% FCT, 11% digital, 10% on-ground, 14% non-FCT on-air
items.quote: The digital segment achieved an impressive of 33% year-on-year growth, contributing 11% to our total revenue.

items.statement: Digital investments primarily in specialist manpower for video, influencer and distribution platforms; SMINCO platform development cost under Rs.1 crore
items.quote: For the investment in SMINCO, we already said we have less than Rs.1 crores is what we had invested from a platform development is concerned. And that's a one-time investment.

items.statement: Inventory utilization at 71% in H1 FY25; 38% of industry client base and 30% of new radio clients chose Radio City
items.quote: Our inventory utilization in H1FY25 stood at 71%, showcasing the efficiency of our operations and our ability to maximize all the resources.

items.statement: Phase III auction participation depends on government standardizing license fees at 4% of gross revenue and extending timelines; will bid in existing states or strategic new markets
items.quote: So as AROI, which is our industry forum, has already, a, appealed to the government to kind of relook at the licensing fees because if you know the newer market, they have agreed to the 4% of the gross revenue as the licensing fee.

items.statement: Full-year cost of funds guided at 7.10%-7.15% vs earlier 7.20%-7.25%
items.quote: And we now expect the full year cost of funds to be in the range of 7.10% to 7.15% range rather than 7.20% to 7.25% initially expected.

items.statement: Loan growth target of 25% for FY25 maintained despite MFI and credit card slowdown
items.quote: Our loan portfolio now stands at ~INR105,000 crores, and we remain on course to hit our growth target of 25% for the year despite slowdown in MFI and calibrated approach in credit cards.

items.statement: Full-year NIM expected to be protected close to 6%
items.quote: So we expect that our NIM should get protected close to 6%.

items.statement: Full-year cost-to-income ratio expected around 60%
items.quote: Operating expenses would be seasonally higher in H2, but I expect cost-to-income ratio to be around 60% for the full year.

items.statement: Full-year ROA target defended at 1.6%
items.quote: For the full year, we aim to defend ROA of 1.6%.

items.statement: Full-year credit cost expected to remain broadly at H1 level (~1.28%) with 5-10 bps variance
items.quote: As things stand today, we expect credit costs to remain elevated and finish full year around broadly the same level as Half 1 based on the current outlook. There could be a variance of 5, 10 bps, depending on the economic condition in the second half too.

items.statement: Yield on gross advances stable at 14.4% in Q2
items.quote: Our yield on assets -- yield on gross advances was broadly stable at 14.4%.

items.statement: Cost of funds stable at 7.04% in Q2 vs 7.03% in Q1
items.quote: Our cost of funds was stable at around 7.04% compared to 7.03% in quarter 1 FY '25.

items.statement: Incremental disbursement yield at 15.2% vs portfolio yield of 14.4%
items.quote: And Rohan, one more thing, that the gross advances, which is 14.4%. So our incremental yield is also more than that. So it's a 15.2%, which is higher than our gross advances yield

items.statement: Total deposits crossed INR 1 lakh crore to ~INR 110,000 crore, up 12.7% Q-o-Q
items.quote: I'm very happy to say you that our total deposits crossed the milestone of INR1 lakh crores to stand at ~INR110,000 crores, registering a quarter-to-quarter growth of 12.7%.

items.statement: CASA deposits grew 11% Q-o-Q; CASA ratio at 32%
items.quote: Our CASA deposits grew by 11% quarter-to-quarter. All key parameters remain on track with CASA ratio at 32% and CD ratio at 86%.

items.statement: GLP portfolio grew ~5% Q-o-Q and 9% YTD to ~INR 105,000 crore
items.quote: On the asset side also, we had a robust quarter with our GLP portfolio growing around 5% quarter-to-quarter, 9% on a year to date basis. Our loan portfolio now stands at ~INR105,000 crores.

items.statement: MBL disbursements up 18% Q-o-Q; Wheels disbursements up 12% Q-o-Q
items.quote: Disbursement was up by 18% quarter-to-quarter in MBL and 12% in Wheels.

items.statement: 81% of disbursements in high ROA assets
items.quote: And more importantly, 81% of our disbursement was in high ROA assets.

items.statement: Wheels rollout to ~250 Fincare touchpoints and MBL to ~100 by FY25 end
items.quote: We are leveraging Fincare's distribution network and increasing our product coverage in each touch point and to do that, we are starting with wheels in around 250 touch point and MBL in 100-touch point by the end of the financial year.

items.statement: Other income rose to 32% of NII in Q2 from 27% in Q1
items.quote: We had another strong quarter of performance in other income, which increased to 32% of net interest income versus 27% in quarter 1.

items.statement: Fee income components expected to pick up further in Q3 and Q4
items.quote: Further, we expect all the fee income component to pick further in quarter 3 and quarter 4.

items.statement: MFI (7% of book) credit cost elevated due to industry overleveraging; 3% through-cycle credit cost expected
items.quote: MFI, which is 7% of our book is cyclical nature and asset quality is elevated, driven by industry-wide issue of overleveraging of customers. As we did communicated previously, we expect a 3% annualized credit cost through the cycle for MFI, and we are building our provisions accordingly.

items.statement: MFI collection efficiency 98.44% in Q2 vs 99.07% in Q1; H1 at 98.75%
items.quote: So the collection efficiency for quarter 2 was 98.44%. Quarter 1 was 99.07%. So overall, in H1, we have delivered the current bucket collection efficiency of 98.75%.

items.statement: Unsecured slippages 33% of total in Q2 vs 25% in Q1
items.quote: Nitin, Quarter 2 was worse than quarter 1. So you are asking in [725] slippages -- 33% is from unsecured and 67% is from secured -- so that's the way we want to say that the entire segment was effective, right?

items.statement: Borrowers with 5+ lenders reduced from 11% in June to 8% in September
items.quote: In fact, Nitin, Prince, here, if you look at the data point, I think from June to September, it has gone down from 11% to about 8%. So it has been reducing as we speak as well.

items.statement: No branch expansion in FY25; leveraging 140 Fincare branches for synergy
items.quote: We've got around 140-odd branches from Fincare. So we haven't done any kind of branch expansion this year. That is helping us to be at lower cost.

items.statement: Applied to RBI for voluntary transition to Universal Bank licence
items.quote: And as you all know, we have recently filed an application with RBI for voluntary transition to Universal Bank and upgrade to Universal Bank license will strengthen our deposit franchise with a better brand acceptance and higher customer perception of safety and trust.

items.statement: SA deposit rates rationalized: 3% rate now offered up to INR 3 lakh from INR 1 lakh earlier
items.quote: And this time, like we did that in the first quarter. And we saw -- we didn't really see too much outflow of deposits. In fact, deposits grew in that particular bucket. So to that extent, we took further steps this quarter and we have now rationalized in up to INR3 lakh as well, taking that number from INR1 lakh to INR3 lakh.

items.statement: Headcount flat despite 11% business growth; productivity focus and Fincare synergies driving cost reduction

items.statement: FSSAI norms becoming more stringent; company actively educating customers on product quality and labelling
items.quote: FSSAI norms are becoming even more stringent. We will be actively trying to make customers more aware of what they require.

items.statement: Excess rainfall in South India may cause loss of couple of days sales in Q3 but not significant; diversified across 4-5 states mitigates regional impact
items.quote: Maybe we lose a couple of days of sales or revenue, but the difference will be very small. It won't be significantly impacting compared on quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Africa milk procurement prices spiked due to delayed monsoon in Kenya; margins compressed but reversing with onset of rains
items.quote: Due to delayed monsoon, the procurement prices in the geographic increased significantly. Recently, some pressure on the margins. With the onset of monsoon, this has already begun to reverse in this quarter.

items.statement: Ghee consumer sales doubled from INR11 crores to INR21 crores YoY; paneer sales nearly doubled; curd and ice cream growing
items.quote: And ghee also, like farfetched consumption, last year we have done around INR11 crores, now we have done around INR21 crores. There is a substantial increase in the ghee consumer sale.

items.statement: Ghee pushed pan-India including North; ice cream focused in operating states leveraging own cold chain; paneer and consumer ghee driving VAP growth
items.quote: Ice cream, sir, we are doing ghee as a major push which we are now selling across pan-India, which we do a bit more in the northern Indian states also.

items.statement: No milk procurement from cooperatives in India; Africa procures at village association level
items.quote: No, we don't procure milk from cooperatives. In India, we don't procure milk from cooperatives. In Africa, we procure at a village level, what is called an association of people, not a cooperative.

items.statement: White Revolution 2.0 seen as positive for industry but no direct/indirect benefits to Dodla
items.quote: No, sir. No benefits, sir.

items.statement: On track to achieve 1,000 stores by March-25 and 2,000 stores by December-26
items.quote: broadly, yes, we are on track to achieve the 1,000 stores by March-25 and 2,000 stores by December-26, as per our guidance.

items.statement: Food delivery GOV growth guidance is 20%+ CAGR over next few years, not 30%
items.quote: We've always spoken about 20%+ GOV growth as guidance on a CAGR basis over the next few years.

items.statement: Quick commerce Adjusted EBITDA margin target of 4% to 5%
items.quote: the guidance we've given on margins is that we believe this business can reach 4% to 5% (Adjusted EBITDA margin).

items.statement: Board approved enabling resolution to raise up to $1 billion via QIP, subject to shareholder approval and market conditions
items.quote: The board has passed an enabling resolution to raise up to $1 billion, which is also subject to shareholder approval.

items.statement: Capex of INR 214 crore spent on 152 new stores and 7 new warehouses
items.quote: the bulk was spent on the store expansion that we have laid out in the letter. In addition to the 152 stores we opened, we also added seven new warehouses.

items.statement: Opened 152 stores and 7 warehouses in the quarter; expansion pace may be lumpy due to external dependencies
items.quote: In addition to the 152 stores we opened, we also added seven new warehouses.

items.statement: Store expansion focused on top 8 cities which remain underserved; non-Delhi NCR share of GOV now below 40%
items.quote: the share of Delhi NCR in our business continues to fall. We had given this data a couple of quarters ago when we had said that the share was around 47%; today, that number is less than 40%.

items.statement: Warehouse and new store costs captured above contribution line, causing margin drag
items.quote: It's above the contribution line, so everything is captured there. One of the reasons for the margin drag, as explained in the letter, is that when new stores are opened, we incur fixed costs

items.statement: AOVs similar across top 7-8 cities; some non-Delhi markets have higher AOV than Delhi
items.quote: If you look at the top seven-eight cities, the AOVs are similar, actually fairly similar. In fact, there could be one or two markets outside of Delhi where the AOV is higher than Delhi.

items.statement: Non-grocery categories (beauty, electronics, toys) growing but still early; focus on building infrastructure across categories
items.quote: the ones we launched over the past year such as beauty, electronics, and toys are still growing categories. We're still learning which use cases within these categories have further room for growth.

items.statement: SKU count will keep increasing as new categories requiring broad selection are added; no hard cap seen
items.quote: we expect the selection available to customers to keep increasing for the foreseeable future because we're adding categories that require a broad selection.

items.statement: Strategy remains to open largest possible dark stores; no shift to network of smaller specialized stores
items.quote: So far, our strategy remains the same. We have always opened the largest dark stores possible since day one, and our strategy is still to continue in the same direction.

items.statement: Quick commerce audience overlap with food delivery decreasing; QC appeals to broader demographic
items.quote: The overlap is decreasing over time because we're seeing that quick commerce is appealing to a much wider demographic than food delivery.

items.statement: Older QC cohorts show rising monthly GOV; new Delhi NCR customers joining at comparable AOVs
items.quote: The answer to both questions is yes.

items.statement: Focused on own business; not predicting competitive dynamics; growing 120-130% YoY at full sustainable capacity
items.quote: focused on market share at this point because our business is growing more than 120% to 130% year on year. That’s the capacity we have in terms of how much business we can service sustainably

items.statement: Fundraise not for discounting; have enough cash for that if needed; raise is to strengthen balance sheet
items.quote: We're not raising money to start discounting more. We need do what is right for the business first, and we don't think that discounting is going to help our business at this point in time.

items.statement: Current marketplace model prevents inventory ownership; no plan to change model but will evaluate as industry matures
items.quote: At this point, though, there is no plan to move away from our current business model

items.statement: Fixed costs rising due to marketing, server, people, infrastructure costs; high-growth businesses (QC, Going-out, Hyperpure) driving increase
items.quote: There is marketing cost, server cost, people cost, and infrastructure cost. Also, quick commerce, Going-out and Hyperpure are high-growth businesses right now, so some of that increase you see is because to that.

items.statement: Food delivery take rate fluctuation due to seasonality and restaurant mix changes; not a structural concern
items.quote: the take rate is just a fluctuation. And you're right, seasonality has a role to play here. It's also influenced by mix changes from quarter to quarter based on the types of restaurants people order from.

items.statement: Store opening process lumpy due to external dependencies (licenses, approvals); not linear
items.quote: This expansion could be lumpy because we don't control the entire process of opening a store. There's a lot of dependency on external bodies, licenses, and so on.

items.statement: Targets net debt of Rs 3,500-4,000 crore in next two quarters and below Rs 4,030 crore by end of FY25
items.quote: we are well on the way to kind of pa ring the debt to just about less than 4,000, between Rs. 3,500 crores to Rs. 4,000 crores in the next two quarters

items.statement: Targets 4% volume growth for full year FY25
items.quote: I am really looking at a 4% volume growth for the full year.

items.statement: Expects H2 volume growth in high single digits
items.quote: Certainly, I am targeting a high single digit growth, only in the coming October end and till 15th of November we will get a good sense of whether there is a little bit of a shift in momentum in the overall offtake.

items.statement: FY25 capex guidance of Rs 300-400 crore holds; may be Rs 20 crore shy of Rs 400 crore in H2
items.quote: Absolutely holds good. We may even be shy of maybe Rs. 400 crores by 20 odd crores in H2.

items.statement: FY26 capex guidance of Rs 900-1,000 crore for expansion
items.quote: and for Rs. 900 crores to Rs. 1,000 crores in FY ‘26. So, does that number hold? Jayakumar Krishnaswamy: Absolutely holds good

items.statement: Clinker capacity: East 28,000 TPD (9.5 mtpa), North 12,000 TPD (4 mtpa); Nimbol expansion to 6,000 TPD by Q4 FY25
items.quote: Overall clinker capacity for the Company would be 28,000 tons clinker in East per day, and North 12,000, 9.5 million tons in East, and 4 million tons in North.

items.statement: Odisha railway siding expected to commission by Q4 FY25
items.quote: The Odisha railway siding project is expected to be commissioned by Q4 FY '25.

items.statement: Project Bridge 2.0 delivered Rs 50/ton cost reduction in Q2; targets Rs 75/ton in H2
items.quote: H1, we are already trending at Rs. 50. We hope to see some upside on this figure. In H2, we should be looking at about Rs. 75 per ton, given the pace at which these various projects are moving.

items.statement: Blended fuel cost at lowest in 12 quarters at Rs 1.54/Mcal; power & fuel cost per ton down 3% QoQ
items.quote: Power and fuel costs per ton reduced by 3% quarter-on-quarter. The Company has reached the lowest blended fuel cost in the last 12 quarters at Rs. 1.54 per Mcal.

items.statement: Blended realization per ton fell 2.7% QoQ to Rs 5,362; industry prices down 4% QoQ
items.quote: Our Q2 blended realization is Rs. 5,362 as against Rs. 5,513

items.statement: October prices volatile with no firm trend; yoyo movement up and down
items.quote: A little bit of a next quarter, so for me to kind of tell anything about this quarter is not appropriate in this call. But suffice to say there has been an upward movement as well as a downward movement. So, it's kind of yoyo in it actually, literally there is no firm trend which is there which is kind of giving any great confidence to the industry that it will go one way up.

items.statement: Premium product share in trade segment hit record 43% in Q2 FY25

items.statement: Expects demand recovery from mid-November post-festivals and budget execution
items.quote: So, we would get growth from November, post-Pooja, post-Chhath pooja and Dussehra. So, come November, till November 15 till March I guess there should be a home stretch for the industry and certainly for us as well

items.statement: Bullet payments due in next 10 months; can refinance if needed

And even if somewhat muted demand is there, I think we always have the leverage of refinancing it, and it should not be a problem at all.

items.statement: Grid integration at Chhattisgarh units completed, enabling power cost savings

items.quote: We successfully commissioned a new clinker wagon loading system at Sonadih, which enables enhancement of clinker dispatch via rail, and is expected to aid in cost savings.

items.quote: we are seeing improving asset quality ever since we restarted doing the merchant loanbusiness in March and April, so we're seeing improving asset quality that's very encouraging. Our collection performance is also improving

items.quote: Standalone EBITDA is close to the breakeven, and that is what the strategy is. By design, the EBITDA levels are low in the Food and FMCG segment as the entire focus of the Company remains on the volume and topline growth.

items.quote: HoReCa channel, which is another alternate channel for us, which we started 2 years back is growing very fast. 40% plus kind of year -on-year growth and now contributing close to Rs. 500 crores of revenue basis last 12 months.
