But what will we do with the cash? I mean, it is better that for us to see a long-term horizon with the hospitality play and additional, which will be more beneficial than one time selling it.

items.statement: H2 FY25 revenue expected to increase 35% over H1 FY25, driving full-year FY25 revenue growth of 35% over FY24
items.quote: We do expect H2 revenue to increase 35% over H1 which shall drive full year revenue growth of 35%.

items.statement: Target to become debt-free by end of FY26 as capex intensity slows down
items.quote: We will turn debt-free again by end of FY '26 as capex intensity will slow down.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 10-12% once capacities and products are fully scaled up, gradually increasing to 11-12% by FY26 and early FY27
items.quote: EBITDA margin, the target is 10% to 12% overall, okay? Once we have all these capacities and products fully lined up and scaled up, till then, the margins will be under pressure because of high operating costs as we build up the capacities.

items.statement: Net working capital target of around 40 days, achievable if H2 performs with 35% revenue growth over H1
items.quote: Our target is around 40 days of net working capital, which consists of debtors, inventory and creditors, okay? And if second half performs as we are expecting today with 35% growth in revenue over H1, then these numbers will be easily achievable for working capital.

items.statement: Residual capex of INR250 crores to be funded from internal cash flows and residual capital infusion; capex to finish by June 2025
items.quote: Almost 250 crores of balance capex will be funded from internal cash flows and the residual capital infusion. With this, we will be nearly 3 lakh metric tons of annual capacity.

items.statement: H1 FY25 capex of INR65 crores; INR180-200 crores in H2 FY25 and balance in FY26
items.quote: So far we did INR65 crores in H1. The residual capex is INR250 crores. Out of that, INR180 crores, INR200 crores will come in second half and balance in FY '26.

items.statement: Annual capacity to reach nearly 3 lakh metric tons after current capex completion by June 2025
items.quote: With this, we will be nearly 3 lakh metric tons of annual capacity.

items.statement: Varanasi plant to add 40,000 tonnes capacity, production expected by March 2025, real contribution from Q1 FY26
items.quote: Varanasi segment is on track which will add up 40,000 tonnes to overall capacity. With this plan t, we will have pan -India presence

items.statement: Greenfield plant in Southern India construction to begin early FY26, funded from internal cash flows
items.quote: Sometime in the beginning of FY '26, we will start construction of a larger Greenfield plant in Southern India to further expand capacity. This capex shall also be funded from internal cash flows.

items.statement: Brownfield expansion of 28,500 tons for CPVC, uPVC pipes and silent pipes to be completed by June 2025
items.quote: So Brownfield is like some expansion of C PVC and uPVC pipes and one silent pipe what we are working on. So all this capex will be done by June 2025.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 8% in Q2 FY25; Apollo Pipes standalone at 9-10%, Kisan at 4-5%
items.quote: So although we are super aggressive in putting up capacities and super aggressive in gaining market share in Indian geographies, we don't see like margins remaining too much under pressure, right? So I mean, 100 bps, 150 bps leeway we need to perform with 25%, 30% volume CAGR, okay, in current market conditions when the stronger players are also performing pretty well, and we see competition from

items.statement: Gross margins improved due to contribution from PVC-O pipes
items.quote: One highlight is improvement in our gross margins due to contribution from PVC-O pipes.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 was one of the toughest quarters due to heavy monsoon, low government spending on water infrastructure, and 17% fall in PVC resin prices causing massive channel destocking
items.quote: What a quarter it has been. I would say one of the most tough quarters in the last few years. Things were slow right from the start of the quarter due to heavy monsoon and low government spending on water infrastructure. And then final nail in the coffin which was 17% fall in PVC resin prices during the first 2 months in the quarter a nd it took the whole industry by surprise and led to massive ch

items.statement: Government infra and agri contribution declined sharply by almost 30% in Q2 FY25; government HDPE share fell from peak 15% to less than 5%
items.quote: This quarter, it has sharply declined by almost 30% for this specific segment. And that's why you see a decline in Apollo Pipes' standalone volume data.

items.statement: HDPE pipe sales even worse in Q2 vs Q1; pickup expected only after assembly elections
items.quote: Even worse in Q2. And outlook, like we believe that only after assembly elections which are under way, there could be some pickup in this product.

items.statement: Green shoots visible in construction activity pickup; government thrust on water infrastructure expected to return after state elections
items.quote: Some green shoots are visible in terms of pickup in construction activity, we expect government's thrust on water infrastructure to return after some important state elections are over.

items.statement: O-PVC contribution in Q2 was single-digit percentage; expected to contribute 7-8% of revenue by FY26 with three lines operational
items.quote: O-PVC is like the 3 lines should be contributing 7%, 8% of my revenue, okay, by FY '26 by the time we have like full 12 months of 3 lines operational.

items.statement: Around 5-6 state approvals for O-PVC pipes already obtained; more in process
items.quote: Around 5 to 6 state approvals are already there with us and we are in the process of, you can say, likely in other states to get the product approved.

items.statement: Inventory loss in Q2 FY25 was very mild, under INR5 crores, due to low starting inventory and adjusted raw material purchases
items.quote: The inventory loss will be very mild, Sneha. The reason is that we started the quarter with low inventory levels, right? And once we took a sense that the sales are going to slow down because of the external factors, so we also planned the raw material purchase accordingly. This helped us to nullify massive inventory losses unlike our other competitors.

items.statement: Antidumping duty on PVC resin imports rumored in $50-250 range but no certain date; QCO implementation extended to December 2024
items.quote: Bhavin, there has been rumors regarding this PVC antidumping for a quite long time, you can say for the last 3, 4 months. People are anticipating that this antidumping can come any day. But right now, there is no such update. Of course, it has to come. It's in the process, but we don't have exact dates. And it should come, you can say, in the near future, but there is no certain date for that. And

items.statement: Receivables at 20-22 days, expected to come under 20 days with higher H2 sales
items.quote: Receivables are already around 20, 22 days, okay? So yes, I mean there would be -- I mean, again, on days basis, they look high, right? But when we will finish the year with higher sales in second half, they will come under 20 days.

items.statement: H2 FY25 operating cash flow generation expected at INR50-60 crores; plus INR100 crores from warrant conversion to fund capex
items.quote: Now in H2, the capex intensity will be even higher, b ut what will change is number one, the EBITDA growth in second half, we expect INR50 crores, INR60 crores of operating cash flow generation in the second half. Then there is a new capital -- I mean, residual capital from warrant conversion, which will come of around INR100 crores

items.statement: Housing/building material now >60% of revenue vs 35% three years ago; agriculture/infra below 40%
items.quote: As Apollo, you would see last 3, 4 years, we used to be like 35% housing and 65% agriculture. We have been tracking our company long enough. Today, we are proud to say that we are 60% -- more than 60% housing, and below 40% agriculture, right?

items.statement: CPVC >15% of volume; fittings similar contribution ramping up; water tanks ramping up month-on-month; O-PVC 3 lines to contribute 7-8% by FY26
items.quote: One is CPVC, which is more than 15%. Then the fittings, right? Again, it's the similar contribution level, which is ramping up, right, our capacity in Varanasi and some brownfield expansion for some of the products in the existing capacity.

items.statement: Strategy remains 25-30% revenue CAGR with margins at Apollo ~10%, Kisan ~5-6%, consolidated ~8-9%; confident in viability despite competition
items.quote: So strategy is that 25%, 30% revenue growth, right, with margins like at Apollo level, we are about 10% and Kisan, near about 5%, 6%. On a lender basis, we do 8%, 9%. So this strategy remains as we have been articulating for last many quarters, and we are confident that this is a very viable strategy.

items.statement: Channel partners afraid of restocking, evaluating PVC resin price movement daily before deciding to restore inventory
items.quote: The channel partners are still afraid of going for restocking. They are evaluating the situation day by day. I mean there is some confidence because of a slight pickup in the construction activity. But in terms of stocking, they would like to look at the PVC resin price movement for next few days, and then they would take a call whether to restore or maintain low inventory levels, which are curren

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance maintained at 10-15% for FY25; bottom line guidance also 10-15%
items.quote: We do think that, the guidance that we've given for about 10 to 15% on the top line stands, as is the guidance on the bottom line for the 10 to 15% also stands

items.statement: Freight division expected to reach 7-8% to 10% top line growth and last year's bottom line in H2 FY25
items.quote: We think that we should get to around closer to 7- 8% to 10% top line, and we should reach the last year's bottom line, numbers as well

items.statement: Full year capex revised to Rs 300-350 crore from earlier Rs 350-375 crore; ship advance of Rs 70-75 crore pending
items.quote: I think we are , as I mentioned, that my comments may be 300 to 350 is what we are looking at this year

items.statement: Secondhand ship acquisition not on horizon and not part of budget
items.quote: We do not have visibility yet on the secondhand ship. Again, thank you for joining and I am happy to answer any questions

items.statement: Seaways EBITDA margin guided at 25-35% range, down from current 40% but stable
items.quote: I think 25 to 30 to 35% type of EBITDA is still reasonable, but I would, I would warrant any kind of guess right now on this because it has remained a little bit, perplexing

items.statement: Supply chain margin slightly weaker due to investments in new warehousing contracts
items.quote: The margin structure is, is the same, It's the same as last year, slightly weaker actually, on the Ebit side. This is some investment that we are doing in the new contracts we've got in on the warehousing side

items.statement: Auto sector production cuts started earlier than usual; two-wheeler sales robust but four-wheeler and tractor weak; MSME credit offtake low
items.quote: production cuts in auto sector has also started, It has started a little earlier than anticipated

items.statement: Festival stocking 5-10% better than last year; Seaways benefited from ships shifting to international routes
items.quote: This year we expected we saw that stocking was slightly better, maybe 5-10% better than last year in terms of the festival stocking

items.statement: Supply chain business has strong pipeline on warehousing side; expected to become largest business by FY26
items.quote: We are seeing as as I have been saying that we should get to this business will be the largest business for us in FY 26

items.statement: Cold chain joint venture revenue up 32%; bought 75 new trucks last year; major storage capacity expansion underway
items.quote: Similarly cold chain joint has gone up by 32%. Margins are a little tight, but because of the investment we've made into new trucks, we bought 75 new trucks last year

items.statement: Opened 32 branches in H1 FY25 (15 in Q1, 17 in Q2); target 40% branch network expansion next financial year
items.quote: We are continuously increasing our branch network, We have opened 32 branches. The target to get to 40% next year, next financial year is strong

items.statement: No dry docks scheduled until last 10 days of FY25; full capacity available for Seaways until then
items.quote: But now the next dry dock is only at the end of the financial year that to towards the, last ten days of the financial year. Otherwise we are clear for the full year now

items.statement: Receivables increased proportionally with revenue; tighter credit from large customers delaying payments; expected to resolve in H2
items.quote: Some of the large customers are just trying to withhold the payments, not giving on the time. So I think these are some temporary issues which I think will be resolved in the next, the next half year

items.statement: Company remains net debt free; debt of ~Rs 100 crore is truck-related and cheaper than using cash
items.quote: Buyback was about 160 crores plus tax, debt is about 100 odd crores, which is, essentially all, truck related debts, which are cheaper than using cash

items.statement: Buyback of Rs 160 crore plus tax completed; dividend payout ratio increased from 125% to 175% (approx 20% of annual profit)
items.quote: The dividend payout ratio increased too, from 125% to 175%. This is in line with, overall thought process of about, roughly about 20% our payout for the year

items.statement: Freight division facing competitive pricing pressure from listed players entering express/LTL space and driving down rates to utilize capacity
items.quote: Companies who have, I guess have been listed also, who've just got into some kind of express business and they are not exactly express, but they are in between express and LTL and they are trying to push down the pricing

items.statement: No blanket price hike announcement planned; cost escalations passed through 1:1 in contracts for wages and fuel
items.quote: it cannot be an announcement that we would, like, increase throughout all the contracts, probably we may not have that kind of outlook

items.statement: Supply chain auto exposure changing very slowly; EV companies and spare parts providing growth; no significant mix shift expected in 2-3 years
items.quote: the mix is, is slowly, very, very slowly changing but you would not see any significant change in the next, 2 or 3 years

items.statement: Quick commerce fulfillment (warehouse to dark stores) growing; not doing dark store management or last mile; taking wait-and-watch approach
items.quote: Not even dark store management from the fulfillment warehouse to the dark stores, the management of the fulfillment warehouse and then the delivery to the dark stores is, that's all we do

items.statement: Regional/unorganized players always present; new listed entrants in express/LTL pressuring pricing; FTL less vulnerable due to pan-India network and local sourcing needs
items.quote: regional players and local players, unorganized players have always been there. But what has added on, are some Companies who have, I guess have been listed also

items.statement: Seaways Q2 revenue up 22%, bottom line up 65%; EBITDA margins 40%+; gross margins 50%+
items.quote: I mentioned Seaways has done, very well, with a 22% top line increase on the in the quarter, as well as our 65% increase on the bottom line

items.statement: Standalone H1 revenue growth 10.9%, console 11.5%; standalone profit up 25%, console up 16%
items.quote: Net net on the standalone basis, 10.9% on the console level for, sorry, on the standalone for H1, and, similar numbers, about 11.5% on the console level

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions fluid; international freight rates easing possibly indicating global recession; Seaways performance unpredictable
items.quote: the geopolitical tensions have not eased. However, international shipping and freight rates have eased a little bit. I think that could be a little bit sensitive to what is happening with, perhaps an indication of global recession

items.statement: Credit slowdown and higher interest rates causing payment delays from corporates; receivables elevated
items.quote: Interest rates are starting to play on corporates where they are, not paying on time, I guess, because they are finding some areas of reducing cost

items.statement: ULIP integration ahead of competitors with 7-8 APIs integrated (Vahan, FASTag, FIOS, European APIs); participated in ULIP hackathon
items.quote: Our company is one of the only companies that has really integrated almost 7 or 8 APIs from Europe directly into our systems

items.statement: Coastal shipping seen as major growth area; India at 6% coastal modal share vs China 20%+; 7000 km coastline; investing in new and secondhand ships
items.quote: a country like China has 20 plus percent of its movement happening through coastal trade , We had 6%. So and we have a very, very large 7000 kilometer coastline

items.statement: Investing in bench strength for manpower to support new warehousing contracts before revenue starts
items.quote: a little stretch on the margins, because of that, bench strength that we have to create for manpower as well as for setting up the equipment

items.statement: Expect margin improvement starting Q4 FY25 and continuing each quarter thereafter to reach 15-16.5% range over 4-6 quarters
items.quote: But we are very confident that starting 4Q, you will see the margin improving. And over the next subsequent quarters, every quarter, you will see margin improvement going forward.

items.statement: Expect better TCV performance in Q3 and Q4 FY25 compared to H1 FY25
items.quote: I strongly feel that in our Q3 and Q4, we will have a better TCV performance than what we have seen in the first half year.

items.statement: Expect Life Sciences vertical to return to growth in a couple of quarters
items.quote: Our Life Sciences business has been a struggle. I believe it will continue to be soft for a couple of more quarters before we turn the corner there.

items.statement: Expect effective tax rate for full year FY25 in range of 25% to 26%
items.quote: We do expect the ETR for the full year to be in the range of 25% to 26%.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin at 12.1%, down from 14.7% in Q1 (which included Rs 222M one-time benefit); like-to-like drop ~100 bps
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the quarter was at $19.7 million versus $23.4 million in the previous quarter and the EBITDA margin stood at about 12.1%.

items.statement: Salary hike in Q3 FY25 to dent margins by ~150 bps; Q3 margins muted, improvement from Q4
items.quote: So, really, salary hike will dent our margins by 150 basis points further, but obviously a part of it, we will definitely recover operationally. So, Q3 will be a muted quarter from a margin standpoint, but Q4 onwards, you will see a clear margin improvement.

items.statement: Margin pressure from consolidation deals: ~50 bps from onsite-heavy mix, ~50 bps from pricing flexibility
items.quote: So, of that 1 percentage point, 100 basis points drop, probably half of it will be because our revenues have come more on-site, which by nature is lower margin business as a part of the consolidation build, and half of it is because of the pricing flexibility.

items.statement: Demand environment unchanged; client budgets on 'hold and wait' pattern due to US election uncertainty; green shoots visible but clarity may come only by year-end
items.quote: Our client budgets have not gone down, but it is on a 'hold and wait' pattern. So, we will have to see how our client spending goes forward with the election looming in the U.S., which is our biggest market. It is a wait and watch for our clients.

items.statement: H1 FY25 TCV signings ~$300M, lower than prior year; no significant deals lost; decision-making pushed to Q3/Q4; pipeline improving with ~50% deals in net-new or existing-new
items.quote: If you look at our half-year performance on deal flow, we have delivered about $300 million worth of signing. That is obviously lower than what we delivered last year. But that is not such a big concern for us at this point in time, because we have not lost any deals.

items.statement: Renewals concentrated in H2 (Q3/Q4); no renewal concerns indicated; pricing on renewals under negotiation
items.quote: Our renewal cycle essentially comes in more in the 3rd quarter and the 4th quarter of the financial year. So, our renewals will be much more than it is in the first and second quarter.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 revenue $163.3M (Rs 1,368 crore), up 2.6% QoQ USD, 3.1% QoQ INR, 3.2% YoY USD, 4.5% YoY INR; broad-based growth across verticals and service lines
items.quote: Our consolidated revenues grew 2.6% in dollar terms to 163.3 million. In rupee terms, it has been Rs 1,368 crore, a sequential growth of 3.1%, and a year-on-year growth of 4.5%.

items.statement: Top 5, 10, 20 accounts grew QoQ 3.9%, 2.4%, 2.3% respectively; contribution 36.7%, 52.5%, 64.9%
items.quote: I am happy to say that the revenues of our top 5, top 10, and top 20 accounts have grown quarter-on-quarter by 3.9%, 2.4%, and 2.3%, respectively. As a result, our top 5, 10, and 20 accounts now contribute 36.7%, 52.5%, and 64.9%, respectively to our total revenues.

items.statement: Manufacturing and E&U verticals up 4.7% QoQ each; BFSI up 1.4% QoQ; Life Sciences weak; ERP up 4.3% QoQ; Digital & Data up 6.6% QoQ; Infra down QoQ due to base effect
items.quote: Amongst our verticals, both Manufacturing and E&U were up by 4.7% each quarter-on-quarter, while BFSI grew by about 1.4% quarter-on-quarter. The Life Sciences vertical remained weak during the quarter under review.

items.statement: Onsite revenue ratio increased to ~51% in Q2 due to consolidation deals; offshore revenue declined due to some engagements ending
items.quote: Yes, you are absolutely right Ravi, because of the shift in the onsite ratio that we have seen in this quarter moving up to almost 51%.

items.statement: Continue investing in capabilities (Digital, Data, Rest of World, Life Sciences turnaround); investments to deliver returns; no capex number disclosed
items.quote: We will continue to make investments as necessary, but we are now focused on driving returns from this investment.

items.statement: Operating cash flow $12.9M; quarterly collections $176M (highest in 6 quarters); DSO 58 days, up QoQ due to collections shifting to early October; expect Q3 DSO to normalize
items.quote: Operating cash flow for the quarter was at about $12.9 million on the back of the sequential improvement in our quarterly collections during Quarter 2, which stood at $176 million. This has been the highest in the last six quarters.

items.statement: Board recommended interim dividend of Rs 2.50 per share
items.quote: As you would have observed, the Board today has recommended an interim dividend of Rs. 2.50 per share.

items.statement: Salary hike planned for Q3 FY25 impacting margins by ~150 bps
items.quote: We are going ahead with our salary hike in quarter 3. So, really, salary hike will dent our margins by 150 basis points further.

items.statement: Win ratio 30-32%, target 35-38%; no significant deal lost to competition; pipeline improving
items.quote: Our win ratios are anywhere ranging between the 30% to 32% range at this point in time. Clearly, there is an opportunity to improve the win ratio. Ideally, we want our win ratios to be 35% to 38%.

items.statement: Digital & Data business grown to ~$250-280M annualized run rate
items.quote: Our Digital and Data business has also grown to become almost $250-$280 million, right?

items.statement: US election uncertainty causing client 'hold and wait' spending pattern; furloughs in Q3 may mute growth
items.quote: Overall, while we do see some green shoots, there might not be too much clarity till the end of the year as things unfold in terms of whether our customers will continue to focus on cost take-outs or start investing in the transformation projects.

items.statement: $100M deal ramp-up on schedule; no structural issues with clients or execution
items.quote: First of all, the $100 million deal is on schedule. And one more thing I want to state, Dipesh. Structurally, there is no issue, neither with our clients nor with us.

items.statement: Margin aspiration remains 15-16% over time, but not achievable in next two quarters; Q3 FY25 expected as absolute bottom due to salary hike, with margin uptick from Q4 FY25 onwards over next four quarters
items.quote: Now, can I get to a 15% margin two quarters out ? The answer is no , but over period of time , is that my aspiration? It absolutely is, and we will drive towards that.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 will be absolute margin bottom due to salary hike; Q4 FY25 onwards margins will improve over next four quarters as deals mature
items.quote: One, after Q3, which will be our absolute bottom because of the salary hi ke, Q4 onwards we will start improving margins and Q4 , Q1, Q2, Q3 the next four quarters you will see our margin uptick coming in

items.statement: Digital and Data business grown to $250-280 million, helping balance margins from vendor consolidation deals
items.quote: I don't know if you realize this , but I am sure you do , our Digital and Data business has also grown to become almost $250-$280 million, right?

items.statement: Subcontracting costs expected to decrease as consolidation deals move work from onsite to offshore and replace subcontractors with own employees
items.quote: Yes, that's the expectation as we start replacing these people with our own employees . Yes, we would expect this cost to come down, Sandeep.

items.statement: Project Optimus internal tech transformation will contribute to cost takeout over next three-four quarters
items.quote: Project Optimus that Kamini spoke about will contribute over the next three-four quarters to cost takeout.

items.statement: Deal pipeline currently 50% transformation deals and 50% vendor consolidation deals; transformation deals include marquee E&U and BFSI projects
items.quote: So, currently, the deals that we have on table is really 50/50 . We have got 50% transformation deals. We have got 50% vendor consolidation deals .

items.statement: H1 FY25 deal signings only $300 million; need >$550 million in H2 to show annual growth; targeting $250 million per quarter in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Our dream is to deliver growth on order book even this year, though it is going to be a very tall order because in the first half year, we have delivered only 300 millions of signings and I really need to deliver more than 550 million in the next two quarters even to show growth.

items.statement: Vendor consolidation deal sizes range $10-30 million with shorter tenures of 1-3 years due to market uncertainty
items.quote: these deal sizes range from anywhere between $10 million to $30 million. But there is a small change, Anmol. You know, in today's world, the long-tenure deals are pretty much over

items.statement: Deal signings delayed due to customer wait-and-watch approach ahead of US election; transformation projects expected back on table ~6 months post-election
items.quote: The real estate that is our current real estate, I can't talk about the market in general, but in our current real estate, our deal signings are getting delayed. Now, not that our customers that we serve are in financial trouble or anything. I mean, they are very strong financially, but it's a wait and watch model in our customer real estate in terms of how the election results will pan out.

items.statement: Healthcare vertical muted for 2-3 quarters due to project completion timing, not sector or client issues; strong bounce back expected in couple of quarters
items.quote: But you give it a couple of quarters, you will see the healthcare bounce back very, very strongly. Now why has this happened? It is not a sector issue or a client specific issue. It is only because the real estate that we have, the projects that we sign.

items.statement: Focus on cutting long tail of customers further beyond original optimal level to redeploy human capital for growth
items.quote: My original thought was that we were at an optimal level, but with the market uncertainty and with the way things are happening in the world, I feel we have more possibility to cut down the tail and so the team has a plan in place to reduce the tail even further.

items.statement: Sales and support headcount fluctuations due to Project Optimus ramp-up and support staff optimization via automation
items.quote: The reason the headcounts went up is, a couple of quarters we have spoken about our investment in our tech transformation internally within Birlasoft, w hat we call ed Project Optimus, where we had actually started ramping headcount on that project and that continues. The reduction this quarter that has happened has been in other areas where we have started optimizing some of our support staff in

items.statement: Onsite mix increased to 50-51% from 46-48% due to consolidation deal ramp-ups and pass-through revenue changes; aim to improve offshore ratios over time for margin improvement
items.quote: If you look at our previous quarter s trend, I think the differential would be we were operating at about 46 %, 48% levels, and that's probably what's gone up to about 50%-51% that you see this time.

items.statement: Vendor consolidation deals face pricing pressure and margin dilution in medium term but expected to recover as work moves offshore and efficiencies improve
items.quote: The vendor consolidation deals are also not margin dilutive. It is only the timing issue that when you do a vendor consolidation deal, you take over people, etc. For the medium term, you will see pricing pressures and margin pressures.

items.statement: Management acknowledges unpredictability will persist for a couple of quarters due to market volatility, but aims for predictability over next 6-9 quarters
items.quote: But Manik, I will also say this. Even in the future, will there be a couple of quarters where there will be a little bit of unpredictability? It will happen, because the markets are very volatile. But our job now going forward is to be very predictable over the next 6, 7, 8, 9 quarters

items.statement: FY24 TCV grew only 1% YoY; H1 FY25 signings $300 million; net new and existing new business showing reasonable traction
items.quote: Last year, if you look at it, our order signings were just 1% growth over the previous year, FY '24 over FY '23. So, clearly, that was a cause of concern.

items.statement: Annuity business statistics to be disclosed in a couple of quarters as part of revenue quality improvement from staff augmentation to annuity work
items.quote: But give us a couple of quarters. Then we will clearly call out in terms of what will be our annuity business be, which will be a part of our quality of revenue, right?

items.statement: Continued investment in Project Optimus internal tech transformation and sales (general and specialist) despite support staff optimization
items.quote: Like Angan said, I think we continue to invest in sales, both general and specialist sales. So, I don't think that's an area of investment that we would cut back on.

items.statement: Business growth guidance for FY25 is 10%; achieved 9.42% YoY as of September 30
items.quote: The whole financial year we have given a guidance of business growth at 10%. As against that, 9.42% we have grown up to September 30th.

items.statement: Gross NPA guidance for March FY25 is 3.5%; currently at 3.73% as of September
items.quote: Our Gross NPA has come down from 4.14% to 3.73% as against our next March level guidance of 3.5%.

items.statement: Net NPA guidance for March FY25 is 1.10%; currently at 0.99% as of September
items.quote: Our Net NPA, next March level guidance w e had given 1.10, but already we are at below 1% i.e. 0.99

items.statement: PCR guidance for March FY25 is 90%; currently at 90.89% as of September
items.quote: Our PCR we had given a guidance of 90% at the next March level , but we are already touching the 91% at 90.89%.

items.statement: Slippage ratio guidance for March FY25 is 1.3%; currently at 1% as of September
items.quote: Slippage ratio also we had given a guidance of 1.3% for March , but we alr eady could successfully control slippages and we have touched that 1% slippage

items.statement: Credit cost guidance for FY25 is 1.10%; currently at 0.97% as of September
items.quote: Our credit cost slightly increased quarter-on-quarter from 0.9 to 0.97, but still it is much below the guidance that we have given at 1.10.

items.statement: RoE guidance for FY25 is 18%; currently at 20.44% as of September

items.statement: EPS guidance for FY25 is Rs 16.40; achieved Rs 17.41 as of September

items.statement: RoA guidance for FY25 is 1%; currently at 1.05% as of September

items.statement: Gross NPA declined to 3.73% from 4.14% QoQ, down 103 bps YoY
items.quote: Our Gross NPA has come down below 4% i.e. June Quarter it was 4.14%. Now it has come down to 3.73% with year-on-year decline of 103 basis points.

items.quote: This increase in the credit co st is from 0.9 to 0.97 is not because of any of the quality. We have provided additional more than 500 crores in existing NPA accounts to strengthen our PCR coverage ratio.

items.quote: Already, e arlier also I shared with you , 15% we already provided , which is a round 560 crores.

items.quote: In our bank, the unsecured loans in the RAM sector, especially retail se ctor, is only approximately 18,000 crores.

items.quote: Slippage breakup is total 2,300 crores. Out o f that, 1,000 crores is from MSME, 800 crores from agriculture, 500 crores from retail.

items.statement: Housing loan NPA uptick due to one-time system rectification on joint borrower slippage; no serious concern
items.quote: We have allowed such type of things all into the NPA. That is why there is a slight increase showing in that, otherwise there is no serious concern on that.

items.quote: In NPI there is a reduction. Sequentially if you look at that, our total NP I is around 5,900 crores, and last June it was around 6,000 odd. It has come down slightly. And there is no further slippages in the NPI. The write back is 72 crores.

items.quote: Our restructured book, RF1, RF2 and all together, now it is 14,000 crores. Out of that, 4,500 crores under NPA and 9,500 crores is under standard asset.

items.quote: First time in the last three quarters, CASA has shown uptick on growth compared to sequentially the quarter-on-quarter. June Quarter to now it has improved by almost 28 basis po ints. It was 30.98%, now i t is 31.27%.

items.quote: Our NIM slightly has come down compared to the peer banks. It come down from 2.9 to 2.88. Though there is a lot of pressure on the cost of deposits, but we could manage this because of efficient management of o ur resources.

items.statement: Yield on corporate advances improved from 7.12% to 8.48% over three quarters; shed Rs 35,000-40,000 cr low-yielding corporate loans
items.quote: Earlier just three quarters back, our yield on advances, especially on the corporate sector used to be 7.12%. Now it has increased it to 8.48%.

items.quote: Under such circumstances, expecting a crossing of the NIM for 3% in the near quarters, in one to two quarters, it may not be possible.

items.quote: Sir, if you look at the last consecutive five quart ers, more or less, we are able to manage around 1 ,500 crores in that ; 1500 to 1600 crores every quarter. The same tempo will continue.

items.quote: Now unlike other banks , we have not shred 5% of our HTM which we are entitled to. So, we will use that amount for our profits because yields are softening.

items.statement: Global advances grew 9.53% YoY to Rs 10.11 lakh crore; domestic advances up Rs 35,000 cr QoQ
items.quote: Our global advances also have grown at 9.53% and stood at 10.11 crores.

items.quote: Our RAM credit has grown at 11.54%. If you see , sequentially, our RAM credit growth in the current quarter itself is 4.5%, contributed by the retail credit grown at 31.27% and stood at Rs 1 .94 lakh crore.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio Rs 1.65 lakh cr; new metro gold product ~Rs 28,000 cr (up from Rs 19,000 cr QoQ); yield 9.15% (10 bps above 1-year MCLR)
items.quote: Actually, as on date, whole entire bank, our gold portfolio was 1,65,000 crores. This retail growth , with the product what we launched , is around 28,000 crores.

items.statement: Education loans ~Rs 16,000 cr, growing double-digit; mortgage loans also in Other PL
items.quote: Educational loan is almost 16,000 crores, ma'am. That is also growing at double -digit growth.

items.quote: Our LCR is 130.55 i.e. 131%. And even the RBI new guidelines if you implement it, it may impact around 10 to 11 bas is point s. So, we will be comfortable at around 120%.

items.statement: Canara Robeco AMC IPO scheduled for Q4 FY25
items.quote: As on date it is scheduled in the 4th Quarter, sir. Still we believe that it may happen in the 4th Quarter only.

items.statement: Gold loan process digitized end-to-end from mid-September; loans disbursed in 10-15 minutes; centralized LTV control
items.quote: middle o f September onwards we have digitized this entire process end-to-end. So that has helped us in meet ing the customer requirements in a faster mode. Nowaday s, we are giving loans within the 10 to 15 minutes

items.quote: NCLT resolutions of quarter, total together we got around 549 crores. Out of that , some accounts are from liquidation. But these are all not more than 100 crores e ach.

items.statement: Annual recovery + technical write-off expected ~Rs 4,000-5,000 cr; will continue to support balance sheet
items.quote: I believe , that whatever we are shown in the last one year or two years , similarly, we are expecting that every year the r ecovery and technical written off is around 4,000 to 5,000.

items.statement: EBITDA margin to improve 100-125 bps annually for next 3 years, reaching late teens
items.quote: As we have been guiding in earlier calls also that we will improve our margin every year by 150 basis points or so. So, over the last year, we will be doing much better than that. And thereafter, also for the next 3 years, we will continue to improve our margin by 100 to 125 basis and that's how we will reach to the late teens margin in 3 years' time.

items.statement: Prestige & Above volume grew 12.6% YoY in Q2 FY25
items.quote: We achieved a 12.6% growth in the Prestige & Above category, along with a sequential improve ment in EBITDA margins

items.quote: Increase in net debt over March '24 is primarily due to the cyclical buildup of the inventory and higher receivables in certain states.

items.quote: Going forward, our focus will be on improving profitability along with cash flow generation and a more efficient working capital management resulting into debt reduction.

items.quote: No. I think we will stick to our guidance of 15% to 20% growth. And if you see, realization from raw material basically has gone down by 4% in this quarter. That also has resulted in lower revenue. But overall, we expect 15% volume growth for the full year.

items.statement: Confident of 15-20% year-on-year growth for next year as well
items.quote: Yes, we are confident of 15% to 20% year-on-year growth also.

items.statement: Aluminum forging capacity of 3,000 tonnes per annum approved at Rs 57.5 Crores in Jamshedpur for EV segment, fully backed by 5-year firm order
items.quote: The Board of Directors has also approved an investment of Rs. 57.5 Crores to establish an aluminum forging capability around 3,000 metric tonnes per annum at Jamshedpur, primarily to serve the EV segment. This will significantly enhance our presence in EV market.

items.quote: I think by next year FY '26 we will be having almost 60,000 tonnes of casting capacities , and we are going to sell casting both domestic and international.

items.quote: Raghu, right now the market is flattish. We are growing and we are doing exceptionally well because of our marketing has been able to penetrate new segments and new customers in North America. And that's the reason we are growing.

items.quote: Against the Rs. 1,522 Crores orders, we have Ramkrishna Forgings Limited 24 October, 2024 received from North America orders worth Rs. 1,475 Crores, in which we have secured Rs. 1,312 Crores from the auto segment and from the non -auto segment we have fetched orders worth Rs. 163 Crores. items.statement: Internal vision for 15-20% revenue from EV/hybrid vehicles by FY27; on track to achieve

items.statement: Vande Bharat bogie frame prototypes to be submitted this month; bulk production post approval; Rs 270 Crores orders to execute over FY26-27

items.statement: Ramkrishna Titagarh JV on track; wheel production and delivery to railways to start in Q4 FY26
