items.statement: Paints business targets Rs 400-450 crore revenue in FY26 and Rs 600 crore by FY27 with break-even
items.quote: And next year we have a plan as a ramp up, next year we have a plan of about 400 crores top line 400 to 450 crores and 600 crores by FY27 where we should be having a break even.

items.statement: Capex target maintained at Rs 1,800-1,900 crore for FY25 with Rs 750 crore spent in H1
items.quote: We have spent 750 crores till now out of the target of 1,800-1,900 crores.

items.statement: 6 million ton expansion at Panna on track for commissioning by end of Q3 or beginning of Q4 FY26
items.quote: As regards the project, the 6 million tons expansion work is at a good speed and we are confident that we would be able to commission as per the expected lines either by end of third quarter or beginning of fourth quarter FY26.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin at 11.7% vs 18.7% in Q1 and 18% YoY due to lower volumes and one-time costs
items.quote: EBITDA margins was 11.7% for the quarter as against 18.7% in the previous quarter and 18% in the previous year.

items.statement: Unit production cost expected to reduce by Rs 50 per ton each in Q3 and Q4 FY25 with fuel price softening
items.quote: With the fuel prices softening and all, we should see an impact of about Rs. 50 coming up in each of the remaining two quarters.

items.statement: Grey cement realization flat QoQ despite price pressure due to favorable product mix and cutting low-retention volumes
items.quote: All these factors have resulted that though the prices were under pressure but on an average with a mix, we are not seeing any fall in the realization per ton.

items.statement: October grey cement prices marginally up vs Q2 average with potential for further increases post-Diwali
items.quote: Q2 average marginally up. But we have to really see this is, whatever some prices had increased but not across but in the north and all, so marginally up as compared to average of Q2. But we have to see, how we are able to increase upon some more pricing in coming days post Diwali maybe.

items.statement: AFR cost increased due to fuel-price linkage; renegotiating to maintain gap with pet coke prices
items.quote: The kilocalorie cost has gone up during this quarter because one the AFR cost has increased. So, we are seeing that there is a fall in the fuel prices, marginal fall. But the usage of AFR, the AFR supplies, the AFR cost has increased whatever contracted quantities which we had. Now we have again renegotiating. Actually, AFR pricing is also linked to the fuel pricing. So, what they do they always l

items.statement: Toshali limestone long-term supply agreement discussions restarted with Odisha government; response expected by December
items.quote: We had a meeting and we had discussed with him and for a long term arrangement and we had a meeting with the Chief Secretary also. I think we should get some their proposal whatever we have submitted their response sometime in the month of December or so.

items.statement: Gross debt Rs 4,664 crore, cash Rs 1,620 crore, net debt Rs 2,582 crore as of Sep 2024; net debt/EBITDA 1.6x
items.quote: The gross debt as on 30th September was 4,664 crores as against 4,592 crores as on March. The cash balance as on 30 th September was 1,620 crores as against 2,011. Net debt was 2,582 crores as against 3,044 crores. The net debt to EBITDA was 1.6x as against 1.29x and the net debt to equity was 0.56x as against 0.48x.

items.statement: Thermal substitution rate dropped to 13% in Q2 due to kiln maintenance and inclusion of 4 new plants in SBTi reporting scope
items.quote: So, see you would see that Q2 being a maintenance period for all the kilns, so that has resulted in a sharp decline. Management: And secondly, Navin there is one more factor. Actually, earlier we were covering only 9 plants out of the 13. Now we have got the SBTi approval for covering all the 13 plants. So, this data is actually revised for the 13 plants now. That is also a reason for the reductio

items.statement: Rail share in logistics mix at 9% in Q2 FY25; blended cement mix at 70%
items.quote: The rail-road, rail was only 9%.

items.statement: Pet coke constituted 75% of fuel mix by heat in Q2 FY25
items.quote: By heat pet coke was around 75% and balance is the alternate fuel and the imported.

items.statement: Logistics savings of Rs 22/ton achieved; targeting Rs 45-50/ton exit rate by March 2025
items.quote: I think we have already been able to factor in about Rs. 22 of logistic savings. And we expect that by March our exit should be around Rs. 45 to 50 in case of logistic.

items.statement: Total cost savings target of Rs 150-200/ton over FY25-26; Rs 60-75/ton exit rate targeted by March 2025
items.quote: I think if we look at an exit by FY25, we should definitely have an exit of between Rs. 60 to 75. So, Rs. 60 which is a saving which would have accrued we should be seeing that saving in FY26 and other savings will come in FY26 which will pile up to about Rs. 150 to 200.

items.statement: Won two coal blocks (Shahdol and Mahan) in Madhya Pradesh; targeting commissioning 12-15 months ahead of FY29 deadline for first block and 30 months for second
items.quote: We have won two coal blocks, one is Shahdol and one is Mahan, both in Madhya Pradesh. So, the first block is a smaller block, that was that block we have to work from the beginning. The vesting agreement has been done and now we have the full team on board for the block and we have initiated a plan to start work to do the mining lease and the mining evaluation and everything, procurement of land s

items.statement: Coal blocks expected to reduce fuel cost to Rs 1/100 NCV vs current Rs 1.5-1.6 for linkage coal
items.value: Rs. 1 max, outer limit Rs. 1.10 paisa
items.quote: Today we are getting linkage fuel at about Rs. 1.50 paisa to Rs. 1.60 paisa per 100 NCV. This would come at a much lower around Rs. 1 max, outer limit Rs. 1.10 paisa.

items.statement: Demand weakness in North and South regions during Q2; Central India relatively stable
items.quote: See the demand slip was not so much felt in the central India. There was a dip in demand definitely in the north and the southern part.

items.statement: October demand better than September; government spending expected to pick up from November
items.quote: October is definitely much better than what September is. But some of the government spending that has to really come in full-fledged and I think that should come from November onwards.

items.statement: Asian Paints holds ~30% putty market share vs 24% for Birla and 22% for JK Cement; aggressive pricing with hidden discounts continues
items.quote: Asian Paints with all that they have already taken the #1 position in the putty field. They have become the largest player of though they don't have any production facilities. But they are still the largest seller of putty with a market share of close to about 30% as against 24% for Birla and 22% for us.

items.statement: Extended 70-day shutdown at South plant due to monsoon disruption vs planned 45 days; forced clinker purchases causing Rs 10-12 crore contribution loss
items.quote: So, because of that extended shutdown of about 25 days we were forced to even to be in the market and not lose the trade market, we had to even purchase a lot of clinker to feed in the market. So, extended shutdown has not been I mean on the cost front it has not something substantially high. But that has resulted in some additional period, the clinker which we had to buy from the market. So, that

items.statement: Panna kiln availability impacted by erratic monsoon; ran at normal output only one-third of month near shutdown
items.quote: But this excessive rain when the kiln was closer to the shutdown, it did have an effect on the kiln and we had to run the kiln at a very low output for almost a month and also in between we had to close the kiln for two days, one day and that. So, during the quarter the availability of the kiln was also less. The kiln ran at normal output only for one-third of the month and at reduced output for t

items.statement: New heads appointed for Retail/MSME/SME/Agri assets, Liabilities & Third-Party Sales, and Retail Collections; senior leadership restructuring now complete.
items.quote: We have brought in a new leadership for Head of Retail, MSME, SME, Agri assets, that is Mr. Sreenivas Mylavarapu, a Head of Liabilities plus Third-Party Sales to focus on the business growth, that is Mr. Venkateswarlu Mallineni.

items.statement: Major tech infrastructure enhancements completed across storage, processing, and functional features.
items.quote: All the enhancements are in place, and we have done some major enhancements both in terms of our storage, processing, and also a lot of other functional features in our overall tech stack.

items.statement: Focus on portfolio quality over growth in Q2; will accelerate growth in retail and corporate segments in upcoming quarters.
items.quote: During this Q2, we have taken a conscious decision to focus on portfolio quality over growth. And during Q2 FY25, we will continue to maintain that focus on critical parameters.

items.statement: Aggregate business turnover grew 12% YoY to INR 175,284 crores.
items.quote: Overall, aggregate business, the business turnover of the bank stood at INR175,284 crores, up 12% on a year-on-year basis against INR156,468 crores in September '23, the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Profit after tax for Q2 FY25 was INR 336.07 crores, up from INR 330.26 crores YoY; H1 PAT INR 736.4 crores, up 5% YoY.
items.quote: On the profit after tax, for Q2 FY '25, the current quarter, it was INR336.07 crores as against INR330.26 crores in the corresponding quarter previous year. The PAT for the half year stood at INR736.4 crores versus INR700.96 crores as part of H1 of the last year, an increase of about 5%.

items.statement: Gross advances grew 12.5% YoY to INR 75,316 crores, in line with industry growth of ~13%.
items.quote: As far as the gross advances book, the total of the advances remained at INR75,316 crores as of September '24, and this reflects a year-on-year growth of about 12.5%. The industry growth for the same corresponding year-on-year was about 13%.

items.statement: Retail, agri, and mid-market RAM growth led by retail housing and gold loans with net accretion of INR 3,691 crores YoY; reduced exposure to low-yield bulk PSU advances.
items.quote: Our overall strategy was to grow retail, agri and mid-market RAM, and where the growth has been led by retail housing and gold loan for us, with a net book accretion of about INR3,691 crores on a year-on-year basis in this segment.

items.statement: Deposits grew 11.66% YoY to INR 99,967.99 crores, in line with industry growth of ~12%.
items.quote: The deposit number stands at INR99,967.99 crores, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 11.66% over September '23. And the industry growth, again here, among scheduled commercial banks is about 12%.

items.statement: New product launches planned: KBL Genius student savings account, KBL Peak education loan, premium savings account, merchant payment app, enhanced mobile apps for pre-approved personal loans, medical equipment loans, wealth management platf
items.quote: We are launching KBL Genius, which is a student savings account, KBL Peak, which is an education loan, a premium savings account, a merchant payment app, which will be QR code-based, and also enhancing our Mobile Plus and Mobile One applications for preapproved personal loans and also launching for specific medical equipment loans and a wealth management advisory platform.

items.statement: NII for H1 FY25 up 6.1% YoY to INR 1,736.92 crores; NIM at 3.38% for H1, within guidance range of 3.4%-3.6%; expect improvement from retail and direct-to-corporate growth.
items.quote: The NII for H1 FY '25 was INR1,736.92 crores. It was up 6.1% on a year-on-year in comparison. The NIM, we have clocked at 3.38% for the half year. There has been a dip in Q2. But overall, we still have done better and we are still within the guidance for 3.4% to 3.6%.

items.statement: CD ratio at 75.34% with headroom to grow advances; target to replace bulk advances with higher-yielding retail and direct-to-corporate loans.
items.quote: Our CD ratio is still at 75.34%, continuously improving every quarter, but we still have a headroom there and we believe that our ambition to grow the overall advances book with our capital and our CD ratio and our deposit acquisition engine, which will definitely show much better results as we go forward.

items.statement: Gross NPA improved to 3.21% from 3.54% QoQ and 3.47% YoY; Net NPA improved to 1.46% from 1.66% QoQ; on track to reach ~3% GNPA and ~1% NNPA.
items.quote: On the standard assets, this is one area where we'll be very proud this quarter because the gross NPA significantly improved from 3.54% to 3.21%. And this is something that we had committed in the last few quarters to say that we will come closer to 3%.

items.statement: Gross slippages dropped to 0.33% in Q2 from 0.59% in Q1 and 0.52% YoY; H1 slippage ratio 0.94% vs 1.03% YoY; recoveries of INR 148.01 crores in Q2.
items.quote: This has been achieved because the gross slippages has come down drastically, and we are at 0.33% in Q2 as against 0.59% in Q1 and as against 0.52% in Q2 of last year. For the 6 months ended September '24, the half year H1, the capex ratio stands at 0.94% as against 1.03% in 6 months.

items.statement: LCR at 143.93% under revised RBI draft guidelines (statutory minimum 100%), comfortable liquidity position.
items.quote: But as a conservative mechanism, we, at Karnataka Bank, have tested the LCR based on the revised guidelines. So even after the revised guidelines as of September 30th, we stand at 143.93% on the LCR, which is very comfortable and as against the statutory target of 100%.

items.statement: Cost of funds stable at 5.58% for Q2 and H1 FY25 vs 5.29% YoY; strategy to avoid high-cost bulk deposits.
items.quote: As far as the cost of funds is concerned, despite the market volatility, we have remained stable at 5.58%, and it was the same number almost for the Q1. And cost of funds for the entire half year was about 5.58%.

items.statement: Credit cost at 0.09% in Q2 (lowest so far) vs 0.11% QoQ and 0.17% YoY; H1 credit cost 0.2%; expect trend to continue.
items.quote: There is one other good part, which we need to report, which is credit cost. Our credit cost for the Q2 was at 0.09%, which is actually the lowest that we have had so far compared to 0.11% in the previous quarter and as against 0.17% in the quarter 2 of last year.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio elevated at ~58% due to tech investments, actuarial provisions (INR 23 cr increase), and lateral hires; target to return to ~55% in H2 and ~50% in following quarters.
items.quote: One of the areas of concern for us is the cost to income. We have incurred extra as far as elevated onetime costs in technology, some lateral recruitments and also increased provision for superannuation benefits because of the fact that the rates have moved -- the rates have decreased as far as the superannuation benefits of our staff, the actuarial calculations.

items.statement: ROA at 1.13% in Q2 vs guidance of 1.2%; expect to return to 1.2%-1.25% in following quarters.
items.quote: Because of this, the ROA has come to about 1.13% for Q2 as against 1.19% in March FY 24. Our guidance has been 1.2%. I think that we will get back to the 1.2% to 1.25% in the following quarters.

items.statement: ROE dipped to 11.63% due to equity raise; CRAR at 17.58% without H1 profits, >18.5% with profits; comfortable on Tier 1 and Tier 2.
items.quote: The ROE has dipped to 11.63% compared to the earlier quarters. And this, again, is because of the additional equity that we had raised, which all of you are aware. Our CRAR, without the half yearly profit being folded into the results, stands at 17.58%.

items.statement: Advances growth guidance revised to 15%-18% for FY25 (from ~18-19% earlier) due to transition from bulk PSU advances to retail and direct-to-corporate; expect to be ahead of market by year-end.
items.quote: So I think we will grow probably about, in the next 2 quarters, at about 15%, and then grow to the 18% because this is the transitionary phase where we were growing with some bulk advances in the past, but the bulk has come down drastically.

items.statement: Loan book 90% secured (collateralized); unsecured retail exposure minimal (<INR 250 crores via co-lending); agri loans gold and land-backed; NBFC lending 18% of book, all AAA/AA rated.
items.quote: The unsecured and secured mix has always been 90% fully collateralized book for us, and that continues. There is no change to that. The balance 10% also has been more to large corporate PSU, etc. So technically, we do not have any unsecured retail exposure per se, other than some co-lending and a couple of other arrangements that we have.

items.statement: Added ~10 branches in last 2 quarters; established national back-office in Mangalore (centralized clearing, treasury back-office shift underway); centralized account opening to free branches for sales.
items.quote: Yes, we are doing that. It's not as if we are expanding by the dozen. But yes, over the last 2 quarters, we have added about 10-odd branches including some shifting of branches. And also, we have set up a national back-office in Mangalore.

items.statement: Technical write-off book ~INR 3,000+ crores (100% provided); recovered INR 78 crores in H1, targeting INR 170-175 crores for full year.
items.quote: In the last two quarters, we made INR46 crores and INR32 crores. So approximately, we are at INR78 crores. And we believe that we would be about, let's say, another 100-odd crores, which will come in for this year also -- this rest of the year.

items.statement: Loan book ~50% EBLR-linked; retail liabilities 92% of deposits allow quick repricing; ALM managed to match asset-liability repricing on rate cuts.
items.quote: About 50% of our book is EBLR linked. There could be some on the retail side also. But overall, I'm saying I'm calling out to say that about 50% would be EBLR plus. Now as and when there is a rate change, obviously, the asset side will be repricing first and followed by the liability side.

items.statement: Fee income low vs peers but growing; third-party distribution income doubled YoY; wealth advisory platform, trade/forex cross-sell, and supply chain financing to drive future fee growth.
items.quote: In fact, compared to the last year, the number was almost like doubled of last year, and we are on that track. The second is that, there is a cross-sell opportunity, which is basically on trade and foreign exchange. And this is something that will materialize in the next following quarters only.

items.statement: RBI draft LCR guidelines increase runoff factors and change HQLA valuation; industry-wide impact; bank reporting 143.93% under draft rules vs higher under current rules; awaiting regulatory clarity.
items.quote: Currently, the changes were for the top line, i.e. HQLA were there was a change from the way the level 1 assets were being taken, basic from the book value to the market value. Second point was the runoff factor changes based on the type of digitalization availability that was a point.

items.statement: Management expects double-digit growth in Q3 and Q4 FY25 for standalone business
items.quote: It should be in the case of quarter 3 and quarter 4.

items.statement: Strong demand traction seen from August end, expected to continue for next two quarters
items.quote: We have seen a strong traction coming from August end itself. And we feel that, okay, this positivity is going to continue for the next 2 quarters at least.

items.statement: Pre-booked orders in hand but production could not meet demand in Q2
items.quote: We work on a pre-booking perspective. So we had orders in hand, but we were not able to produce it equivalently well.

items.statement: Kraus EBITDA margin at par with KKCL at 18-20%
items.quote: The top line has been INR 55 odd crores, and the brand has been able to achieve EBITDA margins, which is equivalent at KKCL.

items.statement: Company targets 18-20% EBITDA margin across brands including Junior Killer
items.quote: And if we see on margin -- see, we will maintain as Kewal Kiran, we will maintain 18% to 20% EBITDA margin. And averaging is around 18% to 20%, we will maintain that.

items.statement: Purchasing land for INR 57 crores for new head office, 100 meters from current office
items.quote: The property, which we are looking at buying out, it is required for the head office and the registered office.

items.statement: Production issues in Q1 led to inability to meet Q2 demand; reverted to earlier inventory model
items.quote: However, we had corrected that situation, but garment manufacturing being a lengthy process, we couldn't cater the demand fully in Q2.

items.statement: Kraus revenue INR 55 crores in Q2 FY25, full year FY24 revenue INR 175 crores
items.quote: Kraus has performed extremely well, okay, during this quarter, the total revenue is around INR 55 crores

items.statement: Junior Killer launched in April, available in all large format stores, strong response
items.quote: Junior, we launched in April and we have a very good performance. And I feel, we will get to good numbers by Season 2 and Season 3.

items.statement: Kraus sales primarily through LFS channel with high working capital needs
items.quote: Most of it sales -- generally, it operates a majority of it's sales is from one of the channel of sales, which is LFS, where the working capital requirement is very high.

items.statement: Consolidated working capital to stabilize at 120-130 days; Q2 receivables increase one-time
items.quote: I feel, okay, our total working capital would still stay ahead at 120-day to 130-odd days period. And this trade-off receivable is a one-time structure.

items.statement: Kraus net working capital around 100 days; debtor days high due to LFS channel sales
items.quote: Ideally, okay, on Kraus, we look at the net working capital. The net working capital will be a close around 100-odd days.

items.statement: Paid INR 116 crores to Kraus subsidiary in H1 FY25
items.quote: INR 116 crores, we have paid to the Kraus.

items.statement: Amortization of intangible assets from Kraus acquisition INR 6 crores per quarter for 7 years
items.quote: Total amortization for the quarter was around INR 6 crores. And the total --- It is going to continue for a 7-year period.

items.statement: Kraus positioned in women's denim western wear competing with Levi's, Only, Spykar Women at reasonable pricing
items.quote: It's core competition, on those channel of sale is, I would say Levi's, Only and it is priced reasonably as compared to these competition brand.

items.statement: Lee/Wrangler re-entering market but currently scaling from zero, not yet impacting business
items.quote: They're scaling up the business from 0-based structure. So right now, I would not say that it is hampering the business, but definitely, it's a competition.

items.statement: Net addition of 21 EBOs in Q2 FY25 plus 8 Kraus EBOs; total 534 EBOs as of Sep 30, 2024
items.quote: In this direction, there was a net addition of 21 EBOs in Q2 FY '25 and further 8 Kraus EBOs was added on account of consolidation bringing the total number of EBOs to 534 as of September 30, 2024.

items.statement: 55 EBOs under development across metro, Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities
items.quote: Further, there are around 55 EBOs which are in various stages of development.

items.statement: EBO expansion strategy: 85% FOFO, 15% COCO model; COCO stores metro-centric
items.quote: See, as far as company policy is concerned, 85% should be the FOFO model and the 15% should be the COCO model.

items.statement: Standalone sales declined 3.5% YoY in Q2; consolidated sales grew 17.4% YoY to INR 308.2 crores
items.quote: The sales performance in the quarter was positive and stood at INR 308.2 crores with the consolidated growth of 17.4% year-on-year.

items.statement: Winter season timing uncertain; late start increases discounted sales, not in management's control
items.quote: The only thing is when it starts, that allows you to have an additional margin or not the margin because if it starts late, the number of stocks sold during the discounted period increases, not in the fresh sell-through.

items.statement: Integriti brand revamp targeting value segment and private labels; results expected from Q1 FY26
items.quote: Integriti, we have looked at, okay, competing against the value price brands and as well as private label, okay. The extraction or maybe the numbers for the same should fall from quarter 1 of the next year.

items.statement: Lawman brand focusing on retail expansion from Q3 and Q4 FY25
items.quote: Particularly for Lawman, we are looking at retail expansions, which you'll see from quarter 3 and quarter 4.

items.statement: K-Lounge format on hold for at least a year
items.quote: For the K-Lounges, okay, as we said, okay, it's too early, and it is a stand-still position for at least a year period, okay.

items.statement: FY25 volume growth guided at 10%-11% and EBITDA margin at 12%
items.quote: As per earlier guidance given , we will be having a growth of about 10% and the EBITDA margin will be in the range of 12%.

items.statement: Gross margin target raised to 34-35% going forward
items.quote: Yes , we are focusing on increasing as our brand spend is increasing and we want to increase further this gross margin to 34 to 35 levels going forward.

items.statement: Freight cost expected to normalize in Q4 FY25 and Q1 FY26
items.quote: Actually, we have our inventory. So , there will be impact in the third quarter as well. Yes , the freight costs have more or less normalized and we are expecting it to come back in the fourth quarter and the later part the next year.

items.statement: UK revenue expected at €24-25 million for FY25
items.quote: We are expecting a revenue of €24 to €25 million this fiscal.

items.statement: Depreciation for FY25 guided at INR 175-180 crores
items.quote: It will be more or less in the same range that is there the half year, the 87 crores, it will be around 175 to 180 crores.

items.statement: Associate profit share expected at INR 30 crores for FY25
items.quote: That will be in the range of around 30 crores , 30 crores profit that will be coming from the associate.

items.statement: Ready-to-eat/cook breakeven targeted at INR 350-400 crores revenue in 2-3 years
items.quote: We will be breaking even at a revenue of around 350 to 400 crores. So, that will be the breakeven point and this we wish to achieve. We have plans to achieve at 2 to 3 years' time frame.

items.statement: Organic business expected to exceed INR 1,000 crores revenue this year with 10-12% growth
items.quote: This year we are expecting to do more than 1 ,000 crores in organic. So, that's building up. We are expecting both in terms of growth and margin expansion.

items.statement: H1 FY25 gross margin expanded 160 bps to 33.8%; Q2 gross margin up 320 bps to 34.1%
items.quote: Gross profit stood at Rs. 1 ,427 crores and the gross profit margins expanded by 160 bps from 32.2% to 33.8%.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin down 50 bps to 12.2% due to higher freight
items.quote: EBITDA margins were 50 bps lower at 12.2% on account of increased freight rate.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis impact on EBITDA margin ~1% (INR 27-28 crores)
items.quote: Roughly we have impact of Rs. 27-28 crores on our budgeted number, the Red Sea that counts for 1.2%.

items.statement: Logistics cost rose to 6.6% of revenue in H1 FY25 from 4.8% in H1 FY24
items.quote: So, it is now 6.6% of my revenue as compared to 4.8% last half year.

items.statement: No demand challenges; Basmati category growing in USA, Middle East (34% growth), India
items.quote: No, we are not facing challenge, actually whichever part of the world we are present the category is growing be it USA, Middle East. Middle East we have grown 34%.

items.statement: Inventory days increased to 194 from 166 to meet higher demand across regions
items.quote: our inventory days have increased from 166 to 194 days. So, that is an increase of 28 days. This inventory day is actually in order to c ater the increase in the demand that we are seeing in the different

items.statement: Inventory days expected to return to prior March levels by March 2025
items.quote: So, yes of course we will be maintaining the ROC at level of (+20) and the inventory days will be of course in line to that ROC level. So , we will be maintaining the (+20) ROC levels in the going forward quarters or year to come.

items.statement: UK plant inaugurated in July and contributing; US ready-to-eat capacity doubling from 15M to 35M pouches
items.quote: UK plant has already been set up and we just done inauguration in July. That has started contributing. Regarding the USA, we are doubling our capacity of ready to eat plant. Right now, we are producing 15 million pouches which is totally sold out. Now we are doubling to 35 million.

items.statement: Uganda soya mill investment small, for organic business
items.quote: Uganda is a small investment, very small investment. That is mainly for our organic business where they are putting the soya mill.

items.statement: Paddy prices down 10-17% on new crop; expected to improve FY26 margins
items.quote: Roughly it depends on variety to variety but in the range of 10% to 17% or same that is the range.

items.statement: Premium and organic mix drove gross margin expansion; $3 tier contributes 40-45% of GP margin
items.quote: Because of the mix a ctually, we have in a basket , we have a three range , a $3, $2, $1. $3 contributes around 40% to 45% of the GP margin

items.statement: Middle East premium share rose to 9.8% from 6.2% in Dubai per Nielsen; Saudi distributor appointed
items.quote: In Dubai, our share in premium segment as per Nielsen has gone to 9.8% from 6.2 %. we are improving our market share in Kuwait , in Qatar, in Muscat and Iraq also.

items.statement: SALIC partnership progressing; good news expected within a month
items.quote: So, that's progressing well, as told in the last meeting we have appointed distributor and there's better news is coming. We are in process maybe in a month's time you will hear a good news.

items.statement: Net working capital days rose to 195 from 174 in H1 FY24
items.quote: Our net working capital days stands at 195 days versus the 174 in H1 of the Financial Year '24.

items.statement: Ready-to-cook working capital cycle ~90 days
items.quote: That must be 90 days working capital side.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR 546 crores from INR 569 crores; debt-to-equity 0.2x, debt/EBITDA 0.8x
items.quote: The cash profit increased by 7% to Rs. 393 crores versus Rs. 366 crores last year and the net debt reached to 546 crores versus 569 crores in the last half year.

items.statement: H1 FY25 ROCE 20.8%, ROE 17.1%, current ratio 2.5
items.quote: The return on capital employed stood at 20.8% in first half of the Financial Year '25 compared to first half of '24 which was 21.6%. Return on equities stood at 17.1% for the first half of '25 compared to 19.5% of first half of '24.

items.statement: FY25 constant currency revenue growth guidance raised to 19.5%-20.5% including ~5% from Ascensos; organic guidance 14.5%-15.5%
items.quote: For FY25, we now expect our revenue to grow in the range of 19.5% to 20.5% in constant currency terms. This includes about 5% contribution from Ascensos over the 7 months in FY25.

items.statement: FY25 normalized EBIT margin guidance 11%-11.5% excluding one-time acquisition charges
items.quote: For operating margins, we expect our normalized FY25 EBIT margin, excluding one-time charges related to the acquisitions, to be in the 11% to 11.5% band.

items.statement: Q2 normalized EBIT margin 11.1% excluding Ascensos acquisition one-time charges, stable QoQ and YoY
items.quote: EBIT margin for the quarter was 11.1%, excluding one-time charges related to the Ascensos' acquisition. This is broadly stable, both on a QoQ and a YoY basis.

items.statement: Number of $1M+ clients increased to 105 from 101 YoY; $20M+ clients increased to 11 from 8 YoY; three large deal wins each in Q1 and Q2
items.quote: the number of clients with over $1 million of revenue has gone up by 4 to 105 in Q2 from 101 a year ago. During the same period, the number of clients with whom we get over $20 million of revenue has increased from 8 to 11. Similarly, we are now clocking three large deal wins in the quarter versus just about one deal a year back.

items.statement: Added new seat capacities in Chennai, Hyderabad, Philippines and Mexico in Q2
items.quote: We continue to invest in expanding our execution infrastructure in Q2. We have added new seat capacities in Chennai, Hyderabad, Philippines and Mexico.

items.statement: Headcount 32,898; trailing 12-month attrition 31% down from 32% in Q1 and 39.8% in Q2 FY24; expect gradual further decline
items.quote: On the people front, we ended Q2 with a total headcount of 32,898 Firstsourcers. Our trailing 12-month attrition rate for the quarter was 31%, a reduction from 32% in Q1FY25 and 39.8% in Q2 of last year.

items.statement: DSO improved to 65 days from 68 days in Q1; OCF/EBITDA 79%, FCF/PAT 101%
items.quote: Reported DSO came down to 65 days in Q2 from 68 days in Q1 as I spoke last time that there are some of the one-off delays which have got normalized this quarter. We have a healthy cash conversion this quarter. Our OCF to EBITDA was 79% and FCF to PAT was 101%.

items.statement: Hedge book: GBP 75.6M covered for 12 months at avg 109.3 INR/GBP; USD 141.3M covered at avg 85 INR/USD
items.quote: Our hedge book as of September 30th was as follows. We have coverage of £75.6 million for the next 12 months with an average rate of 109.3 to the pound and coverage of $141.3 million with an average rate of Rs. 85 per dollar.

items.statement: Annual wage hike effective July 1; continued investments in sales, capabilities, AI/automation; margin stable despite cost increases
items.quote: We have been able to keep our margin stable despite giving out the annual wage hike to our employees effective 1st July and continuing to make investment in our businesses.

items.statement: Constant currency revenue growth 6.9% QoQ (4.2% organic excluding 1 month Ascensos); fourth straight quarter >3% QoQ CC growth
items.quote: In constant currency, revenue grew at 6.9% quarter-on-quarter. Adjusted for one month of Ascensos' revenue, our growth was 4.2% in constant currency terms. As you may note, this is the fourth straight quarter where we have delivered over 3% QoQ constant currency revenue growth.

items.statement: Ascensos adds nearshore delivery in South Africa, Romania, Trinidad & Tobago, Turkey; existing UK client already awarded additional business in South Africa post-acquisition
items.quote: Ascensos brings to us a scale presence in several strategically important global delivery locations. For example, its presence in South Africa improves our attractiveness to the clients and prospects in the UK who are actively exploring economical outsourcing capacities in the same time zone. In fact, one of our existing clients in the UK has already awarded us additional business in South Africa

items.statement: Completed acquisition of Jindal Rail and Infra, renamed Texmaco West Rail, enhancing market reach and leadership in freight cars and high-tech wagons
items.quote: A significant development in H1 FY '25 was the completion of our acquisition of Jindal Rail and Infra. Now we have named it as Texmaco West Rail.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR8,200 crores with freight car business accounting for 72%
items.quote: Looking forward, our order book is at INR8,200 crores with freight car business accounting for 72% of the same.

items.statement: Expect H2 FY25 wagon production to be better than H1's 5,300 units, implying full-year run rate near or above 10,600 wagons
items.quote: Sir, we have produced 5,300 wagon in a consolidated manner half yearly. If you multiply by 2 because we cannot go down, so it becomes 10,600. So we will be any time near to that or bit even a little better to that.

items.statement: Target to increase EBITDA margin from ~10% to 12-13% over next 1.5-2 years driven by higher private sector wagon share
items.quote: So Rahul, absolutely, yes, what you mentioned, we all are working towards the common goal to increase the EBITDA margin, what the numbers you mentioned.

items.statement: No significant capex needed for wagon capacity expansion; new foundry being set up in Odisha for export-oriented castings
items.quote: So these are -- I mean, to answer you, I don't -- we don't need any CapEx to do that. So these capacities, you can see that it's not a problem and not a challenge for your company.

items.statement: Wagon production capacity is elastic with current infrastructure; no limitation on numbers, focus on product mix and export portfolio
items.quote: Capacity of production is kind of elastic in terms of freight rolling stock when you have a decent infrastructure. It's a question of utilization with the right product mix.

items.statement: Expect ~30,000 wagons from Indian Railways this year and 12,000-15,000 from private sector, with large private tenders in pipeline
items.quote: And this year and middle of next year, we expect around 30,000 more wagons to come in, whatever we know about -- I mean, the tenders have come up and something is in the pipeline.

items.statement: Private and export wagons have higher margins than Indian Railways; export margins highest, then private, then railways
items.quote: So private is always better than what we have in terms of railways. And after private, we have export. Export is even better than what we supply to private.

items.statement: Exports of INR185 crores in H1 FY25 including freight cars to Africa and steel foundry castings to US, Australia, Europe
items.quote: The total export number, yes, I have now, Rahul, it is INR185 crores in H1.

items.statement: Jindal Rail acquisition funded through internal accruals and QIP funds
items.quote: The fund has been remitted, and it was done through internal accruals from the company and certain portion from the QIP funds, which were there.

items.statement: Net debt increased to ~INR800 crores post-acquisition; management targets 70:30 debt-equity ratio for future projects
items.quote: So generally, we work on a debt equity of 70% - 30%. Texmaco Rail & So depending upon the case-to-case basis, the call would be taken by the

items.statement: GPWIS moratorium easing; ~40-50 racks ordered recently out of expected 200 racks; Texmaco benefiting from early deliveries
items.quote: And around -- we expected around 200 racks were supposed to be procured. items.statement: Jindal Rail (Texmaco West Rail) contributed INR426 crores revenue and INR62.73 crores PBT in H1 FY25
items.quote: So yes, Mohit, the H1, they made a total revenue from operation was INR426 crores and their PBT was INR63 crores, INR62.73 crores to be exact.

items.statement: Jindal Rail executed 891 wagons in H1 (484 in Q2) vs Texmaco's 4,410 (2,443 in Q2); Jindal focuses on specialized wagons with lower volumes
items.quote: Texmaco, that is Texmaco Rail and Engineering did executed an order of 4,410 wagons and Jindal Rail did 891 in H1 last quarter 2. And in quarter 2, Texmaco Rail did 2,443 and Jindal Rail did 484.

items.statement: Both Texmaco and Jindal capable of double-decker wagons; Jindal has ACC1 design with 3-rack order from APL Vascor; Texmaco nearing ACC3 approval
items.quote: And ACC1 recently from a company called APL Vascor, we have got in September an order of 3 racks to deliver to them. And for Texmaco, Texmaco is in the final stage of approval from Indian Railway for designing ACC3.

items.statement: Infra Rail and Green Energy segment demerger in progress but timeline uncertain due to government/statutory processes
items.quote: Sir, of course, our intention is common with you, but you know that the government machineries and statutory obligations are there where it is very difficult for you and me to commit.

items.statement: Freight car sales: 2,927 units in Q2 FY25 with 72% to Indian Railways, balance to private and export orders
items.quote: Operationally, we reached a new milestone in freight car Texmaco Rail & sales with 2,927 units delivered in Q2, of which 72% were for Indian Railways and the balance fulfilled private and export orders

items.statement: Infra Electrical segment order book INR1,700 crores; expect top line to multiply in coming quarters with strong bottom line
items.quote: And along with -- as I mentioned about top line, but I must add that bottom line will be very strong of that business too.

items.statement: Awarded 3-star export house certification by Government of India
items.quote: Notably, Texmaco has been awarded the 3-star export house certification by the Government of India, affirming our role as a valued contributor to India's trade landscape.

items.quote: So those redundancies, we want to convert it into assets and convert it into some good returns for the company in the way forward. So that's why we thought of having a kind of enabling resolution to get into.

items.quote: So, if you sum it up, it could be somewhere around 225 basis points for the year.

items.quote: The SMA-1 and 2 of the retail books (excluding microfinance) is 0.87% actually reduced over last quarter. It's come down by 8 basis points.

items.statement: Collection efficiency in urban retail book stable at 99.5%
items.quote: It is stable at 99.5%. So, this is something important to note that our collection efficiency of this front is holding up pretty well.

items.quote: We've taken 100% provision against this legacy toll account. Now with this, there is no more exposure left in the account. We believe that the end of the day, the government will pay for this because I don't think any government will really cancel a contract like this and not pay. items.statement: NII up 21% YoY to Rs 4,788 crore; NIM stable at 6.18% (down 4 bps QoQ)
items.quote: increased by 21% on a YOY basis to Rs. 4 ,788 crores. NIM was broadly stable, I would say, at about 6.18%, which was lowered by about 4 bps on a sequential basis

items.quote: Our rating continues to be AA+ (Stable). But on the fixed deposit program, CRISIL has rated us AAA, which to us is a huge arrival moment because of AAA by CRISIL, even on the FD program, it's a huge moment for us.

items.quote: As we mentioned on slide 19 of the presentation, the high-cost legacy borrowing further reduced by Rs. 2,400 crores during the current quarter. At the end of this year, there will be a few more repayments and we will be left with just about Rs. 4,800 crores to be paid off.

items.statement: Retail segment growth: home loans 20%, LAP 20%, vehicle finance 32%, consumer 21%, gold loans 185% (low base)
items.quote: Within that also, let me just share that the home loan business is growing by 20%, loan against property is growing by 20%, vehicle financing is going by 32%, the consumer business is growing by 21%, and the gold business is growing by 185%, but that's of course coming from a very low base.

items.statement: Microfinance delinquency rising across industry; bank tightened lending, reduced disbursements from Rs 4,250 crore (Q2 FY24) to Rs 2,000 crore (Q2 FY25); 50% of book now CGFMU insured
items.quote: So, our disbursal came down from Rs. 4,250 crores. It's what we disbursed in Q2 FY24 , in Q3 we brought it on to Rs. 3,800 crores. And we did one more thing. We started insuring the book with CGFMU. So

items.statement: Toll road account shock due to state government waiving toll fees; fully provided; expects government to eventually pay

items.statement: Credit deposit ratio improved sequentially to 97.7%; incremental CD ratio ~78% over last year
items.quote: The credit deposit ratio improved on a sequential basis to 97.7%. The incremental CD ratio during the last year is at about 78%.

items.statement: LCR stable at 116%
items.quote: LCR was broadly stable at 116% and this is well within the range which we have been guiding over the quarters.

items.statement: Branch count at 961; opened 17 branches in H1 FY25
items.quote: Our branch count is now at 961 branches. During this half year, we have opened about 17 branches for the year.

items.statement: Expects operating profit to grow 24-25% in FY25; core operating profit was Rs 6,030 crore in FY24 and grew 29% YoY in H1 FY25
items.quote: Now, at least we are in a position to predict Rs. 6,000 crores of operatin g profit and we can expect about 24%-25%, we can expect operating profit to increase this year also.

items.statement: Ex-microfinance credit cost at 180 bps in H1 FY25 vs 165 bps guidance; driven by Rs 250 crore toll account provision; other products stable with SMA data disclosed by product
items.quote: Even now, if you exclude these two, 180 is not the bad number. You can see the numbers in the market. So, we feel that this is reasonably under control and basically the way to think about it as compared to last year to this year.

items.statement: Blended credit cost expected to stabilize at ~1.85% of loans (1.3% of assets) long-term based on product mix math; current SMA by product shows mortgages 0.39%, vehicles ~1.07%, MSME 1.26%, consumer durables 1%
items.quote: you will get a number of about 1.85% for our Bank. So, in one quarter, one month, something may be up, something may be down, but blend -blend, our Bank is heading for about 185 and for this yield that we are getting , 185 is a good number , stable number coming for 15 years.

items.statement: Restructured book at 0.23% of loans (~Rs 500 crore), mostly mortgages, carrying 19% provision; contingency provision of Rs 315 crore created in Q2
items.quote: the restructured book, as I said, that book is now only 0.23% in value terms that it is about Rs. 500 crores of restructured book which we have and the predominant part of it is the mortgage book which is sitting here. On this, we are carrying a provision of about 19%.

items.quote: since our core CET1 is also at 14%, including the benefit of the merger and otherwise it is 16.6% including CET2, so as of no w we are comfortable. We are not thinking of, even internally, we are not talking capital at this point of time.

items.statement: Merger networth accretion of Rs 618 crore (combination of cash, investments) effective Oct 1; 24 bps CET1 benefit in Q3
items.quote: Yes, networth accretion would be about Rs. 618 crores at September end and this benefit would flow into Q3. And in terms of capital adequacy benefit, this would give us about 24 bps of relief, right, which will come in Q3.

items.statement: Full-year capacity growth guidance of early double digits maintained
items.quote: We will continue to execute our long -term strategy and are fully confident in meeting our full -year capacity growth guidance of the early double digits.

Currently, while some of the markets are still underserved, some markets especially international are witnessing added competitive intensity.

items.statement: October domestic demand showing high single-digit to early double-digit growth

items.quote: We reported a net loss of 9.9 billion rupees with a negative net profit margin of 5.8 percent compared to a net profit of 1.9 billion rupees with a net profit margin of around one percent during the same period last year.
