items.quote: Potentially, within next 6 to 8 months, we'll have to open up the construction for the new site as well. And that is where we are looking at a capex of about INR200 crores to begin with as a part development of the project.

items.statement: Monoglyme pilot at 10kg catalyst scale; 100kg scale equipment ready except cooling system (delivery Jan); 1000kg scale equipment ordered for delivery by June 2025
items.quote: Right now, we are successfully piloting at a 10 kg catalyst level. We have our equipment for 100 kg catalyst levels ready, except for 1 cooling system is missing, which is expected to be delivered roughly in the beginning of January.

items.statement: New distillation plant to be operational by Nov 2025 to support agro/pharma volume ramp-up
items.quote: So, we are breaking ground for this plant. So, we will start construction post Diwali and this will become operational after 1 year, so November of next year. November of 2025.

items.statement: COGS improved to 50-51% from 54% as high-value inventory consumption nears end; expects margin recovery
items.quote: Also, if you see the cost of materials consumed has actually, from the earlier, it was a very -- at about 54% levels, I believe, has come down to a range of between about 50% to 51% levels.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 6.7% in Q2 FY25 vs 20.7% YoY; H1 FY25 9.6% vs 19.7% YoY due to higher COGS and expenses
items.quote: EBITDA margin decreased by 14% to 6.7% due to increase in COGS and other expenses by 12.6% and 1.6% Y-o-Y respectively.

items.statement: SDA raw material prices stabilized at 20-year lows; no further decline expected, only upside
items.quote: Yes. So now the prices have very much stabilized and practically not only on the raw materials for SDA, but generally speaking, most of the raw materials have kind of stabilized? Or I would say right now, they are stable at the bottom level.

items.statement: Flame retardants pricing shifted to cost-plus mechanism with large European customer to manage bromine volatility
items.quote: So finally, after a lot of convincing we agreed on a cost plus basis. So, we have fixed up a pricing mechanism. So irrespective of where the market price is, because realistically speaking, today, the level at which the market price is, is absolutely an unrealistic, unviable option to even think of producing these items.

items.statement: Electrolyte salts for supercapacitors and zinc batteries (not lithium); only Indian player, two Chinese competitors
items.quote: So, the place where we are involved is definitely absolutely nowhere close to the lithium battery application. We are into the super capacitor batteries and the zinc battery application. So here, we don't see any competition in both of these two segments within India.

items.statement: Polymer products: 2 electrolysis-based products to commercialize in FY26; Monoglyme capacity 2,000 MT/yr at ~$4/kg
items.quote: We have successfully completed planned trials for 1 product using electrolysis technology. The outcome of this product is meeting the stringent quality requirements of the end use customer. Plant trial for the second product in this segment will begin post Diwali, both these products are expected to commercialize within next fiscal year.

items.statement: Onboarded 3 large new SDA customers (petrochemical applications); Euro 7 norms to drive growth from mid-late 2025
items.quote: Now as I had said in my earlier calls, if I remember correctly, we have also onboarded two good customers having applications on the petrochemical side. So, we are kind of trying to balance this temporary phenomena of loss in terms of volumes on the vehicle applications getting balanced by the petrochemical side.

items.statement: Electrolyte customer for hybrid vehicles advancing well; commercialization from H2 2025; second customer by end-2025
items.quote: The qualification process with the customer engaged in creating batteries for hybrid vehicles is advancing remarkably well. This encouraging trend suggests a strong alignment between our product and the customers' requirements.

items.statement: Exports 60% of revenue in Q2 FY25 (INR508 cr); key markets USA, UK, China, Germany, Japan, South Africa
items.quote: During Q2 FY '25, exports stood at INR508 million, contributing 60% of the revenue. The major countries include USA., UK, China, Germany, Japan and South Africa.

items.statement: SDA market share ~15-16%; market size ~7x current volumes; Euro 7 to expand market ~50%
items.quote: In terms of SDAs, we typically are at about 12% to 15% in terms of market share. Probably between 15%, 16% is my estimation, right? So, there are no definitive numbers by which I can very strongly say, but this is a very fair estimation based on our market information or market intelligence.

items.statement: PTC export market share ~25-30%
items.quote: In terms of segments, if we say we can define this, the question only for 3 segments, which is based on for catalyst, where we believe in terms of export market, we handle roughly about 25% to 30% of the volumes.

items.statement: Transit times increased (3 weeks avg) due to geopolitical issues; goods in transit rose from INR7.1 cr to INR17.5 cr QoQ, deferring revenue recognition
items.quote: Basically, as you are aware that the transit times have increased drastically because of this rate issue, let's say so. So, the longer transit time to US and to Europe is hurting. So, basically, typically speaking 3 weeks transit time has on an average increased if we compare an average between these 2 routes, which is impacting this change.

items.statement: Agro/pharma customer volume commitments may be 20-30% lower than forecast due to market conditions
items.quote: Of course, I can understand considering the Agro market as of today. There could be a potential up and down in terms of volumes, what the customer commit maybe 20%, 30% lower than that may end up.

items.statement: Targets 15% EBITDA margin for Agrochemical division and 10% EBITDA margin for Pigment division in next financial year
items.quote: So, first target somewhere for the Agrochemical division, we target to reach at 15% EBITDA margin. That is the first target. Once we reach at that level, then we will think of taking it to the next level.

items.statement: Expects gradual price improvement in agrochemicals from Q4 FY25 or Q1 FY26
items.quote: But we feel somewhere from January onwards or from the first quarter onwards in the next financial year, there should be gradual improvement in the pricing also, which will not be significant like which used to be in the old days.

items.statement: Destocking largely complete in agrochemicals; demand recovery expected from Q4 FY25 or Q1 FY26
items.quote: Now, I would say in majority of the market for majority of the products, the destocking has already been taken place and gradually the demand has started improving.

items.statement: Pigment segment EBITDA turned positive at INR4.2 crore vs negative INR2.5 crore YoY
items.quote: The segment reported the revenue of about INR135 crores, which is up by 23% year-on-year, and EBITDA of INR4.2 crores against the negative EBITDA of INR2.5 crores in the corresponding previous year.

items.statement: New product registrations in Brazil pipeline; subsidiary approval at final stage with RBI
items.quote: We have received few registration, we have received so far few registration and a lot of new registrations are in pipeline. So, over a period of next 2 to 3 years, we will be getting many, many new registrations.

items.statement: No significant capex needed for Agrochemical and Pigment divisions for next 1-2 years; focus on debt repayment
items.quote: So, I think for Agrochemical division and the Pigment division, we don't need to do any significant capex over a period of next 1 or 2 years' time. So, we will be rather repaying the debt and we'll bring down our cost of finance and we'll maintain relatively low-level debt in the company.

items.statement: TiO2 plant running at 40% capacity; expects improvement after anti-dumping duty
items.quote: If I talk about the capacity utilization, we are currently running the plant at about 40% capacity. It should improve gradually going forward.

items.statement: Interim anti-dumping duty on TiO2 from China expected in Q3 FY25; should improve price realization
items.quote: With the interim anti-dumping duty on TiO2 from China expected in Q3 FY'25, we anticipate further improvement in price realization going forward.

items.statement: Logistics costs increased drastically but started declining; expected to normalize next quarter
items.quote: At the same time, the logistic cost, which has increased drastically in the last few months that has also started going down a little bit. And again, we feel that it will be at a reasonable level in the next one quarter.

items.statement: Crop protection 75% of revenue, Pigment 25% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: If I talk about the revenue mix in Q2 FY25, Crop protection constitutes about 75% of the total revenue, while the balance 25% comes from the Pigment segment.

items.statement: New niche products launched: Flonicamid, Ethiprole, Cyfluthrin, Beta Cyfluthrin, Dinotefuran, Spiromesifen, Flubendiamide, Cyhalothrin
items.quote: So, the product, if I give you the idea, then a lot of new products like Flonicamid, Ethiprole, Cyfluthrin, Beta Cyfluthrin, Dinotefuran, Spiromesifen. So, a lot of new products we have introduced.

items.statement: Chinese TiO2 dumping globally; anti-dumping duties initiated in EU, Brazil, Saudi Arabia, India, Japan
items.quote: So we can understand there has been significant dumping of TiO2 from Chinese market globally in different, different markets, which is creating a major pressure. But we see that as the price will go up, we will also be able to sell more quantity in the domestic market.

items.statement: Pigment green/blue exports to China now only 8-10% of pigment revenue after Chinese anti-dumping duty
items.quote: Now, earlier it was little more, but now there is not any significant revenue which is coming from China. It is relatively low. We have been exporting to other markets now. I would say it would be probably 8% to 10%.

items.statement: Finance cost spike due to INR15 crore MTM loss on Euro borrowing; offset by INR14 crore forex gain in other income
items.quote: So, there was an MTM during this quarter around INR15 crores and on YTD basis also it was INR14 crores, that reflects in the finance cost, but if you see the overall foreign currency gain or loss, so there is a roughly INR14 crores gain in that other income.

items.statement: Focus on debt repayment and reducing finance cost; maintain low debt levels
items.quote: So, we will be rather repaying the debt and we'll bring down our cost of finance and we'll maintain relatively low-level debt in the company.

items.statement: Safety incident in pigment plant during maintenance shutdown; no injuries or significant asset damage; implementing ECS automation and Responsible Care certification
items.quote: There was no operation. The plant was under shut down for maintenance and the incident took place in one of the isolated scrap area. So, which has not impacted any damage on human life, which has no one is even injured.

items.statement: TiO2 plant economics challenging without anti-dumping duty; payback longer than historical Meghmani standards
items.quote: Without antidumping duty, it's going to be a little difficult, but we are confident that it will come.

items.statement: Standalone revenue INR532 crore (+42% YoY, +30% QoQ); EBITDA INR41.2 crore (+179% YoY, +190% QoQ); Net profit INR8.6 crore vs loss YoY
items.quote: In Q2 FY25, on a standalone basis, revenue from operations stood at about INR532 crores, reporting a growth of 42% Y-o-Y and 30% quarter-on-quarter basis. EBITDA for the quarter grew to INR41.2 crores, increasing by 179% year-on-year and 190% on quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Aims for 100 net store additions in FY25, down from earlier 120-150 guidance
items.quote: So, on a net basis, we will be at around 100 stores net for the full financial year, against the original guidance of 120 to 150 stores.

items.statement: Targets 120+ net store additions in FY26
items.quote: So, on a net basis we see ourselves adding at 120+ stores next year, for sure.

items.statement: Expects inventory days of 90-95 by March 2025
items.quote: We expect our inventory to remain in the range of 90 to 95 days by March 2024.

items.statement: Targets >50% EBITDA to pre-IndAS operating cash flow conversion
items.quote: Going forward, we aim to convert more than 50% of our EBITDA in pre-IndAS days operating cash flow.

items.statement: Capex guidance of Rs 25-30 crore for H2 FY25
items.quote: See, it will be anywhere in the range of between Rs. 25 crores and Rs. 30 crores.

items.statement: A&P spend maintained at 2% of revenue for H2 FY25
items.quote: So, we will be maintaining the same hygiene level of 2% spend even in H2. So, marketing spend as a percentage of revenue will not change.

items.statement: Steady state gross margin expected at 61-62%
items.quote: So, I think on a steady state basis, Ankit, you can expect a GM of about 61% to 62%, it will range in that bracket.

items.statement: Demand slow in Q2; September weak after decent July-August; South slower than other regions
items.quote: In fact, July and August, we have seen a decent improvement in demand. In fact, we were having single digit SSSG also by September first week. But unfortunately, September was a very weak month with a slight early sharp as well.

items.statement: Optimistic on festive season recovery driven by weddings, urban mobility, consumer sentiment
items.quote: Several factors support this outlook, including the festive season ahead, which typically boosts consumer spending, a graduate recovery in economic conditions, and a return to social events and weddings.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin 31.7% vs 31.9% YoY; Q2 EBITDA margin 30.5%
items.quote: EBITDA for H1 FY '25 stood at Rs. 136 crores as compared to Rs. 121 crores in H1 FY '24, a growth of 12% Y-o-Y. Our EBITDA margin stood at 31.7%.

items.statement: H1 FY25 revenue Rs 429 crore, up 13% YoY; Q2 revenue Rs 209 crore, up 10% YoY
items.quote: Revenue stood at Rs. 429 crores in H1 FY '25 as against Rs. 379 crores in H1 FY '24, a growth of 13% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Capex Rs 25-30 crore for H2 FY25, funded by operating cash flow
items.quote: See, it will be anywhere in the range of between Rs. 25 crores and Rs. 30 crores. Since you are generating healthy operating cash flows in the line of more than Rs. 50 crores, I do not think --

items.statement: Opened 54 gross / 41 net stores in H1 FY25; closed 13 very small stores (<200 sq ft); plans 80 gross / 60 net in H2
items.quote: In H1 FY '25, we opened 54 new stores on a gross basis, and on a full year basis on a full six months H1 we opened 41 stores at the net level.

items.statement: Average store size 300-500 sq ft; closing very small stores as they cannot accommodate full collection
items.quote: Our average store size is between 300 and 500. In our network of stores, there are still some stores which are very small, some stores might be 150 square feet, 190 square feet, and those stores are not able to accommodate the range what a 300 or a 400 square feet store can take.

items.statement: H1 ASP Rs 759, up 1% YoY; full price sales 95%
items.quote: Our full price sales accounted for 95% with an average selling price of Rs. 759 for H1.

items.statement: Pants and jeggings gaining share; core leggings/chudidaars stable
items.quote: See, there are a few products in the pants category and there are some few products in the jeggings category which have slightly higher gross margins, because of which it is reflecting in our GM.

items.statement: LFS receivables up due to new store additions; no festive stock dumping at LFS
items.quote: So, Ankit, I think receivable days have little increased because we have added more number of stores in H1. And because we added a good number of new stores, the sales in those counters would not have really been reflected, but we placed the inventory which is better than our books.

items.statement: No impact from Zudio or Meesho; differentiated as dedicated bottom wear brand
items.quote: See, Zudio or any other large format stone will not impact our sales. See, we are a very specialized bottom wear brand with so many color options and product options.

items.statement: Inventory days reduced from 104 (Mar'24) to 97 (Sep'24); pre-IndAS OCF Rs 55 crore in Sep'24
items.quote: As a result, our inventory days have decreased from 104 days in March 2024 to 97 days in September 2024, showing a 17 days reduction.

items.statement: Debtor days 150-155 due to SOR inventory accounting; true debtor days 37-40 on company revenue
items.quote: See, the thing is, the debtors which are in our books is actually inventory on the shop floor, the unsold inventory because of accounting standards is debtors in our books, so that's why the number of days has always ranged between 150 to 155 days.

items.statement: Promoter pledge clearance delayed; no timeline given; family priority to clear at earliest
items.quote: Right now, Rahul, no update here. I mean, honestly, we wanted to clear the pledge by December is what we had committed to everyone. But as of now, we do not have an update.

items.statement: Appointed Vijay Srinivas (ex-TTK, Cafe Coffee Day) as Head of MBO sales to build selective MBO channel
items.quote: He was into FMCG, and he worked earlier in many FMCG companies. And he has very good experience in the MBO and distribution. He has earlier worked in TTK and has also worked in Café Coffee Day as well.

items.statement: Q2 SSSG 0.54% (volume -0.6%); H1 SSSG 0.46% (volume -0.59%)
items.quote: As far as SSSGs are concerned, so for Q2 our SSSG was 0.54%, on a volume basis it was minus 0.6%. And for H1, our SSSG was 0.46% and on a volume basis it was minus 0.59%.

items.statement: Store closure risk: sales may not fully transfer from closed small stores to larger ones
items.quote: We are confident that sales from the smaller stores will transition to a larger store in line with this approach.

items.statement: App not officially launched; currently in Play Store for internal training; official launch in coming months
items.quote: No, Saurav, actually what happened, we have not really launched our application officially yet. We had actually launched that application more from an internal training perspective.

items.statement: Revenue guidance for FY25 is INR2,500-2,700 crores; management targeting midpoint given H1 performance
items.quote: I think our revenue guidance was INR2,500 crores, INR2,700 crores. Yes. So I think at half year, we are at INR1,225 crores. We are trying to still see how much we can do in H2. We will hope to be somewhere in the midpoint of the range.

items.statement: No revenue guidance provided for FY26 or FY27; focus on ending FY25 strongly for FY26 base
items.quote: No, not at all. Right now, I think we just want to end Q4 on a strong base so that we get a good base for FY '26.

items.statement: Cash Logistics business expected to grow 10-13% in midterm; H1 grew ~9% despite weak consumption
items.quote: I think we've guided to the fact that the cash business has the potential to grow in the 10% to 13% in the midterm. And I think we are sort of ballpark in that range, subject to plus or minus a little bit of the consumption and activity level.

items.statement: Managed Services services revenue flat YoY in H1 due to delayed order execution; product revenue rose from 2% to 12% of mix
items.quote: Given the fact that some of these projects haven't gone live as per our books, we did accelerate some of the product business because that's a little more easier to go execute and get them live and bill.

items.statement: Consolidated PAT margin 14.5% in Q2; Cash Logistics EBIT margin 25%, Managed Services EBIT margin 15.1%
items.quote: PAT grew by 8% to INR90.4 crores, and PAT margin stood at 14.5%.

items.statement: H1 EBITDA margin ~25.3% vs H2 FY24 ~25.5%; management expects margin improvement in H2 as order book executes
items.quote: And therefore, if you think H2 last year, the EBITDA was about 25.5%. H1 this year is about 25.3%. I think these are numbers for this type of business.

items.statement: INR1,600 crores orders won in last 4 quarters; only 15% executed vs expected 30-35%; INR200 crores new orders in H1, total INR400 crores
items.quote: we secured INR1,600 crores in orders over the last 4 quarters, only 15% of these have been executed, largely in part due to some delays, which is bank-dependent technical testing, integration issues primarily in the PSU bank space

items.statement: H1 capex INR30 crores net of CWIP vs FY25 projection INR300 crores; full year estimate revised to ~INR250 crores
items.quote: I think the rest of the year -- for the full year, I think Pankaj's estimates will be roughly at INR250 crores capex.

items.statement: Cash Logistics touchpoints grew 11% to 143,000; direct-to-retail lines increased from 40 to 60 since March
items.quote: We've seen an 11% growth in our touch points to 143,000 points, which also showcases and demonstrate the results of our investments in building capacity and deepening our coverage

items.statement: ATM interchange rate likely to increase from INR7; industry working with regulators to make rural deployments viable
items.quote: Interchange is an issue because at the INR7 interchange, banks are not able to deploy new ATMs. Therefore, there has been a lot of industry work going on between the banks and the regulators to relook at interchange to make it viable for them to roll out more ATMs.

items.statement: BLA pricing saw aggressive bidding from MOF project incumbents; CMS limiting exposure, prefers fixed-price contracts
items.quote: The BLA sector did see very aggressive price bidding in the last 6 to 9 months, primarily from MO, Ministry of Finance Project incumbents, whic h are trying to defend their revenue as the project went end of life

items.statement: AR increased INR270 crores in H1; INR175 crores due to payment slipping from Q2 to Q3 for a large bank project
items.quote: Out of total AR increase, INR175 crores is on account of payments slipping from Q2 to Q3 for a key project of a large bank.

items.statement: H1 OCF typically 25% of full year; working capital increase higher in H1 than H2 historically
items.quote: If I will give the context that in FY '23 and FY '24, OCF of H1 was only 25% of the full year OCF. So working capital increase is higher than the H1 than the H2.

items.statement: Bad debt provisions at 4.3% of revenue in H1 FY25 vs 4.1% last year; guided range 4-5%
items.quote: Our provisions in H1 of this year are about 4.3%. And I think this number was roughly 4.1% from last year, about 5.1% for FY '23. And we have guided to the 4% to 5% range as a range to estimate just as a trend line what we think.

items.statement: Robust M&A pipeline under evaluation; targeting synergistic deals to expand offerings; timing uncertain
items.quote: On the M&A front, we have a robust pipeline of deals under evaluation. Given our track record of scaling up businesses, our customer access, our brand in BFSI and Retail, a deep countrywide network and balancesheet strength, all of these attract founders and companies who want to partner with us or get required.

items.statement: RBI currency chest white paper indicates revamp with CIT companies as key stakeholders; cassette swap compliance at 25%, new RBI push for March deadline
items.quote: The RBI currency chest white paper indicates RBI's plans to revamp the currency chest infrastructure and distribution logistics with CIT companies as key stakeholders.

items.statement: AIoT RMS business scaling with retail pilots; software/AIoT ~5% of revenue, targeting 8% midterm
items.quote: I think they largely will be around the 5% contribution to revenue. And we think in the midterm, that can go up to 8% or so.

items.statement: Direct-to-retail clients increased from 40 to 60 since March; expanding both depth and breadth in banking relationships
items.quote: In the retail business, where specifically our direct-to-retail segment, we now are working with 60 direct lines, up from 40 in March.

items.statement: Competitive intensity moderating in Managed Services and cash networks after 1-1.5 years of pressure
items.quote: I think the competitive intensity has reduced. We saw intense competitive pressures across Managed Services and cash networks in the last 1, 1.5 years. I think that seems to be getting better, but only time will tell if that remains or not.

items.statement: Order execution delays due to bank-dependent technical testing and multi-OEM integration (NPCI, MasterCard, Visa)
items.quote: Given these are integrated contracts, a lot of them have seen multiple OEMs, which need integration and testing, both at the bank IT level, the NPCI and MasterCard and Visa, which has led to delays in execution.

items.statement: New President Puneet Bhirani appointed to unify operations platform across cash, Managed Services and RMS
items.quote: We have invested significantly in unifying our operations platform across cash, Managed Services and RMS under our new President, Puneet Bhirani.

items.statement: Cassette swap compliance at 25%; ATM and RCM network almost fully compliant; RBI urging acceleration to March deadline
items.quote: So overall cassette swap, I think we are right now about 25% compliant, as we have said earlier. Very recently, there's been an update from the RBI urging the idea to sort of accelerate and expand on cassette swap and achieve a further milestone by end of March.

items.statement: Manufacturing plant in Chennai for ATM machines aligned with Make in India; will supply Ferosum-partnered machines for order book execution
items.quote: We have a manufacturing plant, which we had invested in to align with Make in India norms in India for large contracts. And as and when we are winning the order book, which will need ATM machines from our partner, Ferosum, they will be partially manufactured at our plant in Chennai.

items.statement: FY25 revenue target of Rs 120 crore at group level
items.quote: March '25, our expectation is that we will end at close to Rs. 120 crores top line, that's what we are looking at.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target of Rs 300 crore at group level
items.quote: And March '26 we will cross Rs. 300 crores.

items.statement: FY25 standalone revenue target of Rs 45-50 crore
items.quote: we expect the standalone to come to around Rs. 45 crores, Rs. 50 crores which we were expecting at the start of the year also

items.statement: FY26 standalone revenue similar to FY25 at Rs 45-50 crore
items.quote: FY '26 will be around the similar numbers. It will not be higher than that, it will be similar numbers.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin at 18% and PAT margin at 14%
items.quote: our EBITDA margins have also increased to 18% and PAT margins to 14%.

items.statement: PAT margin may see slight impact from acquisitions and marketing spend
items.quote: With the acquisitions that we are doing, and we will expect a slight impact on our PAT margins wherein we might spend a little more on innovations, on marketings, on brand building.

items.statement: 184 active pursuits as of October 1, 2024
items.quote: as of 1st October 2024, the team was working on 184 pursuits.

items.statement: Added 130 new pursuits in H1 FY25, starting from 92 at beginning of year
items.quote: if you look at the number of pursuits that we had at the beginning of this year, it was 92, and we added 130 new pursuits in this year.

items.statement: Raised Rs 120 crore in subsidiaries as of September 30, 2024
items.quote: the balance Rs. 110 crores, Rs. 120 crores is for the raise of money that we have done subsequently. So, the Rs. 120 crores is the acquisitions.

items.statement: Plan to continue acquisition spree for IP, revenue, and profit
items.quote: we will continue our acquisition spree. So, we will continue, we will keep on acquiring companies.

items.statement: Group headcount grew from under 200 to 1,000+
items.quote: last year if you remember, we were under 200, and now as a group we are 1,000-plus, and we are growing.

items.statement: 100% of employees on ESOPs
items.quote: Every single person in the company, and I say it, every single person in the company is on ESOPs. So, we are one of those rare companies which are 100% on ESOPs.

items.statement: H1 FY25 revenue 75% recurring SaaS vs 50-60% in H2 FY24
items.quote: currently in my H1 FY '25, the recurring percentage is 75%.

items.statement: Trade receivables rose to Rs 28.54 crore; 50% outstanding <60 days, 80% <180 days
items.quote: out of the entire trade receives of Rs. 28.54 crores, 50% of the traders receivables outstanding for less than 60 days, and more than 80% is outstanding for less than 180 days.

items.statement: SaaS credit cycle 30-45 days; delays from high-profile clients and license deals
items.quote: our credit cycle for the SaaS based revenue is 30 to 45 days, because we charge m onthly, and the clients pay us monthly

items.statement: 90% of Indian banks in supply chain finance use Veefin platform
items.quote: If you look at India today, in India 90% of the banks who are into supply chain, they are using our platform.

items.statement: Raised Rs 270 crore total: Rs 170 crore for acquisitions, Rs 120 crore in subsidiaries
items.quote: The Rs. 270 crores include two numbers. We have acquired two companies, so Rs. 170 crores is for that acquisition, and the balance Rs. 110 crores, Rs. 120 crores is for the raise of money that we have done subsequently.

items.statement: Acquired Nityo (Rs 150 crore) and TaxGenie; EpikInDiFi not yet consolidated
items.quote: we acquired Nityo which is a Rs. 150 crores company, and we acquired TaxGenie. And EpikInDiFi is not yet consolidated.

items.statement: Balance sheet increased substantially due to acquisitions and funding, depressing return ratios
items.quote: Your balance sheet itself has increased substantially from March '24, depressing your return ratios.

items.statement: Plan to start quarterly results and earnings calls from next financial year
items.quote: To be able to come out with quarterly results and having earnings call very frequently, you will start seeing that from next financial year.

items.statement: Plan to list on main board as soon as gates open
items.quote: Yes, obviously, all of us have that plan, and as soon as the gates open, we will be waiting.

items.statement: Loan book growth target of 22%+ for FY25
items.quote: Going ahead, we remain committed towards achieving our loan book growth as guided earlier of 22% plus during FY25 by capitalizing on growin g MSME, mortgage segment coupled with expanding over middle -income group segment

items.statement: Annualized ROA target of 1.4%+ for FY25
items.quote: Our focus on operational efficiencies and expansion in NII and increasing fee income will be our key drivers for our annualized ROE target of 1.4% plus for FY25 and continued expansion going ahead of the ROE.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance of 0.15%-0.25% for FY25
items.quote: Yes, I intend to keep our credit cost in the delta of 0.15% to 0.25% for the fiscal.

items.statement: Non-interest income target of 1%-1.1% of average advances
items.quote: Yes, we are intending to maintain in the range of 1% to 1.1% as we move forward which includes our penal charges now which is 0.12%.

items.statement: Opex to average assets guidance of 3%-3.2% for FY25
items.quote: And we are giving the same guidance in the beginning of the year also and now we are retaining the same guidance. That we believe o ur opex will continue to remain the range bound in the current fiscal

items.statement: Branch expansion target of 200+ branches by end of FY25
items.quote: So, typically as we discussed in the last earning call also, we started the branch working, we are targeting, intending to keep it 200 types, 200 plus branches by end of this fiscal.

items.statement: Gross advances at INR 6,718 crores, up 15% YoY and 5% QoQ
